quick: Speak with Isran.
Warn the jarl of the vampire threat.
Find and take evidence to the jarl.
(Alternate) Discreetly kill the Visiting Advisor and return to Isran.
Kill the Visiting Advisor.
Report back to Isran.

paragraphs: After speaking with Isran, you will be sent to inform a random jarl of a vampire threat within their court. The jarl will note the seriousness of your allegation, and ask for evidence. This can be obtained by pickpocketing the Visiting Advisor, who can usually be found in the main court room of the jarl's hall, for his orders. Note that if your pickpocket attempt fails he will attack you, often leading to confrontation with nearby NPCs and likely death. This method is particularly effective when you are a Thane of the relevant hold, as you will then be able to tell the guards to disregard your crime.

Return to the jarl with the note and they will grant you leave to kill the vampire with no retaliation from the hold's guards. Note that despite nominally being a vampire, the Adviser is immune to the Sun Fire spell . Alternatively, you can skip the evidence gathering stage and instead discreetly eliminate the Visiting Advisor through either stealth or using a Frenzy spell while hidden. Once the vampire lies dead, return to Isran.

stages.text: Isran has sent me to <Alias=Capital> to warn <Alias=Jarl> of a vampire masquerading as a visiting advisor to <Alias.PronounPosObj=Jarl> court. I am to destroy the beast. If I fail to secure <Alias=Jarl>'s permission first, the guards will consider it a murder. Objective 10: Warn <Alias=Jarl> about the vampire threat
Objective 20: Find evidence linked to the vampire
Objective 30: Bring evidence to <Alias=Jarl>
Objective 40: Destroy the vampire masquerading as a Visiting Advisor
Objective 40: Destroy the vampire masquerading as a Visiting Advisor Objective 100: Return to <Alias=QuestGiver>
I've destroyed the vampire in <Alias=Capital> masquerading as a visiting advisor to <Alias=Jarl>'s court.
<Alias=Jarl> is no longer the Jarl of <Alias=Capital> and the vampire no longer poses a threat.

notes: If the Jarl you were to report to is deposed, including via Season Unending, this quest will automatically be completed.
It is impossible for the advisor to be at the court of Maven Black-Briar or Ulfric Stormcloak, due to their unique voice types.
Unlike other Dawnguard radiant quests, this one can only occur every twelve days at best.
Isran will only assign Dawnstar or Riften as target locations for this quest.
The Unofficial Dawnguard Patch, version 2.0.0, fixes this bug.

The advisor is supposed to stay within a certain distance of the jarl, but in locations like Understone Keep and occasionally others, this can leave the advisor inside a locked room or in other unintuitive locations.
Save and reload the game, or exit the building and re-enter; the advisor may show up in a different location.

Wait until the jarl goes to bed or wakes up; this will typically cause the advisor to follow or, if locked in a room, to teleport close to the jarl. (This may require you to leave and re-enter or save and reload.)

Use the following console commands to move directly to the advisor: sqv DLC1RH07. Look for the line that starts with Ref 'Vampire' and note the ID in parentheses at the end of that line. Then use player.moveto ID and you should be taken directly to the advisor.
It is not considered a crime to attack the disguised vampire despite being warned by Isran that it would be if you're caught.
The Unofficial Skyrim Legendary Edition Patch, version 3.0.7, fixes this bug.

quick: Speak to the quest giver.
Steal the requested item.
Return to the quest giver.

walkthrough.heading: Dengeir of Stuhn
paragraphs: Dengeir of Stuhn was once the Jarl of Falkreath but has since stepped down and is now a Thane. He is a paranoid and patriotic supporter of the Stormcloaks. He believes that Lod the blacksmith is writing a treasonous letter and wants you to steal it for him.

The letter is on Lod's bedside table. It is simply a note requesting extra iron. Steal it and return it to Dengeir. Dengeir will at first be confused, and then realize Lod is probably not up to treason, even if he is making extra weapons for the Empire. He will then give you a reward of leveled gold.
Completion of this quest opens up another radiant quest, Dark Ancestor.

walkthrough.heading: Malur Seloth
paragraphs: Talking to Malur Seloth and asking him what he does prompts him to reveal that he doesn't really do anything. He wants to appear more mage-like when in the jarl's presence, and wishes to acquire a staff.

The one he wants belongs to Nelacar who resides in the inn. The staff is located in the shop counter in Nelacar's room. Steal it and return to Malur. He will reward you with one skill point in Speech.

walkthrough.heading: Stands-In-Shallows
paragraphs: When speaking to Stands-In-Shallows, he mentions that he overheard sailors talking about their stashed extra powerful Skooma, and he would like to get it.
The bottle is located in the New Gnisis Cornerclub in Windhelm, underneath the second set of stairs. Steal it and return to Stands-in-Shallows, who will reward you with a skill point in Sneak.

stages.text: Objective 10: Steal the <Alias=QuestItem> for <Alias.ShortName=QuestGiver>
Objective 15: Bring the <Alias=QuestItem> to <Alias.ShortName=QuestGiver>

notes: Only one radiant quest of a similar type can be assigned at any given time. You must clear the radiant quest from your miscellaneous quests in order to be eligible to receive another of the same type.
Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the thane quest for the quest giver's hold.
This quest requires you to commit a crime; see that page for details about criminal activity.
Malur's and Shallows' items are available to retrieve from the start of the game, while the letter Dengeir requests only gets enabled once he has mentioned it.
The quest might not trigger if you have already stolen the quest item before talking to the related NPC. Since the quest item is marked as such, you are left with no way of getting rid of it.

quick: (Optional) Learn about the love triangle from the townspeople.
Talk to Sven or Faendal about the love triangle.
(Optional) Talk to the other man involved in the love triangle (Sven if you talked to Faendal first or vice versa).
Give the letter to Camilla Valerius.
Return to the man you decided to help to finish the quest.

walkthrough.heading: The Triangle
paragraphs: When you visit the small town of Riverwood, the local beauty, Camilla Valerius, has sparked the interest of two bachelors in town. The local bard, Sven, and the Wood Elf hunter Faendal, are both vying for Camilla's favor; and will resort to slander and libel to win it.

walkthrough.heading: What a Tangled Web We Weave
paragraphs: If you approach Sven first, at the Sleeping Giant Inn, you will come to know of his love for Camilla, and about his suspicions about Faendal's involvement in her life. Sven will then ask you for a favor: deliver a fake letter supposedly written by Faendal to Camilla, seemingly breaking things off with her due to her being an Imperial, and him a proud Bosmer. You may also speak to Faendal first. He can be found chopping wood near the lumber mill or wandering the village. Faendal also has feelings for Camilla and a desire to see Sven out of the picture. He asks you to deliver his own fake letter designed to disrupt Sven's wooing by outlining out the household chores he has planned for Camilla. With either letter, you can go straight to Camilla, or show the supposed letter to the other man, prompting them to hand over their own forged letter for you to deliver.

walkthrough.heading: When We Practice to Deceive
paragraphs: When you decide who you want to help, either Sven or Faendal, deliver the letter to Camilla. Camilla is usually at the Riverwood Trader, but at night she can sometimes be found at the Sleeping Giant Inn. When you talk to Camilla, you have two ways of proceeding. You can lie to her and give her the forged letter as is, or tell her the truth about the ruse. In either case, she will effectively break off her interactions with the loser. Speak with the winner to collect your reward.

stages.text: Objective 10: Deliver Faendal's letter to Camilla Objective 20: (Optional) Tell Sven about Faendal's letter
Objective 110: Deliver Sven's letter to Camilla
Objective 110: Deliver Sven's letter to Camilla Objective 120: (Optional) Tell Faendal about Sven's letter
Objective 10: Deliver Faendal's letter to Camilla
Objective 210: Talk to Faendal

Objective 220: Talk to Sven
Objective 210: Talk to Faendal

notes: It is not possible to complete this quest in a manner that has both Sven and Faendal become available as followers and have their dispositions friendly towards you.

Despite the events of this quest, Camilla is also a marriage candidate for you, and can be married once her disposition is increased, such as by completing the quest The Golden Claw. However, this does not in any way alter the events or dialogue of this quest, and all participants will act as if Camilla is still available. If Camilla relocates to one of your houses, and you helped one man win her over, his programming will still have him seek her out even at your house.
If this quest is still running when marrying Camilla, it is still possible to finish it by delivering the letter on behalf of one or the other even though this scene no longer makes sense to allow.
The Unofficial Skyrim Legendary Edition Patch, version 3.0.1, addresses this issue. Marrying Camilla while the quest is still active will now cause it to fail.
Orgnar may still mention the love triangle after the quest is finished.
The Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 4.2.6, fixes this bug.

quick: Go to the Sacellum of Boethiah to find a copy of Eranya's Journal
Travel to Sivdur's Respite and read Eranya's Notes on Sivdur's Tomb
Go to the College of Winterhold and read a copy of Eranya's Research Notes
Go to Whiterun to fetch Sivdur's Amulet
Go to Shroud Hearth Barrow to fetch Magrathi's skull
Travel to Sivdur's Respite and enter the warrior's tomb
Locate Goldbrand

paragraphs: There are two locations to start the quest: the Sacellum of Boethiah and the College of Winterhold.

At the Sacellum of Boethiah in the fenced-in fighting area, you will find Eranya, an imperial researcher investigating the legendary Goldbrand. She isn't very eager to tell you the location of it, on account of being dead, but by reading her journal you will find out the katana rests in Sivdur's Respite.

Go to Sivdur's Respite, located to the north of Windhelm and you will be attacked by a few cultists of Boethiah, one of which will have a note detailing their ambitions. There is a gate with two pedestals on either side of it. Both pedestals have etched tablets. The left one states:
While the right one states:
On a table to the right of the pedestals lie Eranya's Notes on Sivdur's Tomb, which will tell you that her research notes were left at the Arcanaeum at the College of Winterhold.
Go there and you will find Eranya's Research Notes located on the floor to the right of Urag gro-Shub's desk among some other books.
Alternatively, you can go straight to the Arcanaeum at the College of Winterhold (or go there after reading Eranya's journal) and read the copy of Eranya's Research Notes.
Once you've read Eranya's Research Notes, you will be attacked by two invisible Boethiah Cultists. Each of them will have a potion of invisibility.
You will then need to find two artifacts to complete the quest: Sivdur's Amulet and Magrathi's Skull. They can be found in any order.

walkthrough.heading: Acquiring Sivdur's Amulet
paragraphs: Visit Whiterun and convince Lars Battle-Born to give you Sivdur's amulet:

walkthrough.heading: Acquiring Magrathi's Skull
paragraphs: Magrathi's Skull is a little bit more complicated than the amulet.

Travel to Ivarstead and enter Shroud Hearth Barrow. If you have not cleared out the barrow beforehand, to the right of you, behind a gate, will be a ghost. That ghost is not related to this quest and you do not have to deal with him, but what self-respecting adventurer would pass up a chance for fame, riches and a word wall?

Magrathi will be in the claw door chamber, past several traps, a copy of the Illusion skill book Before the Ages of Man and the ghost, and, unlike Lars Battle-Born will be reticent in giving you what you seek. He is a maskless Dragon Priest and will be just as powerful as any of the others no matter your level, so make sure you are prepared for the difficult fight ahead. After defeating him make sure to take his skull.

walkthrough.heading: Sivdur's Respite
paragraphs: You will now need to head back to Sivdur's Respite. Place Sivdur's amulet on the pedestal to the left of the door and Magrathi's skull on the pedestal to the right of the door in order to proceed.

The dungeon has some leveled draugr enemies and loot, but it is all of little note except for Sivdur's Tomb, where you will find Goldbrand on a pedestal and a chest near the entrance. When you pick up Goldbrand, two Honor Guards of Sivdur will get out of their sarcophagi, so be ready to fight them or run away; killing them is not necessary for the completion of the quest.

stages.text: I've heard a rumor that a historian researching the whereabouts of lost daedric artifacts has recently gone missing. She was last seen in the mountains east of Windhelm. Objective 0: Locate the missing historian

I've found the body of the historian rumored to be researching daedric artifacts at the Sacellum of Boethiah. She appears to have been killed at the hands of Boethiah cultists. I should read her journal to learn more. Objective 20: Read Eranya's journal

The historian Eranya was researching Goldbrand, a daedric artifact in the shape of a golden katana. Her notes indicate that she was on her way to discover the burial site of an ancient Nord warrior hidden in the mountains north of Windhelm. I should follow in her footsteps and investigate the burial site myself. Objective 30: Locate the ancient warrior's tomb
I've discovered the tomb mentioned in Eranya's journal. I should find a way to gain entrance to the tomb. Objective 35: Find a way to open the tomb
I've discovered the tomb mentioned in Eranya's journal. I now need to find the two artifacts mentioned in Eranya's research notes.
I've discovered the tomb mentioned in Eranya's research notes. I now need to find the two artifacts she detailed that will open the entrance of the tomb.

I discovered another journal left behind by Eranya, the Imperial historian. In them, they detail that the key to opening the tomb lies in understanding the meaning of the two inscriptions in front of the tomb. Her research notes were left in the Arcanaeum in the College of Winterhold, which should have more details on how the tomb can be opened. Objective 36: Read Eranya's research notes in the Collge [sic] of Winterhold Arcanaeum Objective 37: Investigate the tomb entrance

I discovered another journal left behind by Eranya, the Imperial historian that was rumored to have gone missing. In them, they detail that the key to opening the tomb lies in understanding the meaning of the two inscriptions in front of the tomb. Her research notes were left in the Arcanaeum in the College of Winterhold, which should have more details on how the tomb can be opened.

I have discovered Eranya's research notes in the College of Winterhold Arcanaeum. In her notes, she detailed the means to open Sivdur's Respite, the tomb that the artifact Goldbrand is rumored to be within. I must obtain Sivdur's amulet and the skull of Sivdur's nemesis, Magrathi. The amulet has been passed down for generations in the Battle-Born family and is now possessed by Lars Battle-Born. Magrathi was entombed within Shroud Hearth Barrow, a Nordic ruin near Ivarstead. I will need both relics to gain entrance to the tomb. Objective 40: Obtain Sivdur's amulet from Lars Battle-Born

I've obtained Sivdur's amulet from Lars Battle-Born. I should place it on the pedestal near the entrance of the tomb in Sivdur's Respite. Objective 43: Place the amulet on the pedestal near Sivdur's tomb

I've placed Sivdur's amulet on the pedestal near his tomb. When I did so, one of the doors of the tomb seemed to open. I now need to place Magrathi's skull on the other pedestal. Objective 50: Find Sivdur's betrayer in Shroud Hearth Barrow
I located Magrathi, a powerful dragon priest. I will need to defeat him if I am to claim his skull. Objective 51: Defeat Magrathi
I have defeated Magrathi. I should reclaim his skull so that I can return it to Sivdur's Respite. Objective 52: Obtain Magrathi's skull
I have reclaimed Magrathi's skull. I should place it on the pedestal near the entrance of the tomb in Sivdur's Respite. Objective 53: Place Magrathi's skull on the pedestal near Sivdur's tomb
I've placed Magrathi's skull on the pedestal near his tomb. When I did so, one of the doors of the tomb seemed to open. I now need to place Sivdur's amulet on the other pedestal.

I've placed both of the relics on the pedestals near the tomb in Sivdur's Respite. As I did so, the final door to the tomb seemed to open. I should see what awaits inside. Objective 90: Explore the tomb

After exploring the tomb in Sivdur's Respite, I have discovered the burial chamber of Sivdur himself. Lying upon an altar is Goldbrand, the ancient golden katana that the historian Eranya was in search of. Objective 100: Retrieve Goldbrand
Following in the Imperial historian Eranya's footsteps, I gained entrance to the tomb in Sivdur's Respite and retrieved the artifact Goldbrand.

notes: Reading Eranya's Journal at Sivdur's Respite will initiate the miscellaneous journal entry to visit the College of Winterhold if you have not previously been told to visit the College before.
It is not possible to fail the speech checks for aquiring Sivdur's Amulet from Lars Battle-Born. If the player does not have enough gold to bribe him the option to do so will not appear in dialogue.

If this quest is done concurrently with investigating Shroud Hearth Barrow, you will be dealing with a Dragon Priest in the first zone on top of the insane mage Wyndelius Gatharian before you can even reach the claw door and the Word of Power within.

It appears that the Boethiah Cultists will respawn in the Arcanaeum whenever the cell resets. From there, they stalk you wherever you go, and they can appear anywhere, including inside player homes. They only follow at walking speed, so having them catch up to you may be fairly infrequent and appear to be arbitrary.
The Official Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 1.6.629.0, fixes this bug.
Entering Sivdur's Respite before starting the quest may set the quest to Stage 400 and prevent the quest from starting normally.
This can be fixed by using the console command resetquest ccBGSSSE005_MainQuest to reset the quest.

quick: Be informed of your inherited debt by Mogrul.
Pay the debt or kill Mogrul.

paragraphs: After the completion of the quest Reluctant Steward you will be made aware of a debt that Drovas Relvi owed to a money lender by the name of Mogrul operating out of Raven Rock. Now that Drovas is under the protection of Neloth and out of Mogrul's reach, Mogrul expects you to make good on Drovas' debt. To help entice you to pay the debt, Mogrul will send his thugs after you until the debt is paid.
Mogrul will approach you while you are in Raven Rock:
You will then be presented with several dialogue options:
If you decide to pay him later:
At this point, you will have the same dialogue options as above.

If you don't want to pay Mogrul, your only alternative is to kill him, with the risk of the Redoran Guard intervening to stop you. However, if you are observant of your surroundings while you are in Raven Rock, you can detect Mogrul and his bodyguard Slitter approaching you to demand that you pay up if you haven't been informed of your debt yet. He will follow you out of town if you are patient and don't run too far ahead, allowing you to discreetly dispatch him without drawing the guards' ire.

You can also visit Drovas and inform him of Mogrul's harassment. While he will not be willing to pay the debt on his own initiative, you can persuade him to provide you with whatever money he can to help you pay off the debt. You must pass a hard Speech check to successfully persuade Drovas to give you the money. If you succeed, he will give you 250 gold, but that won't be enough to cover the debt. The rest is up to you.
Note that you need a Speech skill of 75 to successfully persuade him:

stages.text: Someone named Mogrul sent a messenger for me. This Mogrul wants to talk. Objective 100: Talk to Mogrul

Helping Drovas has come back to bite me. He owed a money lender named Mogrul 1000 septims. Now Mogrul expects me to pay Drovas' debt. If I don't, he's going to keep sending thugs after me. Objective 200: Pay Mogrul
Helping Drovas has come back to bite me. He owed a money lender named Mogrul 1000 septims. Mogrul expected me to pay Drovas debt, which I've done.
Helping Drovas has come back to bite me. He owed a money lender named Mogrul 1000 septims. Mogrul expected me to pay Drovas debt. However, I killed him instead.
Helping Drovas has come back to bite me. He owed a money lender named Mogrul 1000 septims. I persuaded him to take half that.

notes: When Mogrul first approaches you for the initial conversation, exiting the conversation without picking a dialogue option will not start the quest. Mogrul will continue to follow, and attempt to initiate the same conversation again. You can lead Mogrul out of Raven Rock this way, allowing him to be killed without witnesses. Mogrul will not follow you into a building, or if you fast travel somewhere.

If you attack Mogrul in the Retching Netch and Teldryn Sero either currently is (or has previously been) under your employ, Sero will come to your aid. If you previously finished Unearthed and spared Ralis Sedarys, Ralis will come to your aid as well.

If you don't want to pay your debt but find it impossible to assassinate Mogrul without incurring a bounty, you can use Nightingale Subterfuge. Casting it while he, among others, is in its area of effect will result in them fighting, likely leading to Mogrul's death.
Drovas will comment after the quest is finished, depending on your decision:
If you pay the debt, Drovas will say "I heard you paid my debt to Mogrul. I don't know how I can every [sic] repay you."
If you kill Mogrul, Drovas will say "I heard Mogrul is dead. That is a relief!"
After the quest is finished, you can pickpocket Mogrul to reclaim your money, but the gold may not be present in his inventory if you wait too long.

If Mogrul is killed inside the Retching Netch while you are hidden, Slitter will search for you. If you unhide so that he finds you and then attacks you and you flee outside, he will not follow you. Subsequently, even if you immediately re-enter the Retching Netch, Slitter will not be hostile to you, and will still tell you to talk to Mogrul.
The Unofficial Dragonborn Patch, version 1.0.5, fixes this bug.
Mogrul can still send thugs after you, even though this quest has been completed.
The Unofficial Dragonborn Patch, version 2.0.3, fixes this bug.

You can successfully persuade Drovas to give you 250 gold to help you pay his debt to Mogrul an infinite number of times. Something that should be noted is that he won't pay you a second time immediately afterwards. However, after a short period of time, that dialogue topic will reset itself.
The Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 4.3.9, addresses this issue. Drovas will now only give you the 250 gold once.

quick: Speak with Isran.
Find Gunmar and help him defeat the bear.
Find Sorine Jurard and get her to come to Fort Dawnguard.
Return to Fort Dawnguard and listen to Isran's speech.

walkthrough.heading: Reinforcements
paragraphs: When you have declined Lord Harkon's offer at Castle Volkihar, you are told to return to Isran at Fort Dawnguard and provide information about Serana. Upon arriving in the courtyard, you will find Isran, Celann, Durak, and newcomer Vori doing their best to fight a group of attacking vampires. Help them defeat the vampires, then report back to Isran who will be waiting at the main gate, showing great anger that his hidden fortress was exposed so soon. When you tell him that the vampires were looking for a woman trapped inside Dimhollow Crypt, he will say: "A woman? Trapped in there? That doesn't make any sense. Who is she? More importantly, where is she?" However, he will forget about the woman once you tell him the vampires claimed an Elder Scroll: "By the Divines, this couldn't get much worse. This is more than you and I can handle." He will then realize it is time to bring in some powerful reinforcements to Fort Dawnguard: "If they're bold enough to attack us here, then this may be bigger than I thought. I have good men here, but... There are people I've met and worked with over the years. We need their skills, their talents, if we're going to survive this. If you can find them, we might have a chance." He will then tell you about the two persons, namely Sorine Jurard and Gunmar: "I think we'll want Sorine Jurard. Breton girl, whip-smart and good with tinkering. Fascination with the Dwemer. Weapons in particular. Last I knew, she was out in the Reach, convinced she was about to find the biggest dwarven ruins yet. You'll also want to find Gunmar. Big brute of a Nord, hates vampires almost as much as I do. Got it into his head years back that his experience with animals would help. Trolls in particular, from what I hear." He will then send you on your way, and you will have to convince Sorine and Gunmar to join the Dawnguard, and use their special skills to help out against the vampire menace.

walkthrough.heading: Gunmar
paragraphs: Gunmar will show up randomly in the wilderness in Skyrim or, if you have installed Dragonborn, on Solstheim, or somewhere else with Creation Club content (see notes). Follow your map marker to his location, and you will find the huge Nord in sneaking position, seemingly on the hunt for game, warning you: "Mind yourself. There's a vicious bear on the loose." He then explains that he has chased a bear for two weeks, and that he finally managed to corner it. Keep in mind, if there is not a map marker in mainland Skyrim, check Solstheim. When you tell him that Isran needs his help, he will forget the bear for a while: "Isran? Needing someone else's help? Never thought I'd hear that. I'm afraid he's a few years too late. I've moved on. I have more important business to attend to. Besides, he can handle anything alone! He assured me so himself. What could he possibly need my help with?" When you tell him about the vampire threat and the Elder Scroll, he will reconsider, although he wants you to help him track down the bear and kill it. He will then lead you to a cave near his initial starting point:

Possible locations: Bonechill Passage • Bronze Water Cave • Brood Cavern • Clearspring Tarn • Cronvangr Cave • Crystaldrift Cave • Fallowstone Cave • Honeystrand Cave • Horker Island • Pinepeak Cavern • White Ridge Barrow

There is always one specific bear you will have to kill, although you will often get in battle with several creatures at once. When the bear is dead, a journal update will tell you to speak with Gunmar, who will thank you for the assistance, and agree to help against the vampires: "You've helped me, so I suppose the least I can do is find out what Isran wants. He's still at that fort near Stendarr's Beacon, I assume?" He will then be on his way to Fort Dawnguard.

walkthrough.heading: Sorine Jurard
paragraphs: Sorine Jurard will turn up in the wilderness near an unmarked Dwemer convector, just south of Mor Khazgur. She will be drifting around, obviously looking for something, mumbling: "What would mudcrabs want with my satchel, anyway?" and "Just one gyro. One, and I can get back to work. Where are they?" When you talk to her, she will ask if you have seen a sack full of Dwemer gyros and will proceed to tell you that a mudcrab may have taken it. When you tell her that Isran needs her help, she will respond: "Isran? Wants me? No, you must be mistaken. He made it exceedingly clear the last time we spoke that he had no interest in my help. I find it hard to believe he's changed his mind. He said some very hurtful things to me before I left." When told about the vampire threat and the Elder Scroll, she will change her mind, although she will not do anything before she gets a Dwemer gyro. You can now choose between two options, although the second option will differ if you already have a Dwemer gyro in your inventory. If you do, you can hand it to her and she will be on her way to Fort Dawnguard. You can also choose to persuade her, although you need a Speech skill of 50+ to be successful. If everything else fails, you can look around for her satchel. To find it, starting at Sorine, first face southeast. In this direction, you can see a tree near the water. Travel to the tree. After reaching it, face west. From here, you can see the satchel on the ground a few feet away. When you return to her with one of the gyros she will finally be convinced and walk all the way to Fort Dawnguard for an encounter with Isran.

walkthrough.heading: Isran's Speech
paragraphs: When you return to Fort Dawnguard, you will see that Isran has tightened security and made several changes to the exterior, including a gate and more wooden barricades. Enter the fort and you will find Gunmar and Sorine in the main hall, with Isran looking down at them from the balcony above. Before long, Isran will seal off the chamber, trapping the two new recruits, and shower them both with concentrated sunlight as a test. The following conversation will take place:

Gunmar: "All right Isran, you've got us all here. Now what do you want?" Isran: "Hold it right there." Sorine: "What are you doing?" Isran: "Making sure you're not vampires. Can't be too careful. So, welcome to Fort Dawnguard. I'm sure you've heard a bit of what we're up against. Powerful vampires, unlike anything we've seen before. And they have an Elder Scroll. If anyone is going to stand in their way, it's going to be us." Sorine: "This is all well and good, but do we actually know anything about what they're doing? What do we do now?" Isran: "We'll get to that. For now, get acquainted with the space. Sorine, you'll find room to start your tinkering on that crossbow design you've been working on. Gunmar, there's an area large enough for you to pen up some trolls, get them armored up and ready for use. In the meantime, we're going to get to the bottom of why a vampire showed up here looking for you. Let's go have a little chat with it, shall we?"

Once Isran has removed the barrier, the quest will end and the next quest, Prophet, will initiate. Gunmar and Sorine will then find their respective spots in the western area of Fort Dawnguard. Their presence will net you several benefits. Sorine is a master trainer in Marksman, and will also sell and buy items. She will also hand you several quests, while Gunmar is a master trainer in Smithing, will sell and buy weapons and armor, and will sell you an armored troll to aid you in battle. The next time you visit Fort Dawnguard, Sorine and Gunmar will change into their Dawnguard armor, a blacksmith's forge and arcane enchanter will be found near the smithing area, and armored trolls can be found in the pen across from the smelter. Exiting to Dayspring Canyon (including all 3 balconies) and re-entering from there will suffice.

stages.text: I've rejected Harkon's offer to be turned into a vampire. Now I need to return to Isran and tell him what I've learned. Objective 20: Speak with Isran
I've told Isran what I learned at the vampire castle. Isran has asked me to find Sorine Jurard and Gunmar, and bring them to him. Objective 30: Recruit Sorine Jurard Objective 40: Recruit Gunmar
Objective 45: Help Gunmar defeat the bear
I've found the people Isran said we'd need to fight Harkon and his vampires. Now I should return to Isran and help him formulate a plan of attack. Objective 60: Return to Isran

After rejecting Harkon's offer to become a vampire, I returned to Isran and informed him of what I've learned. I helped him recruit several people into the Dawnguard who can help us fight the vampires.

notes: As they are not protected, both Durak and Celann may be slain in the vampire attack at the beginning of the quest.

If there is no quest marker for Gunmar and Dragonborn is installed, the radiant location might be in Solstheim. If so, traveling to Solstheim will result in the marker appearing normally at that location if the quest is active. The same can happen if you install Creation Club content, depending upon what it is.

Sorine makes a comment that she saw a mudcrab the other day while discussing where her gyros have gone. This is likely a subtle reference to the previous installment, Oblivion, where "I saw a mudcrab the other day" was a sentence commonly uttered by many NPCs.

If you are a vampire, Isran will stop his speech and ask you to get yourself cured before anything else happens. This means that Sorine and Gunmar will wait in the main hall until you have completed Rising at Dawn.

During the quest, you can freely roam inside Volkihar Keep without danger to yourself. You can ask Feran Sadri, Hestla, and Ronthil what they have for sale, and you can ask Ronthil and Fura Bloodmouth for training. The portcullis will be down though, and you'll have to clip through it or the diagonal walls around it to gain access. In addition, everything inside will be owned, and will need to be stolen. To add insult to injury, everyone inside will be hostile once you finish the quest.
You may randomly encounter a vampire assassin at any point after completing this quest.
The quest may fail to start after refusing Harkon's gift and being returned to the landing.
You can fix this by entering either setstage DLC1HunterBaseIntro 20 or setstage DLC1HunterBaseIntro 30, followed by setobjectivedisplayed DLC1HunterBaseIntro 20 1 or 30 1 into the console.

If the above does not work, it may be because you encountered a living Vigilant Tolan in Dimhollow Crypt, and he died. He needs to be alive before the above commands will work. To fix this, you can resurrect him. Open the console and enter prid 02003532 to select him, then enter resurrect. Close the console and wait 5 seconds. Then reopen the console and attempt the above fix.

If neither the above work, then playerfollowercount's value may be the issue. To fix this load a save from BEFORE you open Serana's sarcophagus. Dismiss any current followers, using set playerfollowercount to 0 if necessary (may as well to be safe) then proceed through the quest as normal.
After rejecting Harkon's "gift" in Bloodline, there may be no indication that you completed that quest, which can lead to confusion upon finishing this one.
If you clear the bear den before talking to Gunmar, he will just stand there telling you to slay the (dead) bear.
The Unofficial Dawnguard Patch, version 1.1.1, fixes this bug.
The bear that Gunmar wants you to help him eliminate may be missing due to being deleted by the game's cleanup script.
The Unofficial Dawnguard Patch, version 1.1.3, fixes this bug.
Upon entering the fort, Gunmar and/or Sorine may end up behind the instantly-closing gate, making it impossible to continue the quest.
Exiting and reentering the fort or using the wait function will sometimes fix this and trigger the quest completion.
Open the console, click on each NPC and type moveto player one at a time to bring them to your side of the gate.
Upon completing the quest, the gate may not reopen.
Leave Fort Dawnguard, and immediately re-enter. The gate should now be open.

quick: Speak to Deor Woodcutter in Skaal Village.
Find Baldor Iron-Shaper at the abandoned lodge.
Retrieve the map from Ancarion at Northshore Landing.
Return to Baldor in Skaal Village.

walkthrough.heading: Finding Baldor
paragraphs: If you return to Skaal Village after the quest The Fate of the Skaal, you will overhear a conversation between Fanari and Deor:

Fanari: "Deor, you must be calm. I'm sure there's a good reason Baldor left us." Deor: "Something isn't right, Fanari. I feel it in my bones and I smell it in the air. Baldor wouldn't leave without telling someone." Fanari: "Don't worry yourself over nothing, Deor. Do you want a head full of gray hairs before you've seen forty winters?" Deor: "It makes my heart heavy that you don't believe me, Fanari. Baldor could be in danger, and you will do nothing. If you won't help me, then I'll ask the All-Maker to send someone else who can."

If you ask Fanari about the missing person, she will just brush it off as another of Deor's crazy ideas, but Deor is quite serious. He will tell you that local blacksmith Baldor Iron-Shaper went missing in the middle of the night. Deor suspects a kidnapping motivated by Baldor's valuable expertise in stalhrim smithing. On the night of his disappearance Deor also saw two elves dragging something away to the "south and west", so start your search in that direction.

walkthrough.heading: Abandoned Lodge
paragraphs: While Deor's directions could lead you more-or-less anywhere on Solstheim, your compass objective marker will point you directly to an Abandoned Lodge southwest of the Temple of Miraak. The lodge is normally empty, but once you arrive, you'll be attacked by four hostile members of the Thalmor. Dispose of them and loot their bodies for a note from their commander and the key to the lodge. Inside, head into the basement where you will find the scared, tied-up smith in a corner, weeping: "Help! Somebody! Please, someone, help me!" and "I have been taken against my will! I am in need of rescue!"

When you talk to Baldor, he will remember you as the hero who rescued the people of Skaal Village. Despite his wounds, he'll claim he's not hurt. When you ask why the Thalmor abducted him, he'll reply: "I do not know this word Thalmor, but if you mean the elves, they were trying to learn the secrets of forging Stalhrim. Their leader, an elf named Ancarion, has a map. He says that it shows the location of a hidden source of Stalhrim." He will then explain what stalhrim is: "Enchanted ice as hard as iron and cold as death. Stalhrim can be forged into deadly weapons, but the art is known only to smiths of the Skaal." He will then point you towards a Thalmor ship at the northwestern coast where Ancarion resides. He asks you to retrieve the map as it belongs to the Skaal people. Leave the wounded smith behind and make your way northwest to Northshore Landing.

walkthrough.heading: Northshore Landing
paragraphs: When you arrive, a Thalmor soldier will warn you to be careful. Make your way to the ship, and talk to Ancarion.
Three dialogue options will now be available. Successfully completing the third option will require a Speech skill of at least 75:

If the Thalmor soldiers at the dock engage you in combat, you'll need to kill Ancarion and loot the map from his corpse. Regardless if he gave you the map, if you pickpocketed it from him, or if you killed him and looted it from his corpse, your final step is to return to Skaal Village and give it to Baldor. He will be quite pleased, and will teach you how to smith Stalhrim. This quest is now complete, and the next two will start when you return to Skaal Village.

stages.text: Baldor Iron-Shaper, the smith in Skaal Village, has gone missing. One of the other villagers, Deor, said he saw two elves dragging something through the woods on the day of Baldor's disappearance. They were heading southwest. Objective 10: Search for Baldor Iron-Shaper

Baldor Iron-Shaper, the smith in Skaal Village, was abducted by the Thalmor. They were trying to get him to reveal the secret of forging Stalhrim. Baldor told me that the Thalmor leader, Ancarion, had a map that showed the location of a new source of Stalhrim, and he asked me to retrieve it. Objective 30: Retrieve the Stalhrim Source Map

Baldor Iron-Shaper, the smith in Skaal Village, was abducted by the Thalmor. They were trying to get him to reveal the secret of forging Stalhrim. Baldor told me that the Thalmor leader, Ancarion, had a map that showed the location of a new source of Stalhrim, and I retrieved it. Now I need to bring it back to Baldor. Objective 40: Talk to Baldor Iron-Shaper

Baldor Iron-Shaper, the smith in Skaal Village, was abducted by the Thalmor. They were trying to get him to reveal the secret of forging Stalhrim. Baldor told me that the Thalmor leader, Ancarion, had a map that showed the location of a new source of Stalhrim. I returned the map to Baldor and in gratitude, he offered to let me use his forge, where I can craft new items made from Stalhrim.
Objective 10: Ask Deor about Baldor's disappearance

notes: The stalhrim source that the Thalmor are seeking is in the mountains to the south of Northshore Landing, and its marker will be added to your game map if you read the Stalhrim Source Map, or upon finishing the quest if you don't. There are another two stalhrim deposits just east of the ship, on a small unmarked island surrounded by horkers.

If Deor Woodcutter or Fanari Strong-Voice are killed prior to completing the quest, you will never be able to learn to forge stalhrim yourself. In addition, you will have to discover the Stalhrim Source's location on your own.

If you have completed The Gardener of Men, all the villagers including Baldor will be "busy" until you complete At the Summit of Apocrypha. Make sure to talk to Baldor before you talk to Storn if you wish to complete this first.

Although you must finish this quest before you can craft stalhrim, there is another requirement that must be met: your Smithing skill must be at least level 80, and the Ebony Smithing perk must be active.

After you finish the quest, Ancarion will remain docked at Northshore Landing if you successfully made a deal to sell him stalhrim equipment. You cannot invest with Ancarion, though if the Merchant perk is active, you'll also be able to sell him weapons and armor that aren't made out of stahrim.
With version 2.0.3 of the Unofficial Dragonborn Patch, Ancarion's shop will benefit from the Master Trader perk as well.
After you finish the quest, the Thalmor soldiers you encountered outside the Abandoned Lodge will eventually respawn, though the new ones won't be hostile.

If you talk to the two Skaal villagers discussing the disappearance of the village blacksmith before they have finished talking, you will be unable to interact with the male villager, Deor Woodcutter, thus making the quest unattainable.
If the quest fails to start, use Setstage DLC2SV02 10 to kick it off.
There is a chance that the Thalmor Soldiers at the Abandoned Lodge will not be named, rendering them unlootable, thus making it impossible to obtain the key.
The Unofficial Dragonborn Patch, version 1.0.3, fixes this bug.
This can be fixed by typing player.additem xx027e00 1 into the console where "xx" is the load order number of the Dragonborn add-on.
There is a chance that after you speak with Deor your compass marker will point you to the furthest southwest point on the map, rather than the abandoned lodge.
This can be fixed by waiting 48 hours outside of the abandoned lodge. The compass marker will move to the correct location and Baldor will spawn inside the lodge.
If you successfully make a deal to sell Ancarion stalhrim equipment, he may eventually run out of gold, leaving him with nothing.

Since Deor and Fanari are only marked as Protected, they can be killed by the player (for example, accidentally during the battle with the Lurker after the Wind Stone is freed). This will prevent the quest from starting.
The Unofficial Dragonborn Patch, version 1.0.4, addresses this issue. It resurrects them if necessary, and marks them as Essential until the quest has started.
You can force the quest to start by using Setstage DLC2SV02 10.
If you interrupt the conversation between Deor and Fanari by talking to other villagers, the quest may fail to start, and talking to Deor may give you no dialogue options in order to start it.
The Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 4.3.9, addresses this issue. A possible workaround has been added to the conversation scene to try and keep you from derailing it.

quick: Meet Sam Guevenne and accept the drinking contest.
Help clean up the Temple of Dibella.
Ask about Sam and the staff in Rorikstead.
Talk to Ysolda in Whiterun about the staff.
Head to Morvunskar.
Search Morvunskar for Sam and the staff.
Receive your reward from the Daedric Lord Sanguine.

walkthrough.heading: Drinking Competition
paragraphs: Once you reach level 14, you may meet Sam Guevenne in any inn or tavern. He will challenge you to a drinking contest, offering to award you a staff if you win. Sam reaches his limit after his second drink. You can win by taking a third drink, after which a drunken Sam declares you the winner. However, before awarding the staff, Sam wants to take his new drinking buddy to "a place where the wine flows like water". At this point your mental blackout begins and the screen fades to black until the next day.

walkthrough.heading: The Hangover
paragraphs: You will be woken by Senna, a priestess, in the temple of Dibella in Markarth. When you ask about what happened, she states you were blathering about a wedding and a goat, or blaspheming the statuaries by fondling. You apparently made quite a mess of the temple, so she asks you to clean up the temple and make amends.

If you apologize, you will learn a little bit more information about what happened. You will have to pick up several seemingly meaningless items, namely, a giant's toe, two bottles of Alto Wine, and a confusing note from Sam. According to the note, you need these items, now marked as quest items, and a Hagraven Feather to fix the staff you were promised. You can skip the cleanup through persuasion (Average, Speech Skill 50) or bribe. Note that the Shrine of Dibella in the same room will grant you a +10 Speechcraft blessing for 8 hours, which can potentially help you for all stages of this quest. If you avoid cleaning up, you need not worry about trying to get the items.
After you clean up the temple, the priestess tells you that when you got there you were saying something about Rorikstead.

walkthrough.heading: Grok and a Goat
paragraphs: Head on to Rorikstead and when you arrive, look for Ennis. He will indignantly rebuke you for stealing his prized goat, named Gleda, and selling her to a giant. To get the information you need about Sam and the staff, you can pay Ennis 1000 gold for the goat, persuade him, intimidate him, or simply retrieve his goat.

To get Gleda, head south to find the goat wandering around near a giant named Grok. The giant is non-hostile, but once you get the goat to follow you, Grok will decide to attack. It is possible to steal Gleda without incurring Grok's wrath if you sneak up and "talk" to Gleda and then immediately run before Grok notices you, or yield to Grok if he does attack you. Gleda will follow you no matter how fast you run. Another option is to cast Calm on Grok before engaging with Gleda. Grok will not care that you have taken Gleda for the duration of the spell. If you are skilled enough, you can kill Grok.
Lead the goat back to Ennis to learn that you mentioned something about paying Ysolda in Whiterun for a wedding ring.

walkthrough.heading: The Blushing Bride
paragraphs: Go to Whiterun and find Ysolda. She says that you bought a wedding ring on credit from her, but since there isn't going to be a wedding, she wants the ring back. Your options are much the same as earlier conversations: you can persuade or intimidate her to get the information about Sam, pay her 2000 gold for the ring, or find the ring.
If you choose to get the ring, find your "fiancée", Moira the hagraven, who awaits you at her hut in Witchmist Grove:
"Darling! I've been waiting for you to return, to consummate our love!"
Your only option is to ask for the ring back. Moira gets mad and turns hostile:
"What? You want it for that hussy Esmerelda, with the dark feathers – don't you? I won't let her have you!"
Kill her and take the wedding ring from her inventory.
Once you have the ring, return to Whiterun and give it to Ysolda to learn where you were going to have the ceremony: Morvunskar.

walkthrough.heading: The "Perfect" Wedding Location
paragraphs: Having learned of the wedding's location, head over to Morvunskar. You will find a lot of hostile mages both outside and inside there. Fight your way into the fort. Eventually, after descending one, then ascending another stairway, a ball of blue light will appear. Enter the light and you will be transported to Misty Grove. Follow the path and you will find a party already in full swing, including your drinking buddy Sam. Sam will eventually reveal that he is actually the Daedric Prince of Debauchery, Sanguine. He will tell you that he was introducing some merriment and subversion into the world and was encouraging you to go out and "have fun". The items he had you bring to repair the staff, it turns out, are pointless, and will no longer be quest items. Sanguine will reward your efforts to track him down with the Sanguine Rose and will teleport you back to the pub where you met him.

stages.text: Objective 20: Participate in a drinking contest with Sam Guenvere [sic]
I have awoken in the Temple Of Dibella in Markarth. Sam and the staff he promised me have disappeared.

I have awoken in the Temple Of Dibella in Markarth. Sam and the staff he promised me have disappeared. I have no idea how I got here but a priestess has told me I trashed the Temple. The priestess might tell me what happened to Sam and the staff if I pick up the place. Objective 10: Find Sam Guevenne Objective 12: Find the Staff
Objective 20: Help clean up the Temple of Dibella

I have awoken in the Temple Of Dibella in Markarth. Sam and the staff he promised me have disappeared. I have no idea how I got here but a priestess has told me I trashed the Temple. I have cleaned up the Temple, if I apologize to the priestess she might tell me what happened to Sam and the staff. Objective 30: Apologize to the priestesses of Dibella

I have awoken from a night of debauchery with no idea what happened. Sam and the staff he promised me have disappeared. The priestesses of Dibella have told me to ask about Sam in Rorikstead. Objective 40: Ask about Sam and the staff in Rorikstead

I have awoken from a night of debauchery with no idea what happened. Sam and the staff he promised me have disappeared. Ennis in Rorikstead will tell me more about what happened once I return the goat I stole from him. Objective 50: Find Gleda the Goat

I have awoken from a night of debauchery with no idea what happened. Sam and the staff he promised me have disappeared. Ennis in Rorikstead will tell me more about what happened once I return the goat I stole from him. Objective 75: Bring Gleda the Goat back to Ennis in Rorikstead

I have awoken from a night of debauchery with no idea what happened. Sam and the staff he promised me have disappeared. A note of debt I gave to Ennis in Rorikstead has directed me to Ysolda in Whiterun, she might be able to direct me to Sam. Objective 85: Talk to Ysolda in Whiterun about the staff

I have awoken from a night of debauchery with no idea what happened. Sam and the staff he promised me have disappeared. Ysolda in Whiterun will give me more information about Same [sic] once I return the ring I borrowed from her to give to someone in Witchmist Grove. Objective 100: Find the wedding ring in Witchmist Grove

I have awoken from a night of debauchery with no idea what happened. Sam and the staff he promised me have disappeared. Ysolda in Whiterun will give me more information about Same [sic] once I return the ring I borrowed from her to give to a hagraven Witchmist Grove. Objective 115: Take the wedding ring
Objective 125: Return the wedding ring to Ysolda in Whiterun

I have awoken from a night of debauchery with no idea what happened. Sam and the staff he promised me have disappeared. Ysolda in Whiterun has told me to look for Sam in Morvunskar. Objective 135: Head to Morvunskar
Objective 150: Search Morvunskar for Sam and the Staff
"Sam" turned out to be the daedric prince of debauchery, Sanguine. He spurred me on during a drunken night of revelry that crossed all of Skyrim. I've acquired the Sanguine Rose for my troubles.

notes: If you bypass Rorikstead in this quest, thus never seeing Ennis between cleaning up the Temple of Dibella and speaking to Ysolda, Ennis will not push the issue of Gleda if you talk to him later. Gameplay-wise, this is because he has nothing to offer that you don't already know.

Patch 1.5 sets Senna, Ennis, and Ysolda as essential. Although the patch notes the change as essential "until [their] part in A Night To Remember is completed", they are simply set as essential for the entirety of the game.
Once the scenes with Senna, Ennis, and Ysolda are finished, they will go back to addressing you as they did before the quest began, and no more mention of the latter will be made.

After the quest is completed, you may have a random encounter with an Argonian called Deep-In-His-Cups who, according to him, was a part of the debauchery with you and Sam. He states that you and Sam owe him 10,000 gold for a bet because he ran into a bandit camp and almost died. If you say that you don't have 10,000 gold, he will attack you unless you pass an easy Speech check. If you pass the speech check, he will lower your debt to 750 coins. If you pay the debt (either 10,000 or 750 coins), he will go back to Black Marsh.
Sam can spawn at any of the inns across Skyrim, including those in towns, not just the ones in hold capitals. This includes The Retching Netch in Raven Rock with the Dragonborn add-on.
If Sam was present at the Retching Netch when the drinking contest took place, you'll be sent back there once the quest is finished.

All of the items in Sam's note are indirectly related to the quest: the giant's toe is a reference to Grok, holy water is a reference to Dibella Shrine's well, and a Hagraven feather is a reference to Moira.

Even if you never picked up Sam's note (for instance, by using persuasion or payment at the temple of Dibella) and thus never learned about the items supposedly necessary to repair the staff, dialogue options with Sanguine will still refer to you bringing along those items.

Teleporting to the temple will not count as "discovering" Markarth; if you have not been to Markarth before and fast travel away immediately upon exiting the temple, you will not be able to fast travel back. Instead, you may want to head to the city gates, which will initiate discovering the city. You can also discover Understone Keep before Markarth.
Only the Alto Wine variant with the basket on the bottom counts as a quest item; the one that lacks it doesn't. Likewise, regular wine, Spiced Wine, and empty wine bottles also do not count.

The blue light is on a platform at the top of a stairway, but if you enter the small storeroom below the platform you may be transported to Misty Grove prematurely from there, curtailing collection of loot.
The items on Sanguine's dining table are unowned, and therefore, free to take.
If you have already cleared Morvunskar before starting the quest, enemies will respawn in its exterior cell, but the fort's interiors will stay empty. Loot will also not respawn.
Anything you pick up while in Misty Grove will transfer with you to the real world once the quest is complete.

Neither Ysolda's, nor Senna's dialogue will change if you are married to them. Regardless of where she may be currently living, Senna will still be at the temple of Dibella when you wake up. Ysolda will retain her location if moved somewhere other than Whiterun, and you will need to speak to her there.
Many pieces of cut content related to this quest can still be found in the files:

You and Sam would not get to drinking straight away, as you could have bribed or intimated him in order to get a drink. Bribing would result in him saying "That amount should allow me to readily acquire a drink." and intimidation would result in him saying: "You should try that bit on the barkeep. Maybe get yourself a free drink."

Similarly, it seems like Sam would have started the quest off by talking to you about something he's seen, while also talking about the staff. Four player-only topics remain of this, but Sam's lines are not present: So... you were telling me a tale?, I give up. What did you see?, I'll bet a drunk like you sees a lot of strange things., I could sure use a staff like that....
The "Holy Water" mentioned in Sam's list, actually exists as an unused item. Despite its mention in the note, generic Alto Wine appears in its stead.
The giant's toe found in the temple was originally meant to be a Giant's club, the ref of the former still refers to it as the latter.
The priestess Orla was originally also meant to be present when you woke up in the temple. A marker for her is defined, but the code meant to move her to it is commented out in the quest script.

Priestessess Orla and Anwen both have dialogue related to this quest which can technically be heard, but it needs extreme conditions in order to succeed. You would have to break into the expert-locked inner sanctum of the temple in order to find them and then speak to them before their dialogue gets overridden by the generic trespassing dialogue. Also, while Orla's dialogue is technically linked to the correct stage 30, Anwen's is linked to stage 40, at which point it would've already been cleaned up. Their lines are also conditioned to play before stage 2000 and 5000, respectively, which don't exist. It's possible that Anwen's dialogue was deliberately conditioned to not play, as it erroneously has her mentioning herself in third person, instead of Senna.
The developer message DA14TempFadeInMessage also mentions multiple priestesses being present when you awaken, and they would've all spoken to you.

There's a list called DA14NPCs which contains all NPCs (supposedly) related to this quest. In addition to the other two Dibella priestessess mentioned above, Rorik and Reldith are also listed, but it's unclear what their role could've been, as they have no other leftovers at all.
Grok the giant was meant to have a line of unique attack dialogue, but as Giants can't talk in the final game, it goes unused: "You cannot eat Gleda! Gleda is protected by Grok!"

An NPC called Drunk Cultist was meant to be part of this quest, and she is still placed in Morvunskar, near the base of the portal to Misty Grove, but her ref is never activated. Since she doesn't have any dialogue leftover, it's unknown what purpose she would've served.

There is dialogue present in three different voice types which was meant for (apparent) bandits that you would've encountered in another random encounter after completion of the quest. The bandits would've been familiar with you, and it seems that you and Sam wronged them in some way, as they would apparently attack after saying the following lines: "Once you leave the party you can't just come back.", "Lets [sic] see how tough you are without Sam keeping an eye on you.", "No Sam, no protection. Time to die."
Version 4.1.2 of the Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch replaces the 2 bottles of Alto Wine in the Temple of Dibella with Holy Water.
If you return to Misty Grove after the quest you will be permanently stuck there.
The Official Skyrim Patch, version 1.4, fixes this bug.
Reload a save from before you entered.
It is possible that you will not blackout after the third drink. The reason for this is that one of the characters essential for the quest has died.
The Official Skyrim Patch, version 1.5, addresses this issue. Senna, Ennis, and Ysolda are now marked essential and thus unkillable.

You can use the console to advance the quest using the setstage command. You will need to resurrect the dead NPCs first (all three must be alive to start the quest). To resurrect an NPC type prid refID into the console, followed by enable, resurrect 1, and moveto player (the refIDs are 263CD (Senna), 1CB2B (Ennis), 1A69A (Ysolda)).
Although Senna, Ennis, and Ysolda became essential with Official Skyrim Patch 1.5, the quest may still fail to start after the third drink.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2.6, addresses this issue. Bethesda did not resurrect them if they had already died before Patch 1.5.
The miscellaneous quest prompt to start A Night To Remember refers to Sam Guevenne as Sam Guenvere.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.3, fixes this bug.
After completion of this quest, you may find Sanguine roaming around Morvunskar, killing every mage he can find. Since he is essential, he will always win.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0, fixes this bug.

If you persuade or bribe Senna, then pick up all the trash anyway, the objective to apologize to her will appear, and she will become a quest target, but you can't apologize. The trash also never got disabled once you had left if you DON'T pick it up.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.1, fixes this bug.
You can skip/fix this by leaving the temple, going to Whiterun and talking to Ysolda about the ring.
You also can apologize after you kill Moira and loot her corpse.
The bribery option with Senna doesn't advance your Speech skill due to a missing property.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.4, fixes this bug.

If you convince Ysolda to tell you where the wedding is, going to Witchmist Grove to get the ring results in the quest objective to return it becoming totally stuck. The Hagraven should be disabled at this point as she is not intended to be available when Morvunskar has been revealed.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.4, fixes this bug.
Ysolda may present the dialogue option to accept the wedding ring even if you don't have it with you.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.5, fixes this bug.

The fix from Unofficial Skyrim Patch 2.0.5 created a new bug. Although Ysolda no longer presents the dialogue to accept the wedding ring if you don't have it, the dialogue option to give the ring back to her after retrieving it disappeared too.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.6, addresses this issue. The added condition was incorrectly checking if YSOLDA had the ring, rather than you.
Ysolda won't properly forcegreet you to talk about the ring because she had no proper AI packages for this like all the other NPCs in this quest.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.9, fixes this bug.

The fix from Unofficial Skyrim Patch 2.0.4 only partially fixed the hagraven bug. Although the wedding ring issue has been resolved, the patch forgot to disable Moira in a retro script if the quest had advanced to revealing Morvunskar. Moira should not remain active after that.
The Unofficial Skyrim Legendary Edition Patch, version 3.0.1, fixes this bug.
Ysolda delivers a different line for female players indicating the spouse is male. This is incorrect since the NPC in question is a hagraven, and those are always female.
The Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 4.2.5, fixes this bug.
Sometimes the trash in the Temple of Dibella or Moira won't appear.
Try exiting the Temple to Markarth, then reentering the Temple.
Sometimes Sanguine might not appear at all.
It is possible that when talking to Senna that the dialogue may crash thus not allowing to ask about Sam and preventing any further progress in the quest.
This bug can be worked around by talking to Ennis in Rorikstead.
On PS4, saving immediately upon arrival to the temple and then loading the save, also fixes the problem, allowing you to talk to Senna.
If you enter Misty Grove as a werewolf, Sanguine will be hostile.

quick: Collect thirty samples of the mysterious Crimson Nirnroot.
Take these samples to Sinderion's colleague Avrusa Sarethi so that Sinderion's research may continue.

walkthrough.heading: The "Noisy Red Weed"
paragraphs: Sinderion had been obsessed with Crimson Nirnroot since purchasing a plant from a passing adventurer wanting to get something for the "noisy red weed" he found. Sinderion compensated the man, and then left Skingrad to set up a laboratory in Blackreach, the only known habitat of Crimson Nirnroot.

walkthrough.heading: Continue the Research
paragraphs: The quest begins upon the collection of a sample crimson nirnroot in Blackreach. Your journal will update to reflect your part in finding out the significance of this plant. In order to get started, begin at the beginning in Sinderion's Field Laboratory. The research facility is located in Blackreach, right across from the gates of Alftand Cathedral. Inside you will find Sinderion's remains still clutching his field journal. After reading the journal, the quest will update requesting that you collect thirty Crimson Nirnroot samples from Blackreach - a difficult but rewarding task.

walkthrough.heading: Locating the Samples
paragraphs: There are forty-four samples of Crimson Nirnroot within Blackreach (including some inside Blackreach's buildings). Unlike the more common garden variety Nirnroot, the Crimson Nirnroot does not solely grow near bodies of water. Many plants are found near patches of mushrooms, Dwemer pipes or along the sides of the cavern. Since there are forty-four plants, all required samples can be collected at one time if you thoroughly explore Blackreach (see the Crimson Nirnroot article for more details on plant locations). Alternatively, if you are having a hard time finding enough plants, they will respawn. Leaving Blackreach for ten days allows you to collect another sample from any previously-harvested plants.

walkthrough.heading: A Job Well Done
paragraphs: After collecting the required number of plants, the quest will update again and you will be asked to deliver them to Avrusa Sarethi, Sinderion's former colleague. She is currently residing at Sarethi Farm, between Riften and Ivarstead. Give Avrusa the thirty Crimson Nirnroot samples to complete the quest and receive The Nirnroot Missive. You will also be provided with Sinderion's Serendipity, an ability which provides a 25% chance to mix two potions instead of one.

stages.text: I've discovered an unusual ingredient called Crimson Nirnroot. Objective 5: Discover the significance of Crimson Nirnroot

I've discovered the remains of Sinderion, an alchemist from Skingrad in Cyrodiil. He was exploring Blackreach in search of the Crimson Nirnroot, and appeared to be on the brink of an amazing discovery. Objective 10: Collect Crimson Nirnroot in Blackreach (<Global=NN01Count>/30)

I have brought my Crimson Nirnroot to Avrusa Sarethi, a former student of Sinderion. She was overjoyed that I was able to complete Sinderion's field work and pledged to continue his research in his memory.

notes: The Alchemy perk Green Thumb does not affect Nirnroot and therefore cannot be used to decrease the number of plants needed to be harvested.
The quest is a sequel to the Oblivion quest, Seeking Your Roots.

While this quest is active and toggled on in the quests log, the spell Clairvoyance will determine that the Dragonborn is the closest quest marker, making Clairvoyance less useful. Toggling the quest off mitigates this issue.
The counter for the number of Crimson Nirnroots in your inventory may not function properly, resulting in a number of related issues:
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.2, fixes this bug.

if you consume all the Crimson Nirnroot in your inventory, not only will that amount be redacted from the quest counter, but the counter will even count the removed roots twice, potentially causing the counter to go into the negatives.

The quest may update telling you to return the nirnroot and stating you have found 30 samples when you have actually found less. Once you have the required amount, you will be able to return it and the quest should continue as normal.
Once all thirty Crimson Nirnroots have been collected the option to give them to Avrusa is not there, thus freezing the quest.
Simply drop one and pick it back up to continue the quest.
If you place Crimson Nirnroot in a container or follower's inventory, or otherwise remove it from your inventory, the appropriate number may or may not be removed from the quest log.

To complete the quest even if the quest log does not represent the actual amount of Crimson Nirnroot you have in inventory simply go to Avrusa with thirty in your inventory, and the quest will complete itself without updating in the journal.

The number of Crimson Nirnroot in the quest log is thrown off if you transfer them to or from a container in groups. If you place more than one in a container at one time the quest log will think you only moved one. The quest log number can be corrected by placing them in a container and pulling them out individually (e.g., it says you have nine but you have ten: place two in a container at one time, and then pull them out one at a time). You can also get the quest log up to 30/30 with this method, but you cannot complete the quest without thirty in your inventory.

To fix the count directly, use the console commands: set NN01Count to amount and UpdateQuestInstanceGlobal NN01 NN01Count . Note that this will not cause the quest to advance if set directly to 30. To do so, drop one and pick it up again.
Certain samples of the Crimson Nirnroot can in very rare cases be impossible to pick up and added to your inventory.
This bug can be fixed by reloading a previous save. If reloading does not work, you can try picking up other samples of the Crimson Nirnroot.

quick: Meet and talk to Anska in High Gate Ruins and agree to help her.
Protect Anska as you fight through the ruins.
Defeat Vokun.
Retrieve Anska's scroll.

walkthrough.heading: Anska
paragraphs: High Gate Ruins is a remote Nordic ruin on the snowy tundra east of Solitude, near the shores of the Sea of Ghosts. When you enter, it soon becomes clear that someone visited the ruin recently, as the residing draugr have already been killed. Proceed into the first room and you will meet the person responsible, a Nord wizard named Anska. When approached she will introduce herself and ask if you are there to help her as she has finally located Vokun's Crypt. She then explains her goal, namely to locate a special scroll that could link her family blood all the way back to the legendary Ysgramor. She will also briefly describe Vokun as "Some old priest buried here long ago.", hinting at her lack of research and explaining her need for help. She fears the old priest could awaken and prove too powerful a foe, so she wants you to lead her through the ruin and help her fight the opposition. Accept her request and the quest will start.

walkthrough.heading: High Gate Ruins
paragraphs: Anska is not your average follower and you will have to escort her safely through the ruin; she is, however, capable of taking care of herself using a variety of leveled wizard spells, so keep an eye out and stay upfront as you proceed into the dungeon. Take the northern tunnel to a huge chamber infested with leveled draugr. Claim some minor loot from the chest in the alcove, then head upstairs and locate the iron door leading north where three more draugr will attack. Go through the room with the alchemy lab and a few useful potions. The next tunnel contains a pressure plate triggering a spike wall, so make sure Anska gets through unharmed. A lever puzzle awaits in the next room, so take a thorough look at the symbols above the southern ledge. From left to right, they are: Eagle—Whale—Fox—Snake. Look around the room for the levers, all of them on pedestals with corresponding symbols. The two first levers are upstairs while the last two are on the ground floor. When all four levers are pulled in the right order, the grate in the middle of the room will disappear, so head downstairs and enter the catacombs through the door.

Only one draugr will attack you in the first section of the catacombs and a slide will lead you down to another catacomb area with more draugr. A chest can be found in an alcove, but watch out for the pressure plate and the corresponding darts. Before long, you will reach a room with a leveled soul gem resting on a weight sensitive plate, which releases two draugr from the adjacent coffins if triggered. The locked door to the right contains a chest behind it. Continue into a hallway filled with ancient carvings and numerous pressure plates on the floor, triggering darts or spear traps, then proceed into another puzzle room. Facing the lever, two stone walls cover hidden doors, so pull the lever and watch the wall to the right disappear, then fight the boss-leveled draugr guarding another lever. Pull that lever and the door to the left will open and release yet another boss-leveled draugr. Pull the lever behind him, then head through the now-opened entrance to the east and into Vokun's throne room.

walkthrough.heading: Vokun
paragraphs: Before the throne room, a hallway offers a few potions. As soon as you open the next door, the dragon priest Vokun will burst out of his sarcophagus and use his staff of fireballs to attack you from a distance. Anska will keep her distance from Vokun, but will use her ranged attacks to help out. Defeat the priest and claim his unique mask and his staff from the remains. Proceed to the chamber to the east, where you will find a word wall with a word for the Storm Call Shout. The nearby table holds the sealed scroll for Anska, so pick it up and hand it to her. She will be overwhelmed with joy and hand you the unique spell tome for learning the spell Conjure Flaming Familiar as a reward. Additionally, a boss-leveled chest can be found on the upper level to the north, in an alcove right next to the shortcut back to the first zone of the ruin. Anska will stay behind and try to decipher the scroll indefinitely.

stages.text: Find Anska's scroll and return it to her for a reward.
Help Anska retrieve the scroll from High Gate Ruins.
I have the scroll, I should return it to Anska for my reward.
High Gate Ruins is clear and Anska has rewarded me with a powerful new fire spell.
I have failed to protect Anska, now I'll never know what her scroll was for.

notes: Be careful about bringing other followers with you, since Anska's use of Destruction magic can cause them to attack her if she hits them by mistake, or if they hit her.
This quest only counts towards the Sideways achievement if Anska survives.

Should you choose not to hand over the scroll to Anska right away, she'll continue to follow you around, but only within close proximity to the ruins. In other words, she can't be used as a "free" follower. If you withhold the scroll from her and head outside, then later give her the scroll, she will return to the ruins and remain in Vokun's throne room indefinitely.

It is possible to clear the dungeon without Anska's help. To do this, avoid talking to her when you enter the dungeon. Once Vokun is dead, she will run up to you and allow for the quest to finish normally.
Anska is not considered an essential NPC, and can be killed prior to starting the quest. This prevents the start of the quest and the acquisition of the Flaming Familiar spell.
Area of effect spells such as Fire Storm or Unrelenting Force can cause objects, including the scroll, to fly around the room, potentially becoming lost.
On entering the Catacombs, Anska will comment on the soul gem well before you reach it, and before it is in your line of sight.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2, fixes this bug.
Similarly, she may comment on Vokun's presence and the scroll beyond him ("There it is! On the table!"), before the door to his throne room is even open.
You may be stuck with the sealed scroll, should you pick it up after failing the quest.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.1, fixes this bug.
Upon killing Vokun, Anska may just stand in battle pose, not finishing the quest.
This can be fixed by opening the console, targeting Anska, and using the recycleactor command. She will then vanish, re-enter the room, run toward Vokun's tomb, and you can now speak to her.
The scroll may be left in your inventory after you complete the quest (you can remove it at that stage though, since it is no longer a quest item).
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.1, fixes this bug.

Leaving the reward room without taking the scroll will lead you to be locked out of the room. Even if you return to the throne room, the gates will be locked and cannot be opened anymore since the priest is already dead.
If Anska is killed, the quest does not fail.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.3, fixes this bug.

quick: Enter the Ratway and follow the Ghostly Apparition.
Investigate the Vault.
Defeat The Guardian and see if it has affected the shield.
Head to the north chamber and defeat the Guardian again.
Head to the east chamber and defeat the Guardian again.
Return to the sword chamber.

paragraphs: As soon as you install the Dawnfang and Duskfang Creation, head to Riften. Townsfolk are talking about a ghost hiding in the Ratway and guards have warned them not to approach the area. As you begin your search, a ghostly apparition appears to guide you throughout the Ratway to the Guardian Vault. She then disappears in front of the Guardian Vault, leaving you to your investigation.

In the chamber, you find a long dead skeleton and a sword. Upon inspecting the latter, the Vault Guardian tries to stop you and you have to defeat him. His death seems to have weakened the shield protecting the sword, and a door opens to the north. Head there to find once more the Vault Guardian and weaken the shield. Before leaving the northern room, be sure to open the cages to the left of the upper platform. Behind the gate there sits the skeleton of Verrick Tilwald, which will reanimate and attack you as you enter. Once the skeleton is dispatched, take Verrick's Note, which is pinned beneath a dagger on the table next to Of Crossed Daggers. Reading this will initiate the Bloodthirst quest. Return to the sword chamber and head to the east, defeat the Vault Guardian for the last time.
The Guardian and the Ghostly Apparition, in life Lorant and Emma Bouchard, will be reunited and you'll be free to take Dawnfang and Duskfang.

stages.text: I've heard rumors about a ghostly apparition that has been haunting the Ratway in Riften. I should head there and see if I can learn more. Objective 5: Investigate rumors of ghosts in the Riften Ratway
I've heard rumors about a ghostly apparition that has been haunting the Ratway in Riften. I should investigate the area and see if I can learn more. Objective 10: Find the ghost in the Ratway

I found the ghostly woman, but as I drew near to her, she approached a nearby sewer entrance and vanished before my eyes. I should follow her and see where the sewer entrance leads. Objective 17: Follow the ghost

Having followed the apparition, I have found myself inside an abandoned vault. A mysterious sword floats suspended in a magical field at the heart of the vault. Judging by the condition of this place, it looks as if it has lain undisturbed for a very long time. Perhaps if I proceed forward, I may find some answers and a way to unlock the sword.
