The Two-handed skill point awarded by Octieve may not be given.
You may still receive Irnskar Ironhand as a target even if he is dead.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.5, fixes this bug.

quick: Speak to the quest giver.
Challenge them to a brawl.
Win the brawl.
Speak to them again.

paragraphs: If you talk to one of the quest givers they will eventually challenge you to a brawl. The dialogue and circumstances vary from person to person and are listed in the table above. Accepting the challenge means that you place a 100 gold bet on the outcome. You must then brawl them and win. Standard brawling rules apply and use of things such as hostile magic, shouts, and weapons will instantly change it from a brawl to a criminal assault.

Brawling should be relatively easy if you're wearing any armor and have gained at least a few levels. Only low level players on higher difficulties may have issues with winning a brawl. If you are having problems, use some potions and spells with lingering effects and don't forget about racial powers. It may be of use as well to read more in-depth information on unarmed combat. You do not gain any experience from the unarmed combat during a brawl, although you may gain experience in armor skills.

You can only win a brawl with any given person once. If you lose the brawl, you will not get your wagered money back, although you will be able to get a rematch. If you win the brawl, you will get your wager back and receive an additional 100 gold.

notes: There are other quests that simply involve brawling such as Bloody Nose that are in fact separate from this quest, despite being nearly identical in nature.
If you have less than 100 gold when asking for a bet, the combatant may say things like "Come back when you actually have 100 gold."
When you win your wager back and receive an additional 100 gold, a "Gold (200) Added" message will appear on the top left of the screen.
When you engage in a brawl, spectators may say things like these:
"Twelve septims on the big one!"
"Fight! Fight!"
"Drive that snowback to the ground. Come on!"
"You just going to stand there and take it? Fight back."
"Who taught you to fight? Keep those hands up!"

When you engage in a brawl, viewing NPCs become immersed and tend to run around the fight. This can be quite annoying, as they can potentially run between you and your combatant which can lead you to accidentally punching one of the excited onlookers, which counts as an assault. Also, if you run away from the fight and exit through any doors, the first four NPCs who witness your fight will keep following you and will still think you are in a brawl until you fast travel.
Certain considerations apply to the brawl itself:

Although your opponent may say "No magic," you can in fact use magic on yourself, such as armor, healing, or ward spells. However, using spells on your opponent, even beneficial healing spells, will count as assault.
Wearing the Ebony Mail or using a cloaking spell will also count as assault. However, wearing Ahzidal's Armor of Retribution does not.
You can use a shield bash to "punch" your opponent.

Winning the brawl will raise the disposition of the challenger. This will allow you to take low-value items they own, and they may become available as followers or potential marriage partners. See the individual NPC pages for details.

Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the thane quest for the quest giver's hold (with the exception of quest givers who live in Orc strongholds).

Only one radiant quest of a similar type can be assigned at any given time. However, the dialogue to start the brawl is part of the quest, and the quest starts silently when you approach a location containing a quest giver. If two quest givers are near each other (e.g., Cosnach and Chief Burguk), the quest may start for one and block the dialogue to brawl with the other. Besides winning the brawl, the quest will also silently stop after some time away from the location.

Sometimes your opponent may draw their weapon and attack you like in a normal fight. In this case, your only options are to yield or kill them (except Rolff, who is essential), and it is unlikely you will be able to properly complete the quest even if you try again.
Having the Fists of Steel perk may cause your opponent to remain in bleedout mode after you win the fight. Unequipping your Heavy Armor gauntlets will resolve this.
Engaging in a brawl for this quest can cause the Gray Cowl of Nocturnal to permanently lose its ability to detect life and trigger guard hostility.
Engaging in brawls for this quest while wearing the Ebony Mail can inflict the armor's poison damage effect on your opponent, leading to assault bounties.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2.4, fixes this bug.

quick: Speak to the quest giver.
Steal the requested item.
Return to the quest giver.

walkthrough.heading: Dengeir of Stuhn
paragraphs: Dengeir of Stuhn was once the Jarl of Falkreath but has since stepped down and is now a Thane. He is a paranoid and patriotic supporter of the Stormcloaks. He believes that Lod the blacksmith is writing a treasonous letter and wants you to steal it for him.

The letter is on Lod's bedside table. It is simply a note requesting extra iron. Steal it and return it to Dengeir. Dengeir will at first be confused, and then realize Lod is probably not up to treason, even if he is making extra weapons for the Empire. He will then give you a reward of leveled gold.
Completion of this quest opens up another radiant quest, Dark Ancestor.

walkthrough.heading: Malur Seloth
paragraphs: Talking to Malur Seloth and asking him what he does prompts him to reveal that he doesn't really do anything. He wants to appear more mage-like when in the jarl's presence, and wishes to acquire a staff.

The one he wants belongs to Nelacar who resides in the inn. The staff is located in the shop counter in Nelacar's room. Steal it and return to Malur. He will reward you with one skill point in Speech.

walkthrough.heading: Stands-In-Shallows
paragraphs: When speaking to Stands-In-Shallows, he mentions that he overheard sailors talking about their stashed extra powerful Skooma, and he would like to get it.
The bottle is located in the New Gnisis Cornerclub in Windhelm, underneath the second set of stairs. Steal it and return to Stands-in-Shallows, who will reward you with a skill point in Sneak.

stages.text: Objective 10: Steal the <Alias=QuestItem> for <Alias.ShortName=QuestGiver>
Objective 15: Bring the <Alias=QuestItem> to <Alias.ShortName=QuestGiver>

notes: Only one radiant quest of a similar type can be assigned at any given time. You must clear the radiant quest from your miscellaneous quests in order to be eligible to receive another of the same type.
Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the thane quest for the quest giver's hold.
This quest requires you to commit a crime; see that page for details about criminal activity.
Malur's and Shallows' items are available to retrieve from the start of the game, while the letter Dengeir requests only gets enabled once he has mentioned it.
The quest might not trigger if you have already stolen the quest item before talking to the related NPC. Since the quest item is marked as such, you are left with no way of getting rid of it.

quick: Speak to Revyn Sadri to begin the quest and obtain Viola's Gold Ring.
Choose whether to:
Break into Viola Giordano's House and return the ring, or
Tell Viola Giordano about the ring.

walkthrough.heading: The Accidental Fence
paragraphs: Revyn Sadri runs a pawnshop, Sadri's Used Wares, in Windhelm's Gray Quarter. Revyn tends to tell visitors to his store, somewhat overemphatically, that, "All my goods are legitimate, which is more than I can say for some". If you question him on it, he will change his story and confess that he bought a ring before realizing that it matched the description of an item recently stolen from Viola Giordano.

Even if you offer to return the ring for Revyn, he is still worried. He insists that Viola can't be told, because she would surely report the crime to the Jarl. Instead, he wants you to sneak into Viola Giordano's House and leave the ring.

Your quest log at this point suggests that you only have one option for how to proceed, namely to return the ring. However, Revyn's dialogue hints at a second option: you can tell Viola about the stolen ring.

walkthrough.heading: Option 1: Return the Ring
paragraphs: To return the ring, the first step is gaining entrance to Viola's house. Her house is a large manor located in the Valunstrad district, on the west side of town. The front door is locked with a difficult leveled lock (Expert or Master level). Alternatively, you can opt to pickpocket the key from Viola.

Once you enter the house, the dresser where you are expected to place the ring is located immediately to the right of the front door. Open the dresser, and select that you want to "Store" the ring in the dresser. This will trigger a quest update.

Return to Revyn to obtain your reward, a medium leveled amount of gold. In addition, Revyn's disposition towards you will increase. The most immediate implication is that you will be able to freely take all low-cost items in the store and sleep in his bed for free. You will also be able to buy training in Speech to level 50. He is the only Speech trainer that you can trade with (which you can do to get the gold back) without joining the Volkihar vampires.

walkthrough.heading: Option 2: Tell Viola
paragraphs: The other option requires you to find Viola. She is frequently found walking the streets of Windhelm, or else at Candlehearth Hall in the evenings. If you talk to her, you will have the option to tell Viola about the ring. She takes the ring but seems more interested in finding ways to punish Revyn than actually being happy to have the ring back. In particular, she promises to report this to the Jarl and get Revyn's taxes doubled or even tripled.

She will also reward you with a medium leveled amount of gold. Her disposition towards you will increase, one implication being that you can freely take all low-cost items in her house. This is also the only way to be able to marry her. On the other hand, Revyn's disposition will decrease. This will result in negative comments every time you enter his store, but he will still trade with you (and his other dialogue will be as friendly as otherwise).

stages.text: Objective 10: Plant Viola's Gold Ring in Viola Giordano's House
Objective 15: Tell Revyn Viola's Gold Ring has been planted

notes: Because this is a favor quest which positively affects either Revyn or Viola's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the Thane of Eastmarch quest.

After returning the ring in the drawer and getting the quest update, you can remove the ring and tell Revyn that you returned it. The quest will complete and you will still have Viola's ring, which is no longer flagged as a quest item.

quick: Talk to the quest giver.
Travel to the bandit lair or dungeon.
Return to the quest giver for your reward.

stages.text: Objective 10: Kill the leader of <Alias=Dungeon>
Objective 15: Tell <Alias.ShortName=Questgiver> the bandit is dead

notes: If you kill Captain Hargar during the quest Lights Out!, or by clearing out the grotto without the quest, then Ahtar will give you another Bandit Leader as the target provided they haven't been killed already and you have USSEP 3.0.1 installed. It can be either the Bandit Leader at Ironback Hideout or Orphan's Tear respectively. You can however, depending on luck, have Noster One-Eye's miscellaneous quest to retrieve his helmet, Ahtar's "Kill The Bandit Leader" and Lights Out! all running concurrently and all objectives are located within Broken Oar Grotto.
Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the thane quest for the quest giver's hold.
The quest Harsh Master can have identical quest objectives.
Version 3.0.1 of the Unofficial Skyrim Patch adds the missing bandit camp keywords to Orphan's Tear and Ironback Hideout, resulting in them also becoming possible targets for this quest.
Brunwulf Free-Winter only gives the quest when he's not a Jarl. However, if Brunwulf gives you the quest and the Empire captures Windhelm later on, you can still finish it after he becomes Jarl.
The Solstheim locations for this quest contain Reavers instead of regular bandits. Your journal will still say "bandit leader", though.
Post completion of the main Dragonborn storyline, Fanari Strong-Voice may not give you the option to "Kill The Bandit Leader" for the Skaal.

If you are sent to Gallows Rock after you have already completed the Companions quest The Silver Hand, then the previously-killed generic Silver Hand members, as well as the unique Krev the Skinner, will all have respawned.

The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.1, addresses this issue. This version makes sure that Krev doesn't respawn, while Version 2.0.9 makes sure that no Silver Hand respawn at all, and that the dungeon will be reset to its original state.

If you are sent to Uttering Hills Camp and you have already completed Summerset Shadows for the Thieves Guild, you will be unable to complete this quest, as the bandit leader Linwe will already be dead, but there will be an objective arrow pointing to him as if he still needs to be killed.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.3, fixes this bug.

Selecting Linwe's body in the console then typing resurrect will bring him back to life as soon as you resume the game. Killing him again will then count for the quest completion. (Doesn't work if you have already received the favor quest, as resurrecting Linwe—before or after entering the cave—doesn't put the quest arrow back on him and killing him again doesn't complete the quest)
If Linwe's body has already disappeared, typing setstage Favor104 15 in the console will advance the quest.

If setstage Favor104 15 doesn't help you, type the following commands: prid C5688 and then kill. This should select the original quest target and kill him for you, advancing the quest to the next stage.

If prid C5688 doesn't help you, type the following commands: prid C5675, then disable, and then type prid C5675, then enable, and finally resurrect. This should place Linwe at the empty chair where the quest marker is pointing. Additional Summerset Shadow thieves should spawn as well.
If all previous codes don't work, try prid 7d67a, then resurrect and finally kill.

quick: Speak to Sybille Stentor.
Kill the Master Vampire in Pinemoon Cave.
Return to Sybille Stentor for your reward.

paragraphs: Speak to Sybille Stentor in the Blue Palace throne room and ask what her problem is. She will tell you about a local nest of vampires which you should wipe out.

Make your way to Pinemoon Cave, west of Solitude. It is a very small cave with only four chambers, and an assortment of vampires and wolves. You only need to kill the Master Vampire to complete the quest. He can be found in the third chamber, a large room with pews facing an altar. The Master Vampire can be found on the altar area. However, he has two companions who will also attack if you are detected. They will reanimate a corpse of a Nord which lies on a table in the southern part of the chamber.

If you do clear out the cave, there is a locked chest next to the altar. Also do not forget the fourth chamber, the sleeping quarters, which contains the Illusion skill book Incident at Necrom and another chest.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: Exit the way you came in and return to Sybille Stentor for your reward, which is jewelry and a single free skill boost in Illusion.

stages.text: Objective 10: Kill the leader of Pinemoon Cave
Objective 15: Tell Sybille the vampire is dead

notes: Because this is a favor quest which affects Sybille's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the Thane of Haafingar quest.

walkthrough.heading: Amulet of Arkay
paragraphs: There is a guaranteed Amulet of Arkay at Wayward Pass at the Shrine of Arkay. You can also obtain one easily by starting The Taste of Death in Markarth.

Note: Be careful when bringing the amulet back to Torbjorn Shatter-Shield. The quest marker may indicate that you should enter his house, the door of which may be unlocked, but if you enter you may be treated as a trespasser with no option to tell Torbjorn or his wife what your errand is. Meet him on the street during the day instead.

walkthrough.heading: Black-Briar Mead
paragraphs: Black-Briar Mead can be found in large quantities or bought at the Black-Briar Meadery, and are guaranteed in other locations as well, most closely in Lod's House (on the table with the private letter required by Dengeir of Stuhn's quest Some Light Theft). They may also be bought from most innkeeper merchants. There is also one at the end of the cave in Unbound, right where you are told to sneak past the bear.

walkthrough.heading: Mammoth Tusk
paragraphs: If you are willing to steal, you can find a mammoth tusk in several places in Whiterun:
Dragonsreach Jarl's Quarters — go upstairs and into the main room then head into the room to your right; the tusk is atop the bookcases to the right of the door
Jorrvaskr — on the table in the left room
The Bannered Mare — located on top of a bookshelf right behind the counter; jump on the rafters from the room for rent and pluck it off the shelf

If you'd prefer not to steal one and are unable or unwilling to kill a mammoth, Halted Stream Camp just north of Whiterun contains several mammoth tusks. Belethor, the general goods merchant, has a chance of stocking one if you're willing to pay for it. With Hearthfire, a free one can be found in the Main Hall of your home, if you build one. With Dragonborn, one can be found in Severin Manor, and is free to take after you take ownership.

walkthrough.heading: The Mirror
paragraphs: After accepting this quest, a copy of The Mirror can be found in Windhelm's Palace of Kings. This is where your quest marker will point you, but it will count as stealing unless you are Thane of Eastmarch. Captain Aldis will accept a stolen copy.
Copies may also be found on the bookshelf in the sleeping area of Broken Tower Redoubt in the Reach, or in Forsaken Cave in the Pale, over a table in the first tomb's zone.
With Hendraheim, another copy can be found on the table towards right side end of the hall of the house.

walkthrough.heading: Night Falls on Sentinel
paragraphs: A copy of Night Falls on Sentinel will spawn on a crate in Swindler's Den after accepting the quest. Copies may also be found in a bandit camp near The Guardian Stones, and in Volunruud during the quest Silenced Tongues.

walkthrough.heading: Song of the Alchemists
paragraphs: Unfortunately, Song of the Alchemists cannot be obtained without stealing in the base game. After activating this quest, a copy spawns in the Bards College on the main floor, to the right from the entrance on the counter (a blue book). It is not marked as stolen, but you will still incur the penalties of stealing if you are caught taking it. The book can also be stolen from Anise's Cabin near Riverwood.
If you have the Dragonborn expansion, a copy which does not require stealing can be found in Apocrypha, inside the Black Book called Waking Dreams, in Chapter III.
A copy of the book can also be found in the hidden alchemy laboratory of Goldenhills Plantation.

stages.text: Objective 10: Bring one <Alias=QuestItem> to <Alias.ShortName=QuestGiver>

notes: Halted Stream Camp is the location of a bounty quest, possible location of a Dungeon Delving quest from Amren, and possible location of the Amulet of the Moon quest, making it easy to complete multiple quests at once if you choose to find your mammoth tusk there. It is also one of only two locations where the Transmute spell tome may be found.

If Hearthfire is installed, then the Jarl of Falkreath will send you a message via courier once you have become level 9, as long as you have not yet started the Falkreath thane quest. If Rare Gifts is in your journal when the courier is given the message, you will fail the quest and it will be removed from your journal. Reading the note the courier gives you will start the quest Build Your Own Home.
You must have the item in your inventory for the quest giver's quest pointer and dialogue to display.

If you complete the Stormcloaks quest Battle for Solitude, Captain Aldis will no longer be part of the city and the indication arrow for you to follow will lead to a blank floor, where Aldis previously stood.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.0, addresses this issue. This quest will fail as soon as Battle for Solitude is started.
Captain Aldis can be spawned again using the console command player.placeatme 00041FB8. Afterwards, you can speak with him about quests like normal.
An alternative is to type SetObjectiveCompleted Favor110 10 1 in the console to complete the quest and then to remove The Mirror from your inventory by typing player.additem 0001AFDE -1.

It seems likely that Siddgeir was intended to give a leveled piece of armor as a reward, however he gives potions instead. It's also possible that this was a last-minute change.Mod Notes: The FavorRewardArmor property on TIF__00090DEE is set to FavorRewardPotion.

quick: Talk to Jarl Igmund to initiate quest.
Travel to the dungeon.
Kill the Forsworn Leader.
Return to Jarl Igmund in Understone Keep to collect the gold reward.

paragraphs: Travel to Understone Keep in Markarth and speak to Jarl Igmund to initiate the quest in which you have to kill a Forsworn Leader. He will direct you to a dungeon in The Reach, which is where the Forsworn Leader is hiding. You must travel there and face the leader.
Once you travel to the dungeon you will most likely have to deal with most leveled Forsworn before you can eliminate the leader.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: Once you have dealt with him/her, return to Understone Keep to collect your reward from Jarl Igmund.

stages.text: Objective 10: Kill the leader of <Alias=Dungeon>
Objective 15: Return to Igmund

notes: If Raerek is in a room with an adept lock, wait until he is sitting by the Jarl to receive your reward. He is there by 10am.

It is possible to accept this quest and then find that all NPCs are non-aggressive towards you at the site. If this is the case feel free to kill or pickpocket any non-named NPCs (normally simply named "Forsworn") because none of the other NPCs will attack you.

Upon the initial meeting with Jarl Igmund, he may not have the dialogue option to start this quest available. Exiting Understone Keep and fast travelling somewhere else (e.g. Karthwasten) and back may resolve this.
If you complete the No One Escapes Cidna Mine quest line before ever speaking to Jarl Igmund, he may not ever give the dialogue option to start the quest. No known fix.

quick: Speak with Skald, the Jarl of Dawnstar.
Kill the giant at the given camp.
Return to retrieve the bounty.

paragraphs: The Jarl of Dawnstar, Skald, will ask you to deal with a giant to send a message to all the other giants in the hold, for although they are not a problem now, the jarl believes they will be in the future. The giant can be found at one of three camps (above) and can be taken down by any means necessary.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: Once the giant is dead, return to Skald for your reward of gold:
Completing this quest is required to start the Thane of the Pale quest and Purchase land in Dawnstar if Skald is still Jarl.

stages.text: Objective 10: Kill the giant in <Alias=GiantCamp>
Objective 15: Return to Skald

notes: The quest has a minimum level of 22. If you are not level 22 yet, then you cannot receive this quest from Skald. If Brina is jarl (or Skald has been removed from power and then reinstated), this quest is not required to become Thane.

This quest requires a giant to kill. If you have cleared all of the giants from all of the giant camps, then you cannot receive this quest from Skald. To solve this issue, wait or sleep indoors for 30 days and all giant camps will have been respawned.
This quest cannot be started if you have a bounty in The Pale.
The dialogue for starting this quest might not appear. A probable reason is you might have another Favors quest running that tasks you to kill a certain enemy. This prevents this quest from starting.
Another possible fix is to fast travel to a non-cleared giant camp in The Pale and back to Dawnstar, which may make the dialogue option available.
Sometimes the quest objective will not be removed from the journal.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.0, fixes this bug.

quick: Speak to Siddgeir, the Jarl of Falkreath.
Travel to the assigned dungeon.
Kill the bandit leader.
Return to Siddgeir.

paragraphs: The normal prerequisite for this quest is Rare Gifts, a radiant quest which can be given by six different people. If you have received that quest from any of the other five, then you cannot receive it from Siddgeir, and you must complete the other version before you can get it from Siddgeir. It is advisable that, if possible, Siddgeir's version of Rare Gifts should be completed soon after leaving Helgen, as the mead he wants can be found near the exit to the keep.

If you have Hearthfire installed, then at level 9 a courier will deliver a letter from the Jarl of Falkreath. Reading it will trigger the Falkreath version of Build Your Own Home and, when this quest is running, talking to Siddgeir will allow you to start the Bandit Leader quest without any prerequisites.
After completing the prerequisite quest or receiving the letter from Siddgeir, talk to him in order to initiate this quest.
Once you have reached the assigned dungeon, you will only have to kill the bandit leader of that dungeon; killing the lesser enemies is not mandatory, but would make your job easier.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: Return to Siddgeir to collect your reward of gold.

stages.text: Objective 10: Kill the leader of <Alias=BanditCamp>
Objective 15: Return to Siddgeir

notes: Siddgeir is the only Jarl of Falkreath who gives this quest, which is the last prerequisite he requires before starting the Thane of Falkreath quest. If Dengeir is jarl, then he will already consider you a friend, and start that quest without any further prerequisites.
The quest will not be available if you have another "kill the leader" bounty quest active.
The target location and boss are radiantly chosen the first time entering the Falkreath location, usually long before Siddgeir gives the quest.

if you have the concurrent quest Kill Helvard, remember never to turn in the killing bandit quest right after killing Helvard, or you will lose the chance to elevate Jarl's relationshiprank to 2, thus never be able to receive the next quest to become a thane nor be authorized to buy the property Lakeview Manor, the right method is either to turn in the killing bandit quest before killing Helvard, or go somewhere else after killing Helvard, then come back to turn in the killing bandit quest, the reason behind is about relationshiprank, the relationshiprank mechanism is also mentioned in Kill Helvard page.
If you start this quest after Rare Gifts, before you reach level 9 and then get a letter from a courier, a sidequest to see jarl will remain active forever.

If you did not talk to Farengar Secret-Fire during the Bleak Falls Barrow quest yet, you will not get the option to ask the jarl for any jobs, nor will you be able to tell him you got the letter. This will block you from becoming a thane and thus accessing Lakeview Manor until you progress the main quest. If you want to evade starting Dragon Rising to avoid enabling dragons in Skyrim but still want access to Lakeview Manor, you can progress the Bleak Falls Barrow quest to the point where you need to give Farengar the tablet and stop there. This will make Siddgeir give you this quest and you will be able to progress normally to became the thane.

If you start or complete this quest while having a "kill the leader" bounty quest active for the same location, the kill will just act as if you completed that quest, and not credit you for this quest.

quick: Speak to Igmund.
Find Hrolfdir's Shield.
Bring Hrolfdir's Shield to Igmund.

paragraphs: When you ask Igmund if he has more work for you, he will mention how his father was killed by Forsworn when he tried to negotiate with them. He will then ask you to retrieve his father's shield, which is being guarded by a hagraven.

Note that Bleakwind Bluff is by far the easiest location from which to retrieve the shield, as it is a small tower with no interior zones and is only inhabited by a few Forsworn and a hagraven. So if you don't feel like doing an extensive dungeon delve, it is expedient to reload until you get that radiant location. Unlike the previous favor, you don't need to kill anyone, so a stealthy character can easily grab the shield and get out without having to fight.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: As a reward, you will get a leveled piece of armor, which is either a light/heavy cuirass, helmet, or shield of the best quality for your level. In addition, you'll be able to purchase Vlindrel Hall from Raerek. After completing the quest, the shield can be found in the Jarl's private quarters.

stages.text: Objective 10: Find Hrolfdir's Shield for Igmund
Objective 15: Bring Hrolfdir's Shield to Igmund

notes: You cannot get this quest if Igmund is not Jarl of Markarth.
If you have already started the quest, but Markarth comes under Stormcloak control, you will need to find Igmund in the Blue Palace's basement in order to turn in the quest.

If you meet all the requirements for the start of this quest but the dialogue with Igmund is not appearing, try visiting the Shrine of Talos in Markarth before returning to speak with Igmund. The dialogue should then be available.

If you have accepted but not completed this quest and Markarth comes under Stormcloak control, such that Igmund is no longer the jarl, the quest marker will still point you to Markarth, despite the fact that Igmund is now in exile in the Blue Palace.

quick: Obtain quest from Korir, the Jarl of Winterhold.
Journey to the target location.
Retrieve the Helm of Winterhold.
Return to Korir with the helm.

paragraphs: When asking the Jarl of Winterhold, Korir, for work, you may be asked to find the missing Helm of Winterhold, which was worn by Jarl Hanse in the First Era:

Once you've agreed to find it, head to the location marked on your map, and head to the boss chest, where you will find the helm. The location will be randomly selected from the following: Driftshade Refuge, Fort Fellhammer, Hela's Folly, Hob's Fall Cave, Ironbind Barrow, Pride of Tel Vos, Saarthal, Snow Veil Sanctum, Yngol Barrow, Yngvild.
After you have retrieved the helm, return to Korir to receive your reward.

stages.text: Objective 10: Find Helm of Winterhold inside <Alias=Dungeon>
Objective 15: Return Helm of Winterhold to Korir

notes: The journal entry for Driftshade Refuge is listed as Driftshade Sanctuary.

If the location of the helm is at Hela's Folly, you will need to steal the helm from a locked chest. If you are caught by Deekus, he will take everything you stole from the chest except the helm. If arrested by a guard, they will also not take the helm, as its status as a quest item supersedes its stolen status.

You cannot get this quest if Korir is not Jarl of Winterhold. Fortunately, it is only a prerequisite for becoming Thane while Korir is Jarl: if he is replaced, his replacement Kraldar will give you the title without completing this quest or any other.

The helm can be pickpocketed back off Korir if you are skilled enough. It will no longer be a quest item, but appears to retain its Stolen status even if sold to a Thieves Guild fence and repurchased (at least, this was the case with Mallus Maccius in Skyrim Special Edition).

Unlike many "named" objects, there is nothing much special about the Helm of Winterhold. Once it stops being a quest item, it has the exact same properties and sale price as an unenchanted Steel Helmet.

As of the latest version of Skyrim Special Edition, this also means it can be tempered with a Steel Ingot and the Steel Smithing perk. It can even be enchanted. The latter is not possible while it is still a quest item.
If this quest sends you to Yngol Barrow, it breaks the associated quest, causing Yngol's Shade, the Helm of Yngol, and the skeleton it rests upon not to appear as intended.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.4, fixes this bug.
This quest commonly conflicts with Purity of Revenge, causing one or the other to be unable to start until the other is completed.
The Official Skyrim Patch, version 1.9, fixes this bug.
The quest may, through unknown conditions, become repeatable: pointing you to different locations every time it is given.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2.6, fixes this bug.

If you have initiated this quest but subsequently went on to finish the Reunification of Skyrim questline for the Imperial Legion - or if Winterhold changes hands during Season Unending in the Main Quest line - Korir will be replaced as the jarl and be relocated to Brunwulf Free-Winter's house in Windhelm. If you try to give him the helm after Brunwulf becomes Jarl of Windhelm, he is continuously locked up in the house, and picking the lock will only result in him telling you you're trespassing. There is no way to finish the quest and you are stuck with the helm in your inventory, as it cannot be dropped since it's a quest item.

The quest can be completed by attacking and luring Korir outside, calming him, and then speaking with him before he heads back inside. This will incur a bounty. Trying to engage him in conversation just as you are leaving will also lead to him following you outside.

Alternatively, open up the console, click on the jarl and then type Addtofaction 0005A1​A4 1 into the box. This adds an NPC to the player ally faction, which will make a normally hostile NPC be non-hostile. This should allow you to complete the quest.
You can also finish the quest by typing setstage Favor158 20. This will also remove the helm from your inventory.
Jarl Korir may not give a dialogue option to start this quest.
Some reports suggest that the quest is flagged as completed as soon as one gains access to the College.
This quest can only be started the first time you visit Winterhold, if you fast travel away before initiating the quest then you won't be able to start it.
Starting the quest via console does not work. You can bypass this quest and still become Thane of Winterhold on PC with player.setrelationshiprank 1c1b5 2.

paragraphs: It is a standard fetch-and-return quest. The item will be found in the boss chest in the target dungeon, and is treated as a quest item.

walkthrough.heading: Amren's Family Sword
paragraphs: When you encounter Amren, he may be arguing with his wife Saffir. If asked about the argument, Amren will tell you about his father's sword:
Volunteering to retrieve the sword for him triggers the start of the quest.

When you return the sword, Amren gives you a one point bonus in both Block and One-handed, commenting, "Here, my father had a favorite sword and shield technique. Let me teach it to you, in honor of his memory."

walkthrough.heading: Shahvee's Amulet of Zenithar
paragraphs: If you talk to Shahvee you may have the option to ask her, "Your people have bad luck?" In response she will tell you:
Volunteering to retrieve the amulet triggers the start of the quest.

When you return the amulet, Shahvee gives you a one point bonus in both Light Armor and Lockpicking, commenting, "Before I came into Zenithar's calling, I confess I was a thief. But I learned a few things in my time that might help you survive. Let me show you."

stages.text: Objective 10: Find <Alias=QuestItem> inside <Alias=Dungeon>
Objective 15: Return <Alias=QuestItem> to <Alias.ShortName=QuestGiver>

notes: Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the thane quest for the quest giver's hold.
It is impossible to do both quests at the same time, e.g., if you do the quest for Amren, you are unable to do it for Shahvee until you have completed the quest for Amren.

Shahvee's Amulet can spawn in Uttering Hills Camp, a location that also has a chance for Annekke Crag-Jumper or Brunwulf Free-Winter's personal quests. If they do, none of these quests can be taken at the same time. Waiting 30 days outside their map cells will allow one of the other quests to be taken.
You may be unable to receive this quest from Shahvee, even if none of the other quests are active.

The quest for Amren also conflicts with the miscellaneous quest that can be obtained from the dead Treasure Hunter World Interaction. If you have this uncompleted radiant miscellaneous quest in your quest log, then you will not be able to see the dialogue option to receive Amren's quest when talking to him.

quick: Fight or sneak your way through a dungeon.
Retrieve an item.
Return the item.

paragraphs: This is a radiant quest which you can receive from any of the following five people. The dungeon is randomly determined from those in the table, which are based on the hold in which the quest-giver resides.

stages.text: Objective 10: Find <Alias=QuestItem> inside <Alias=Dungeon>
Objective 15: Return <Alias=QuestItem> to <Alias.ShortName=QuestGiver>

notes: Once you've turned in these quests, the items you were meant to retrieve can then be either pickpocketed from the quest-giver, looted off their corpse, or purchased from them if they are a merchant. The most valuable item to take is the Ring of Pure Mixtures, which is one of only two guaranteed Fortify Alchemy enchantments in the game that can be disenchanted (and the only one that does not require you to join a faction or complete an optional leg of a particular quest). It can be purchased from Frida once you deliver it, but only with the Merchant perk.
If you make Roggi Knot-Beard a follower, you may be able to take the shield from his inventory.

Only one radiant quest of a similar type can be assigned at any given time. You must clear the radiant quest from your miscellaneous quests in order to be eligible to receive another of the same type.
Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the thane quest for the quest giver's hold.
Frida and Oengul will only have the relevant dialogue options during their business hours.
Shrouded Grove should also have been available for Frida's quest, but the location wasn't marked as a cave.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.3, fixes this bug.
For the skill-increase rewards, the quest giver may say that they are giving you the training, but the skill does not actually increase, and you don't get a notification that it has increased.

This may happen when that skill was very close to leveling up anyway when you returned the item to the quest giver. One possible solution is to reload a save from before you returned the item, level up that skill by other means (using it, hiring a trainer, or reading a skill book), and then turn the item in.

quick: Befriend the Jarl of the Reach.
Assist five people of the Reach.
Purchase Vlindrel Hall.
Return to the jarl for your reward.

paragraphs: This is an umbrella quest for several other quests that must be completed if you wish to become Thane of the Reach. The Jarl requires you buy the house in town as well as performing five favors for the townsfolk. Once this is achieved you can become Thane.

In order to receive this quest you must first aid the current Jarl. If the Jarl is Igmund, then you must usually kill a Forsworn leader and Find Hrolfdir's Shield; however, if he was ousted from Markarth during Season Unending and reinstated following The Battle for Fort Sungard, that is sufficient to begin this quest. If the Jarl is Thongvor, whether he was installed via Season Unending or The Battle for Fort Sungard, then the completion of that quest is sufficient to fulfill the prerequisite.

Once you have completed the prerequisite, speak with the Jarl again and he will ask you to assist the people of the hold. You must assist five people in the hold, usually by completing favor quests for them. Note that many of the quest givers are non-essential NPCs, so their deaths would result in a loss of potential quests to complete. If they die after you assist them, they still count towards your Thane status. You can also befriend merchants if you have the Investor perk by investing in their stores.

Note that there are several favor quests involving members of Orc strongholds in the Reach; assisting Orcs living in strongholds does not count towards your Thane quest, but Orcs in Markarth do count.

You may consider completing The Heart of Dibella as successfully completing it befriends all four of the priestesses of Dibella, which is almost enough to qualify for thaneship alone. It also requires you to visit Karthwasten; resolving the Sanuarach mine dispute there (for either side) will be enough to complete this requirement.
You must also purchase Vlindrel Hall, which costs 8,000 gold. Simply purchasing it is enough, there is no requirement to decorate, although it becomes more useful if decorated.

walkthrough.heading: The Reach Favor Quests
paragraphs: Highlighted quests can be easily completed without any skill use. If any citizen offers multiple favor quests, only the first completed one will count towards Thaneship.
Note that Gharol's Message does not count towards this objective, as Gharol and the Stronghold Orcs are not designated as citizens of the Reach.

walkthrough.heading: The Reach Stores
paragraphs: Investing 500 gold in certain stores will count towards Thaneship if you have not befriended the store's owner by other means. If the original owner dies and you had already invested in their store, you [can / cannot ] also befriend their replacement.

walkthrough.heading: Other Quests
paragraphs: The following quests also increase the disposition of citizens of the Reach, and therefore count towards this objective:
No One Escapes Cidhna Mine: If you resolve it in favor of Thonar Silver-Blood.
The Book of Love: Help the Temple of Mara spread the cause of love throughout Skyrim.
The Heart of Dibella: Find a new Sybil for the Temple of Dibella.
New Allegiances: If you turn Cairine into a Vampire.
Private Lessons: Teach Lynea how to fish.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: After helping five inhabitants and purchasing Vlindrel Hall, the journal tells you to return to the Jarl. The reward, the Blade of the Reach, is a random, leveled, enchanted axe. There is a 50% chance that it will be a war axe (one-handed), and a 50% chance it will be a battleaxe (two-handed). You will also receive a housecarl named Argis the Bulwark, who will be waiting for you at Vlindrel Hall.

stages.text: Objective 10: Purchase a house in Markarth
Objective 15: Return to <Alias.ShortName=QuestGiver>

notes: The misnamed Blade of the Reach is an axe (not a blade).
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2.4, fixes this bug.
The weapon may not place properly on weapon racks or plaques. Even on racks it will place horizontally, with the blade part of the axe not showing.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.4, fixes this bug.

The dialogue option to start the thane quest may not appear. This happens if you have too many unfinished miscellaneous favor quests in your quest log. Do a few of these quests and the thane dialogue will appear.

quick: Befriend the Jarl of Haafingar by completing her favor quest.
Assist five people of Haafingar.
Purchase Proudspire Manor.
Return to the Jarl for your reward.

paragraphs: This is an umbrella quest for several other quests that must be completed if you wish to become Thane of Haafingar. The jarl requires you to buy the house in town as well as performing five favors for the townsfolk. Once this is achieved you can become Thane.

In order to receive this quest you must first aid the current jarl, Elisif the Fair, by investigating disturbances in a nearby cave and then completing her favor quest. Once you have completed the prerequisite, speak with the jarl again and she will ask you to assist the people of the hold. You must assist five people in the hold, usually by completing favor quests for them. Note that many of the quest givers are non-essential NPCs, so their deaths would result in a loss of potential quests to complete. If they die after you assist them, they still count towards your Thane status. You can also befriend merchants if you have the Investor perk by investing in their stores.
You must also purchase Proudspire Manor, which costs 25,000 gold. Simply purchasing it is enough, there is no requirement to decorate, although it becomes more useful if decorated.

walkthrough.heading: Haafingar Favor Quests
paragraphs: Highlighted quests can be easily completed without any skill use. If any citizen offers multiple favor quests, only the first completed one will count towards Thaneship.
Note that Return to Grace and Fit for a Jarl do not count towards this objective, as they do not affect anyone's disposition.

walkthrough.heading: Haafingar Stores
paragraphs: Investing 500 gold in certain stores will count towards Thaneship if you have not befriended the store's owner by other means. If the original owner dies and you had already invested in their store, you [can / cannot ] also befriend their replacement.

walkthrough.heading: Other Quests
paragraphs: The following quests also increase the disposition of citizens of Haafingar, and therefore count towards this objective:
Diplomatic Immunity, if you help Erikur talk to Brelas.
The Man Who Cried Wolf: Investigate reports of strange happenings in Wolfskull Cave.
Tending the Flames: Unveil the truth about a deceitful King and become a member of the Bards College.
The Wolf Queen Awakened: Potema must be stopped.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: After helping five inhabitants and purchasing Proudspire Manor, the journal tells you to return to the jarl. The reward, the Blade of Haafingar, is normally a random, leveled, enchanted sword or greatsword. Due to a bug, however, maces are also occasionally rewarded. You will also receive a housecarl named Jordis the Sword-Maiden, who will be waiting for you at Proudspire Manor.

stages.text: Objective 10: Purchase a house in Solitude
Objective 15: Return to <Alias.ShortName=QuestGiver>

notes: Bryling is also set up to give you this quest; she's part of the relevant faction, is included in the related scripting, and has the lines recorded in her voice type. However, since at no point in the final game is there an opportunity for Bryling to become Jarl of Haafingar, this functionality goes completely unused.
If the quest Tending the Flames is active, Elisif might not give the dialogue option to start this quest until after the Tending the Flames quest is complete.

When you become Thane of Haafingar under Imperial rule, the guards do not recognize you as such and there is no thane option to forgive you of petty crime. However, Stormcloak guards in the same city do have this option.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.0, fixes this bug.
The relevant script expects Elisif to be a part of Imperial government faction, but she wasn't actually added to it. To fix this, select Elisif in the console and type addtofaction 00036633 1.
If you become Thane of Haafingar while it is under Imperial rule, and it later is conquered by the Stormcloaks, you retain your Thane status and can use it to remove a bounty then.
If you complete all five favors before being given the quest to do so, the quest will not update correctly, leaving you with a journal entry "Assist the People of Haafingar 5/5".
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2, fixes this bug.

To fix this, complete a sixth favor, such as the Tending the Flames quest, which will give you the message "Completed: Assist the People of Haafingar 6/5", thus allowing you to continue on as intended.
Use the console command player.setobjectivecompleted favorjarlsmakefriends 30 1 to update it and remove it from your journal.
The quest may not track how many favors you have performed, making it impossible to complete the quest.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.5, fixes this bug.
If you have the quest "Tending the Flames" active, Elisif will not give you the quest until you reach the stage where you need to speak to Jorn.

quick: Assist the people of Whiterun Hold.
Purchase Breezehome.
Return to the jarl for your reward.

paragraphs: This is an umbrella quest for several other quests that must be completed if you wish to become Thane of Whiterun. In order for Vignar to be jarl, you have to have completed Battle for Whiterun for the Stormcloaks. Completing this quest befriends him automatically.

Speak with the jarl and he will ask you to assist the people of the hold. You must assist five people in the hold, usually by completing favor quests for them. Note that many of the quest givers are non-essential NPCs, so their deaths would result in a loss of potential quests to complete. If they die after you assist them, they still count towards your Thane status. You can also befriend merchants if you have the Investor perk by investing in their stores.

You must also purchase Breezehome, which costs 5,000 gold, if you have not done so already. Simply purchasing it is enough, there is no requirement to decorate, although it becomes more useful if decorated.

walkthrough.heading: Whiterun Favor Quests
paragraphs: Highlighted quests can be easily completed without any skill use. If any citizen offers multiple favor quests, only the first completed one will count towards Thaneship.
Note that completing Erik the Slayer does not count towards this objective, as it does not affect anyone's disposition.

walkthrough.heading: Whiterun Stores
paragraphs: Investing 500 gold in certain stores will count towards Thaneship if you have not befriended the store's owner by other means. If the original owner dies and you had already invested in their store, you [can / cannot ] also befriend their replacement.

walkthrough.heading: Other Quests
paragraphs: The following quests also increase the disposition of citizens of Whiterun, and therefore count towards this objective:
Before the Storm: Inform the Jarl of Whiterun about the dragon attack on Helgen.
A Blade in the Dark: Prove you are Dragonborn to Delphine by slaying the dragon Sahloknir.
The Blessings of Nature: Restore the Gildergreen for Danica Pure-Spring.
The Golden Claw: A shopkeeper wants you to retrieve his prized possession from a bandit.
Missing In Action: Rescue a missing Stormcloak supporter from the Thalmor.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: After helping five inhabitants and purchasing Breezehome, the journal tells you to return to the jarl. The reward, the Blade of Whiterun, is a random, leveled, enchanted blade. There is a 50% chance that it will be a sword (one-handed), and a 50% chance it will be a greatsword (two-handed).
This is changed with version 2.1.3 of the Unofficial Skyrim Patch.

stages.text: Objective 10: Purchase a house in Whiterun
Objective 15: Return to <Alias.ShortName=QuestGiver>

quick: Befriend the Jarl of Eastmarch by progressing through the civil war questline and complete quest Blood on the Ice.
Assist five people of Eastmarch.
Purchase Hjerim.
Return to the jarl for your reward.

paragraphs: This is an umbrella quest, involving several other quests that must be completed if you wish to become Thane of Eastmarch. You will have to capture Falkreath for the Stormcloaks and complete quest Blood on the Ice (if you joined the Stormcloaks) or complete the Battle for Windhelm (if you sided with the Imperials) before this quest becomes available. Once you have completed the prerequisite, speak with the jarl again and he will ask you to assist the people of the hold. You must assist five people in the hold, usually by completing favor quests for them. Note that many of the quest givers are non-essential NPCs, so their deaths would result in a loss of potential quests to complete. If they die after you assist them, they still count towards your Thane status. Also, you can befriend merchants if you have the Investor perk by investing in their stores.

You must also purchase Hjerim, which costs 8,000 to 12,000 gold. Simply purchasing it is enough; there is no requirement to decorate, although it becomes more useful if decorated. Note that it cannot be decorated unless you have completed Blood on the Ice, and if you have not started that quest yet you should start it before entering Hjerim.

walkthrough.heading: Eastmarch Favor Quests
paragraphs: Highlighted quests can be easily completed without any skill use. If any citizen offers multiple favor quests, only the first completed one will count towards Thaneship.
Note that completing Harsh Master does not count towards this objective, as Kjar is erroneously designated as a Winterhold citizen.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.1.2, fixes this bug.

walkthrough.heading: Eastmarch Stores
paragraphs: Investing 500 gold in certain stores will count towards Thaneship if you have not befriended the store's owner by other means. If the original owner dies and you had already invested in their store, you [can / cannot ] also befriend their replacement.

walkthrough.heading: Other Quests
paragraphs: The following quests also increase the disposition of citizens of Eastmarch, and therefore count towards this objective:
Innocence Lost: Help an orphaned child avoid being returned to a sadistic caretaker.
Rise in the East: Help the East Empire Company take care of some pirates.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: After helping five inhabitants and purchasing Hjerim, the journal tells you to return to the jarl. The reward, the Axe of Eastmarch, is a random, leveled, enchanted axe. There is a 50% chance that it will be a war axe (one-handed), and a 50% chance it will be a battleaxe (two-handed). You will also receive a housecarl named Calder, who will be waiting for you at Hjerim.

stages.text: Objective 10: Purchase a house in Windhelm
Objective 15: Return to <Alias.ShortName=QuestGiver>

notes: Interestingly, when naming you Thane, Ulfric and Brunwulf do not say "Wouldn't want them to think you're part of the common rabble, now." like most other Jarls do.

After finishing the quest "Battle for Windhelm" for the Imperials, Brunwulf Free-Winter sometimes won't appear in the Palace of the Kings. All Stormcloak-supporting jarls and their housecarls will be there sitting at a table, but without Brunwulf in the palace. Without him, you are unable to purchase Hjerim or become Thane of Eastmarch.

One of the possible fixes: use the Unrelenting Force shout on everyone at the dinner table. This will give you a bounty in each of the holds that the jarls are from. Travel out of Windhelm and return.

Using console command addfac 00050920 1 gives him new dialogue, but he still will not reside in the Palace of Kings. However, he should give you the Thane dialogue if you have already helped 5 citizens.
After finishing the quest "Blood on the Ice", Ulfric Stormcloak sometimes won't offer the thaneship.

quick: Befriend the Jarl of Hjaalmarch.
Assist three people of Hjaalmarch.
Return to the jarl for your reward.

paragraphs: This is an umbrella quest for several other quests which must be completed if you wish to become Thane of Hjaalmarch. In order to receive this quest, you must first aid the current jarl. You must usually complete Laid to Rest first if the jarl is Idgrod; however, you can begin the quest if she was ousted from Morthal during Season Unending and reinstated following The Battle for Fort Snowhawk. You can also begin the quest if the jarl is Sorli, whether she was installed via Season Unending or The Battle for Fort Snowhawk.

Once you have completed the prerequisite, speak with the jarl again and she will ask you to assist the people of the hold. You must assist three people in the hold, usually by completing favor quests for them. Note that many of the quest givers are non-essential NPCs, so their deaths would result in a loss of potential quests . If they die after you assist them, they still count towards your Thane status. You can also befriend merchants if you have the Investor perk by investing in their stores.

walkthrough.heading: Hjaalmarch Favor Quests
paragraphs: Highlighted quests can be easily completed without any skill use.
Note that Falion's Secret, Payment Delivery and Rising at Dawn do not count towards this objective, as they do not affect anyone's disposition.

walkthrough.heading: Hjaalmarch Stores
paragraphs: Investing 500 gold in certain stores will count towards Thaneship if you have not befriended the store's owner by other means.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: After helping three inhabitants, the journal tells you to return to the jarl. Note that Idgrod in this context refers to Jarl Idgrod (The Elder), not her daughter Idgrod the Younger. The reward, the Blade of Hjaalmarch, is a random, leveled, enchanted sword. There is a 50% chance that it will be a sword (one-handed), and a 50% chance it will be a greatsword (two-handed). Due to a bug, however, maces are also occasionally awarded. You also gain the title of Thane of Hjaalmarch and, if Hearthfire is installed, a personal housecarl, Valdimar.

stages.text: Objective 15: Return to <Alias.ShortName=QuestGiver>

quick: Befriend the Jarl of the Pale.
Assist three people of the Pale.
Return to the jarl for your reward.

paragraphs: This is an umbrella quest for several other quests that must be completed if you wish to become Thane of the Pale. In order to receive this quest you must first aid the current Jarl. If Skald is Jarl of the Pale, then normally, you must first complete Waking Nightmare and then Kill the Giant in order to befriend him. If Skald was ousted from Dawnstar during Season Unending, and then reinstated after The Battle for Fort Dunstad, that will also befriend him. If Brina is Jarl of the Pale (whether she was installed via The Battle for Fort Dunstad or Season Unending), then she is automatically friendly to you.

Once you have completed the prerequisite, speak with the jarl again and he or she will ask you to assist the people of the hold. In order to assist the people of the hold, you must befriend three people who are citizens of the Pale. Usually you do this by completing favor quests on their behalf. All of the favor quests in the Pale are for people in Dawnstar, except for Aeri, who lives at Anga's Mill. Note that you can also befriend merchants if you have the Investor perk by investing in their stores.

walkthrough.heading: The Pale Favor Quests
paragraphs: Highlighted quests can be easily completed without any skill use. If any citizen offers multiple favor quests, only the first completed one will count towards Thaneship.

walkthrough.heading: The Pale Stores
paragraphs: Investing 500 gold in certain stores will count towards Thaneship if you have not befriended the store's owner by other means.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: After helping three inhabitants, the journal tells you to return to the jarl. The Blade of the Pale is awarded along with the title. The Blade of the Pale is a randomly-leveled and randomly-enchanted sword. There is a 50% chance that it will be a sword, and a 50% chance it will be a greatsword. If you have Hearthfire installed, then Gregor will also be assigned to you as a housecarl.

stages.text: Objective 15: Return to <Alias.ShortName=QuestGiver>

notes: It is possible to become Thane of the Pale and receive a leveled Blade of Pale twice. First from Skald and then from Brina.

quick: Befriend the Jarl of Winterhold.
Assist three people of Winterhold.
Return to the jarl for your reward.

paragraphs: This is an umbrella quest for several other quests that must be completed to become Thane of Winterhold. In order to receive this quest you must first aid the current jarl. If the jarl is Korir, then you must usually Retrieve the Helm of Winterhold for him first; however, if he was ousted from Winterhold during Season Unending and reinstated following The Battle for Fort Kastav, that is sufficient to begin this quest. If the jarl is Kraldar, whether he was installed via Season Unending or Rescue from Fort Kastav, then the completion of that quest is sufficient to fulfill the prerequisite.

Once you have completed the prerequisite, speak with the jarl again and he will ask you to assist the people of the hold. You must assist three people in the hold, usually by completing favor quests for them. Note that many of the quest givers are non-essential NPCs, so their deaths would result in a loss of potential quests to complete. If they die after you assist them, they still count towards your Thane status. You can also befriend merchants if you have the Investor perk by investing in their stores.

walkthrough.heading: Winterhold Favor Quests
paragraphs: Highlighted quests can be easily completed without any skill use.

Note that completing Drowned Sorrows does not count towards this objective, as it does not affect anyone's disposition. Be sure to complete Ranmir's Quest all Drunks Have before starting Drowned Sorrows, as he is removed from the game upon its completion.

walkthrough.heading: Winterhold Stores
paragraphs: Investing 500 gold in certain stores will count towards Thaneship if you have not befriended the store's owner by other means.

walkthrough.heading: Other Quests
paragraphs: The following quests also increase the disposition of citizens of Winterhold, and therefore count towards this objective:
The Black Star: Help find and repair Azura's Star.
New Allegiances: Turn the target into a vampire. (radiant)

walkthrough.heading: College Quests
paragraphs: Completing any quest which increases the disposition of the mages at the College of Winterhold will also count towards this objective, including:
Arniel's Endeavor: Uncover an ancient Dwemer secret. (radiant)
Brelyna's Practice: Help Brelyna Maryon by allowing her to practice her spells on you.
Fetch me that Book!: Fetch a book for Urag gro-Shub. (radiant) (second time only)
First Lessons: Join the College of Winterhold.
J'zargo's Experiment: Help a student test out a fiery new spell.
Onmund's Request: Help Onmund negotiate the return of a family amulet from Enthir. (radiant)
Out of Balance: Purify the focus points for magical energy around the College of Winterhold.
Restocking Soul Gems: Help Sergius Turrianus to fill his stock with soul gems.
Enchanting Pick-Up and Shalidor's Insights do not count as they do not affect anyone's disposition.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: After helping three inhabitants, the journal tells you to return to the jarl. The reward, the Blade of Winterhold, is a random, leveled, enchanted sword. There is a 50% chance that it will be a sword (one-handed), and a 50% chance it will be a greatsword (two-handed).

stages.text: Objective 15: Return to <Alias.ShortName=QuestGiver>

notes: Completing Harsh Master for Kjar in Windhelm counts toward this quest because he is erroneously designated as a Winterhold citizen.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.1.2, fixes this bug.

quick: Befriend the Jarl of Falkreath.
Assist three people of Falkreath Hold.
Return to the Jarl for your reward.

paragraphs: This is an umbrella quest for several other quests that must be completed if you wish to become Thane of Falkreath. In order to receive it, you must first aid the current Jarl of Falkreath. If Siddgeir is Jarl, the previous quest will usually be to kill a Bandit Leader; however, if he was ousted from Falkreath during Season Unending and reinstated following The Battle for Fort Neugrad, that is sufficient to begin this quest. If Dengeir is Jarl, whether he was installed via Rescue from Fort Neugrad or Season Unending, then the completion of that quest is sufficient to fulfill the prerequisite.

Once you have completed the prerequisite, speak with the jarl again and he will ask you to assist the people of Falkreath hold three times in order to become Thane. This can be difficult as there are only a limited number of quests in the hold and the quest givers are non-essential, which could result in their death and irrevocable loss of potential quests. Note, however, that you can also befriend merchants if you have the Investor perk by investing in their stores.

walkthrough.heading: Falkreath Favor Quests
paragraphs: Highlighted quests can be easily completed without any skill use.

Note that Dark Ancestor does not count towards this objective, as Some Light Theft is a prerequisite and therefore nullifies the disposition increase. If Dengeir is Jarl, he will not give out either of his personal quests, but if you completed Some Light Theft for him before making him Jarl, then it will still count towards assisting the citizens of Falkreath.

walkthrough.heading: Falkreath Stores
paragraphs: Investing 500 gold in certain stores will count towards Thaneship if you have not befriended the store's owner by other means.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: After helping three inhabitants, the journal tells you to return to the jarl. The reward, the Blade of Falkreath, is a random, leveled, enchanted sword. There is a 50% chance that it will be a sword (one-handed), and a 50% chance it will be a greatsword (two-handed). You will also receive a pittance of gold and the title of Thane for Falkreath Hold. With the Hearthfire add-on, you will also be rewarded a personal housecarl, Rayya.

stages.text: Objective 15: Return to <Alias.ShortName=QuestGiver>

notes: Favors to Falkreath citizens done as part of Daedric quests do not count toward the total.

The quest may become nearly impossible to complete if you finish the Rescue from Fort Neugrad quest for the Stormcloaks before you enter Falkreath, because it will remove Dengeir as a possible favor giver without incrementing the counter.
This can be fixed with the console command setstage favorjarlsmakefriends 95 and setstage favor258 20
Assistance to citizens done prior to accepting this quest counts towards the total.
Siddgeir may become stuck in a "Foe" relationship with you if you've killed his housecarl for the Dark Brotherhood (even if you did it secretly). If so, he'll never grant you Thaneship.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.4, addresses this issue. The relationship will only be harmed if you are caught killing the housecarl.
You can fix this with the console command player.setrelationshiprank 00019822 2
If Siddgeir is no longer Jarl, the new Jarl will grant you Thaneship.
Zaria's store cannot be invested in with the Investor perk.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.0, addresses this issue. You can now befriend her by investing in her shop, which will count towards Thaneship.

quick: Speak to the jarl to receive the quest.
Improve the disposition of three or five people of that hold, usually by doing favor quests for them.
Return to the jarl.

paragraphs: You will need to improve the disposition of three people for the minor holds Falkreath, Hjaalmarch, the Pale, and Winterhold. For the major holds Eastmarch, Haafingar, the Reach, the Rift, and Whiterun, you will need to help five people. The people you help must be ordinary citizens of the hold; members of Khajiit caravans and Orcs living in strongholds do not count, and neither does befriending the hold's Jarl (as that is a prerequisite to being given the objective).
Disposition can be improved in any of the following ways:
by performing favor quests on their behalf
by completing certain side quests
investing 500 gold in stores, if you have the investor perk
dropping some armor pieces in front of citizens and allowing them to keep it
rescuing kidnapped citizens

Citizens that you befriend before starting this quest also count towards your total, and as such, it is possible to complete this objective for a particular hold immediately after starting the Thane quest. Also, citizens that you befriended which then died still count towards your total. (Usually in those cases, you will have received an Inheritance.) Note that if you befriend the same citizen twice, it only counts once for this quest.

stages.text: Objective 10: Assist the people of the Reach (<Global=FriendsCountReach>/5)
(Quest Completed for the Reach)
Objective 20: Assist the people of the Rift (<Global=FriendsCountRift>/5)
(Quest Completed for the Rift)
Objective 30: Assist the people of Haafingar (<Global=FriendsCountHaafingar>/5)
(Quest Completed for Haafingar)
Objective 40: Assist the people of Whiterun (<Global=FriendsCountWhiterun>/5)
(Quest Completed for Whiterun)

(Quest Completed for Eastmarch)

(Quest Completed for Hjaalmarch)
