(Quest Completed for the Pale)
Objective 80: Assist the people of Winterhold (<Global=FriendsCountWinterhold>/3)
(Quest Completed for Winterhold)
Objective 90: Assist the people of Falkreath (<Global=FriendsCountFalkreath>/3)
(Quest Completed for Falkreath)

notes: While the Rift thane quest is active, most of its objectives do not show up in your journal. The Rift thane quest uses its own code to replace the functions of this quest, so Objective 20 is never assigned. The requirement to assist citizens of the Rift is replaced by an invisible requirement to complete miscellaneous objectives in Riften, which starts automatically after completing Supply and Demand. The game will track the number of Riften quests you complete, unlike in other holds where you are required to ask the jarl if there is something you can do to help first. Once you have completed enough miscellaneous quests, you will be given an objective to return to the Jarl of Riften.

If Balgruuf is Jarl of Whiterun, you cannot receive this quest from him. He will make you Thane as a quest reward for completing Dragon Rising, which is early in the main quest. Only if you side with the Stormcloaks and remove him from power is this quest available in Whiterun.

"Assist the people of Haafingar" may not be cleared from your quest log by Solitude's jarl once completed, though you are able to become a thane and gain a housecarl in your home (once purchased). The concern may be complicated by having already helped five people before talking to the jarl for the first time.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2, fixes this bug.
Entering the console command setobjectivecompleted FavorJarlsMakeFriends 30 1 after becoming a thane may resolve this.
Continuing to assist the people of Haafingar can cause the counter to update to 6/5, at which point the objective is completed and cleared from the quest log.

paragraphs: If you talk to one of the quest givers, they will ask you for some gold. Giving them one gold piece completes the quest and rewards you with the blessing The Gift of Charity.

notes: This quest does not have any stages or objectives.
This quest can be repeated indefinitely.
You will not have the option to give a beggar gold for four in-game hours after you last gave a beggar gold, or if you have no gold.

walkthrough.heading: Easy Money
paragraphs: If you talk to one of the quest givers, they will offer to pay you for chopped firewood. Alternatively, you can also chop the firewood first and then sell the firewood to a quest giver later. You are paid five gold per unit of firewood.

walkthrough.heading: Find a Chopping Block
paragraphs: As a general rule, wood chopping blocks are easily found near the quest givers. Otherwise, they can be found in almost any military camp or Khajiit traders caravan camp, and also at the following locations:

walkthrough.heading: Get Chopping
paragraphs: To chop wood you must have a woodcutter's axe in your inventory (one can usually be found near the wood pile). In addition to standard woodcutter's axes, the Poacher's Axe can be used to chop firewood. Activating a wood chopping block will then cause you to produce firewood at a rate of two units every eight seconds, with a limit of six units per activation. After you have produced six units, you must activate the block again or leave the woodcutting session. You can leave partially through, in which you'll either cut two or four units instead.

It is also possible to have a follower chop firewood for you, even if they don't have an axe. By having someone else do the chopping, you can perform other tasks such as smithing and selling items. By multitasking and restarting their orders every few moments, you can earn several hundred gold on the side while performing bartering.

If a second wood chopping block is nearby, you can chop wood simultaneously to double production while only adding an extra couple of seconds to the equation. This can be done early on in Riverwood by getting Faendal as a follower and then using the two chopping blocks near the mill. Use the command feature to command Faendal from afar and maximize efficiency. After twenty or so minutes of woodcutting, you can earn a few thousand gold at the beginning of the game without gaining any XP.

walkthrough.heading: Achievements
paragraphs: An Achievement is related to chopping wood:
Hard Worker (10 points/Bronze) — Chop wood, mine ore, and cook food
To obtain this achievement you do not need to sell the firewood, or even talk to any of the quest givers. Simply activating the wood chopping block is sufficient.

notes: This quest does not have any stages or objectives.
This quest can be repeated indefinitely.

There is no limit to the amount of firewood you can chop at each wood chopping block and then sell. One (painfully slow) way to get the money to purchase a house is to chop the required amount of wood. For the house in Whiterun, for example, you will get 5000 gold if you accumulate 1000 pieces of firewood. This takes approximately 24 hours of game time when the time scale is set around 10, or 25 minutes in real time. At the standard time scale, it is possible to chop 150 pieces of firewood in 15 real-time minutes, which is a pay rate of 3000 gold per real-time hour.

You can also ask a follower to chop wood for you, by entering command mode and selecting a valid chopping block. The follower does not need to be carrying a woodcutter's axe to perform this. They will begin a single cycle of the chopping animation (3 chops gaining 6 wood) before returning to standing idle. They can continue to chop even when they are overencumbered.

As an augmented way to make money, you can find a location which has two chopping blocks nearby, command your follower to use one, and use the other yourself. This will nearly double your output and allow earning a sizable amount of gold in less time.

Riverwood is the easiest location to do this, as it has two blocks, is accessible immediately at the start of the game, and even provides Faendal as an easy-to-get follower to help you chop wood. Note that the follower will need to be reinstructed to chop wood each time they finish, so there is a bit of micromanagement involved. When your character finishes his/her own chopping cycle, return to the follower and repeat the process.
A less tedious method of earning passive gold is simply telling your follower to chop wood while you are in a city or settlement, checking in every once in a while as you go about your business.

Money you earn from chopping wood is fixed and is not affected by your Speech skill. This makes the quest one of the few ways to make money without increasing any skills, which will help control your level. This is useful when wanting to train in a certain skill as many times as possible. It is also one of the few ways to earn money without doing any questing, merchanting, or crafting.
With the Hearthfire add-on, doing this quest for Aeri, Gilfre, Grosta, Hert, or Hod will increase their disposition such that you'll be able to cut your own lumber for construction purposes.
Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the thane quest for the quest giver's hold.

Each unit of firewood weighs 5, and a full use of the chopping block gives 6 wood, for a total weight of 30. If you become overencumbered, which will happen rather quickly, you can drop the entire stack of wood and pick it up by holding the "grab" button to be able to run over to the person to whom you wish to sell it.
Swinging the woodcutter's axe at a chopping block won't produce firewood; you must activate the animation sequence.

Firewood samples found in the wilderness can also be used. Despite the abundance of wood piles which use the same model, these standalone samples can be quite rare. Autumnwatch Tower has three firewood scattered over the floors of the tallest tower. Given the sheer weight of the wood and the fact that only a handful of NPCs will buy firewood at-cost, it is probably not worth the effort to grab these scattered pieces, unless you have a follower to bear the burden.
Like other gathering quests, NPCs do not care if the firewood is stolen.

Some objects in the game world look like wood chopping blocks, but aren't. If it lacks one or both piles of wood along the sides of it, it is not a wood chopping block. When scrolling over a usable block, the "Activate" prompt will appear.

Version 1.2.4 of the Unofficial Skyrim Patch adds woodcutter's axes next to the wood piles in Whiterun, Riften, and Windhelm so that being asked to chop wood won't result in you needing to exit the city and travel to a nearby village just to get an axe.
Version 2.1.2 of the Unofficial Skyrim Patch adds woodcutter's axes next to the wood piles in Kynesgrove, Dragon Bridge, Ivarstead, and Half-Moon Mill for essentially the same reason.
Time doesn't stop while chopping wood so magicka, health, and stamina regenerate while using a chopping block.
Chopped wood can be sold to general goods merchants, though at a much lower price than someone on the list above.

paragraphs: If you talk to one of the quest givers while having alcohol in your inventory, you will have the option to share a drink with them. This then makes them your friend, meaning that you can take low value items that belong to them and that they may occasionally give you a gift.

notes: This quest does not have any stages or objectives.
This quest can be repeated indefinitely.
Certain expensive drinks will not give you the option to share a drink.
Version 1.3.3 of the Unofficial Skyrim Patch partially fixes this bug.
Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the thane quest for the quest giver's hold.
Because this quest is unmarked, completing it won't help with progress towards the "Hero of the People" Achievement.
Only drunks with the "MaleDrunk" voicetype can be quest givers for this quest.

paragraphs: If you talk to one of the quest givers, they will have one or more dialogue options to sell them crops — one for each sellable crop that you currently have in your inventory. Each quest giver accepts specific crops that are grown on that farm, as listed in the above table. Several crops besides wheat are included in the quest. The "quest" consists of selecting one of the dialogue options, thus selling crops to the farmer.

The implication is that you are being paid for harvesting crops from the farm, but in reality gathering or harvesting the crops is irrelevant. The farmers will accept vegetables from any source — those on the farm that they had previously harvested, ones that you found deep in an ancient tomb, ones that you pickpocketed from the farmer, or ones that you stole from the farm's kitchen table. In short, "Sell Vegetables" would be a more appropriate title than "Gather Wheat".
There are several key differences between selling crops to farmers for this quest and selling crops to normal merchants:

Farmers always take all samples of the specified crop that are in your inventory. If you want to sell only a portion of your crops, store that portion elsewhere before talking to the farmer, then pick it back up when you're done.
Farmers will purchase any stolen samples.
The amount purchased is not limited by the farmer's available gold.

The farmers always pay you the base value of the crops, regardless of your Speech skill and perks. This is the only way for low-level characters to receive money for various vegetables that cost 1 gold.
You never gain any Speech experience for the sale.
After harvesting, crops will regrow when the farm respawns after ten days.

The reward for completing this "quest" is however much money you earn for the sale of your collected vegetables. This is not leveled, as it is the base value of the crops that is being used. Thus, your "reward" depends upon number of crops and the type of crop sold.

notes: This quest does not have any stages or objectives.
This quest can be repeated indefinitely.
You cannot sell crops to either resident of Loreius Farm, despite them also being farmers.

Money you earn from gathering crops is fixed and is not affected by your Speech skill. This makes the quest one of the few ways to make money without increasing any skills, which will help control your level. This is useful when wanting to train in a certain skill as many times as possible. It is also one of the few ways to earn money without doing any questing, merchanting, or crafting.
Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the thane quest for the quest giver's hold.
There is no one in the game that will buy carrots, green and red apples, and tomatoes, most likely because they don't exist as an actual plant (such as potatoes) in the game world in the base game.

In the Hearthfire add-on, you can plant and grow wheat, cabbage, potatoes, leeks, gourds, and carrots in a greenhouse or garden of your player-built property, and you can sell the wheat, cabbage, potatoes, leeks, and gourds to the people listed above. Unfortunately, there still is no one who will buy carrots off of you, and you also cannot plant nirnroot.
Selling wheat to Tulvur at Hollyfrost Farm allows you to take low-value items freely from the House of Clan Cruel-Sea.
Selling crops to Katla will allow you to ride the horses at Solitude Stables for free, due to her being in the same ownership faction as the stablemaster.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.1.2, addresses this issue. This has been adjusted to set ownership correctly.

paragraphs: If you talk to one of the quest givers, they will offer to pay you for any ore you mine. Each quest-giver will only accept a single type of ore, as listed in the above table. You can also mine ore without talking to a quest giver, and either sell them the ore later or use the ore yourself (e.g., by smelting it). For most ores you are paid its standard base value, with the exception of Iron Ore, for which you receive 7 gold instead of 2 gold. The amount you are paid is fixed, and does not depend upon your Speech skill or perks. All ore of the specified type will be purchased.
Information on how and where to mine is provided at Mining.

walkthrough.heading: Achievements
paragraphs: An Achievement is related to mining ore:
Hard Worker (10 points/Bronze) — Chop wood, mine ore, and cook food
To obtain this achievement you do not need to sell the ore, or even talk to any of the quest givers. Simply activating an ore vein is sufficient.

notes: This quest does not have any stages or objectives.
This quest can be repeated indefinitely.
The dialogue option to sell the ore only appears if you have the specified type of ore in your inventory.
The quest giver will buy all the ore of the specified type that you are carrying, so if you want to save any, you must remove it from your inventory first.

Money you earn from mining ore is fixed, and if the ore is sold through direct dialogue rather than the merchant screen, is not affected by your Speech skill. This makes the quest one of the few ways to make money without increasing any skills, which will help control your level. This is useful when wanting to train in a certain skill as many times as possible. It is also one of the few ways to earn money without doing any questing, merchanting, or crafting.
Completing this quest at Redbelly Mine will raise your favor with the owner, Grogmar, and he will make you blood-kin to the Orcs as a result.
Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the thane quest for the quest giver's hold.

quick: Approach an Orc stronghold.
Speak with a member of the stronghold.
Speak with a guard in the stronghold, if not the same person as the previous step.
Retrieve the Forgemaster's Fingers.
Return the Forgemaster's Fingers to the chief of that stronghold.

paragraphs: When you first approach any Orc stronghold, a guard may stop you and tell you that the stronghold is exclusively for Orcs and that no outsiders will be permitted inside. As the other Orcs in the stronghold will tell you that you are not welcome, you must find an Orc guard in order to trigger the quest. If you ask the guard how they can be persuaded to grant you access, they will tell you to reclaim an item: the Forgemaster's Fingers. This item, which grants the wielder a +12 bonus to Smithing, can be retrieved from a randomly determined location.
When you return and give the Forgemaster's Fingers to the chief, you will be permitted to enter all strongholds and will be named Blood-Kin of the Orcs.

walkthrough.heading: Radiant Options
paragraphs: This is a radiant quest that you can receive from an Orc living in any Orc stronghold except Largashbur. You will be asked to bring the item back to that stronghold's chief. The location of the quest item is randomly determined based upon the quest-giver's hold (see table below for specific options).

stages.text: Objective 10: Find the Forgemaster's Fingers
Objective 20: Bring the Forgemaster's Fingers to <Alias.ShortName=Chief>

notes: This quest's main purpose is to provide the Blood-Kin trait to players who don't already have it. As such, the quest generally can't be obtained by Orc players, or by players who have already become Blood-Kin through other quests.
If this quest is active, other quests with grateful Orcs will not name you Blood-Kin as part of the reward.

This quest cannot be unlocked in Largashbur due to that stronghold's unique quest, The Cursed Tribe, taking priority. Completing the Cursed Tribe quest will also make you Blood-Kin, although this is not explicitly mentioned at any point during the quest itself.

After completion of this quest, the Forgemaster's Fingers will not remain with the chief you gave them to, but instead will be placed into the inventory of the Orc who first gave you the quest, from whom you can pickpocket them back.
The quest may fail to activate after agreeing to do the favor.

Adding the gloves to your inventory via the console, then offering to do the quest again, may properly trigger the quest log entry. You can then remove the gloves via console and continue the quest as normal.
After you go to one stronghold and try to accept the quest, go to another stronghold and try to accept the quest again.
Enter the stronghold you're at and speak to the Orc that tried to give you the quest again. The option to ask how to enter should still be there.
Saving the game, restarting Skyrim, then repeating the dialogue may also fix the quest trigger.
Fast-traveling after speaking to the quest-giver may also cause the quest to trigger.
Completing the quest may cause the Blood-Kin topic to become active even though that should not happen and makes no logical sense.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.4, fixes this bug.
Sometimes an Orc guard will not give out the quest when speaking to them.

Favor quests in The Rift do not provide progress towards becoming Thane of the Rift, as that task uses a counter based on completion of miscellaneous objectives in Riften instead. This includes those that are not Favors, and does not include objectives outside of Riften itself.
Only one type of these Favor quests can be active at a time:
A Few Words with You: Do a favor by talking to someone about a problem. (radiant)
Delivery: Deliver an item to an associate. (radiant)
Dungeon Delving (Bandits): Do a favor by retrieving an item from a bandit hideout. (radiant)
Dungeon Delving (Caves): Do a favor by retrieving an item from a cave. (radiant)
Kill the Bandit Leader: Do a favor by slaying a bandit leader. (radiant)
Rare Gifts: Do a favor by finding a rare item. (radiant)
Some Light Theft: Do a favor by stealing an item. (radiant)

quick: Speak to Bralsa Drel.
Convince Geldis Sadri to let Bralsa drink again.
Tell Bralsa the good news.

walkthrough.heading: Bad For Business
paragraphs: Once you have freed the Raven Rock citizens from Miraak's spell as part of the quest Cleansing the Stones you will be able to talk to a former miner named Bralsa Drel. She lives in the abandoned building and can be found browsing the market every day between 8am and 8pm. She has fallen on hard times since Raven Rock Mine closed and has spent all of her fortune made in the mine on drinking Sujamma and abusing Skooma. When you get near her, she will remark: "Don't pity me. And don't look at me like that. I know what I am." You can then ask her why you should pity her and she will explain: "Doesn't everyone pity the hopeless? Look at me... I'm no better than a beggar." She then proceeds to explain that she drank her entire fortune away at The Retching Netch, or that she used to. When asked what happened she will explain: "That fetcher Geldis won't even allow me inside. Said I was bad for business. If I want to spend my last bag of coins getting drunk, that's my business. What does he care?"

walkthrough.heading: The Concerned Innkeeper
paragraphs: Enter the Retching Netch, locate innkeeper Geldis Sadri and ask him why Bralsa was banned from drinking at his inn. His explanation will reveal that he did it out of concern: "Have you seen the poor girl? She's a mess. She used to be richer than Councilor Morvayn and she's spending it all drowning her sorrow. As much as I love making coin, I can't watch her do that anymore. I won't."
You can then choose between three options. You will need a Speech skill level of at least 50 to persuade him.

walkthrough.heading: Back to the Drink
paragraphs: Once you have convinced the concerned innkeeper to let Bralsa drink again, return to her and tell her the great news. She will be quite sarcastic in her response: "Well then, I suppose I'm off to do what I do best. Here. This was something I carried around in happier times. Maybe you can find a use for it." She will then hand you an enchanted weapon of the best possible quality as a reward. After that, Bralsa can be found at the Retching Netch every day between 6pm and 10pm, doing what she does best.

quick: Talk to Urag gro-Shub.
Retrieve the requested book.
Return to Urag gro-Shub.

walkthrough.heading: The Arcanaeum
paragraphs: After joining the College of Winterhold, you will find an opportunity to visit the Arcanaeum. Here you will meet the master archivist, Urag gro-Shub. He is very solicitous of his books, threatening bodily harm should any problems arise under his watch. After his blustering, ask Urag if there is any College business you can help with. If you assure him you are feeling adventurous, he will name a book title he would like to procure from a more "dangerous" location.

walkthrough.heading: Reading List
paragraphs: The book that you are asked to find is randomly selected from the following list:
Arcana Restored
Brothers of Darkness
Children of the Sky
Chimarvamidium
Chronicles of Nchuleft
Cleansing of the Fane
Fragment: On Artaeum
Glories and Laments
Hanging Gardens
Invocation of Azura
Last King of the Ayleids — (NOT the similarly named The Last King of the Ayleids, even though the text is identical.)
The Legendary Scourge
Souls, Black and White
N'Gasta! Kvata! Kvakis!
The Old Ways
Remanada
War of the First Council
The Waters of Oblivion
The Wild Elves
The Wolf Queen, v6
The book will be located in the boss-level chest of any dungeon in the game, and as this is a radiant quest, your destination is randomly selected from over one hundred forty possible dungeons.

walkthrough.heading: A Means to an End
paragraphs: The book you are asked to find is never a skill book, and the monetary reward you get from Urag for returning a book is very small in proportion to the amount of work required to fetch it. However, this quest is a useful means for locating dungeons in Skyrim. The various loot you find in the dungeons will be considerably more valuable than the book.

Objective 20: Return the book to Urag gro-Shub
Objective 10: Find the copy of <Alias=Book>
Objective 20: Return the book to Urag gro-Shub

notes: If Dragonborn is installed, some radiant locations may be on Solstheim. If you are in Skyrim, you will not receive a quest marker pointing you to the quest location, but must travel to Solstheim first (at which point any quest markers you have to quests in Skyrim will disappear).

The two different quest IDs correspond to two nearly identical quests. In particular, the lists of possible books and lists of possible dungeons are the same for both quests. The only difference is Urag's dialogue throughout the quest.

If you find the book before activating the quest, you will be stuck with it. The quest will point to the chest, and the book won't be there, and can't be returned. Once this has happened, you will be stuck with any additional copies you pick up as well, even if you activate the quest before getting a second copy.
The Official Skyrim Patch, version 1.9, fixes this bug.
Use player.drop "book ID" "quantity" to drop and retake the book to complete the quest.
Alternatively use console player.additem 72841 1 to add quest version of that book to inventory. Then use setstage MGR20 20 to finish that stage of quest.
If there is no quest marker pointing you to the book's location, the book may be located in The Katariah, in which case the book cannot be reached until the quest Hail Sithis! begins.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2, fixes this bug.
The quest marker may point to the Thalmor Embassy instead of Shadowgreen Cavern, which is right next door.

If you find the book before activating the quest, the quest will point you to Urag gro-Shub saying "Return the book to Urag gro-Shub" (if you have installed the unofficial patches) but Urag gro-Shub will not provide new dialogue thus making it impossible to complete the quest.
Use setstage MGR20 200 to finish the quest. (use this if setstage MGR20 20 doesn't work). Use "MGR20B" if "MGR20" doesn't work.
Complete find book of azura SetObjectiveCompleted MGR20B 10 1
Urag may not give you a note on the book's title and location, even though he claims you'll get one. Your journal will still be updated, though, and the quest will proceed as normal.

quick: Speak to Milore Ienth.
Obtain five samples of netch jelly.
Return to Milore Ienth for your reward.

walkthrough.heading: Hunt for Jelly
paragraphs: The residing apothecary and Alchemy trainer in Raven Rock, Milore Ienth, sells a wide variety of exotic ingredients, all of which she grows and harvests herself. However, due to the harsh terrain and the dangers outside the Bulwark, she has problems gathering netch jelly. Tell her you are willing to help and she will immediately promise you a reward if you bring back five samples.

The netch jelly samples are dropped by the peaceful, but potentially dangerous, netch that can be found all over Solstheim. If you have started (or completed) the quest The Final Descent you can gather the only two harvested samples of jelly in Solstheim, specifically deep within Raven Rock Mine, on an alchemy lab. However, you will either need to visit an apothecary or go netch-hunting for the rest of the samples. The table below shows all fixed locations of the netch, which often reside in familial groups:

Once you have gathered five samples of netch jelly, return to Milore and hand them over. She will be impressed and say, "Goodness, it must have been quite difficult tracking those creatures down out there. Here, take these. They should help you during your journeys." She will then hand you two Potions of Ultimate Well-Being, ending the quest.

notes: If you already have five samples of netch jelly in your inventory when starting the quest, Milore will say, "My goodness, you're quite resourceful aren't you? This is all I can offer in return for this. I hope it's enough." This ends the quest right away.

quick: Speak to Ingun Black-Briar.
Gather 20 Deathbells, 20 Nirnroot and 20 Nightshade.
Return them to Ingun.

walkthrough.heading: The Black Sheep
paragraphs: Ingun Black-Briar has fallen far from the Black-Briar tree. Instead of learning the family business with her brother, Sibbi, she can be found devising alchemical recipes in Elgrim's Elixirs. The quality of her experiments seem to indicate a dark nature in this well-to-do girl, as she will allude to when speaking to her. Indeed, the ingredients she has depleted from Elgrim's stores are used to make some very powerful poisons.

walkthrough.heading: Helping Out
paragraphs: Whether you speak to Ingun in Elgrim's Elixirs or find her walking through Riften, rouse her from her musings and ask her if she is an alchemist. She will reply: "I'm aspiring to earn that title, yes. However, the road ahead is paved with loose cobbles and deadly pitfalls. Master Elgrim says I'm a natural; that I have a unique talent. But I fear his approval masks his intolerance for my mistakes. My errant formulas have cost Master Elgrim a fortune in ingredients; some of which are almost irreplaceable."

You are a helpful sort, so ask: "What sort of ingredients do you need?" Ingun will tell you: "To restore Master Elgrim's supply I would need 20 deathbell, 20 nightshade and 20 nirnroot. Am I sensing that you may be interested in gathering these rare ingredients for me?" Answer in the affirmative. Ingun will be pleased: "That means more time for my experiments and less time in the field. Much appreciated."

walkthrough.heading: Notable Harvest Locations
paragraphs: Ingun needs you to hunt down 20 Deathbells, 20 Nirnroot, and 20 Nightshade.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: Ingun will reward you with leveled amount of gold (listed in the table below) for each set of ingredients brought to her.

After you have delivered and been paid for all three samples, it will behoove you to see what else you can procure from her. Hint to her: "That was the last of the ingredients." To which she will reply: "Yes, Master Elgrim will be pleased I've restored his stock of these rare ingredients. I feel I owe a bit more than some meaningless coin for all your diligence. Here, this key unlocks my supply chest at Elgrim's Elixirs. Feel free to take what you need from time to time. I'll be refilling it once every few days or so." The chest is found in the back of Elgrim's Elixirs, and she will restock it with 2 - 5 random leveled potions every few days. She will also remind you of this each time you exit conversation with her as she will say: "Don't forget to check to check your supply chest from time to time." The chest will require the key Ingun gave you each time it resets.

notes: It is possible to give the items to Ingun Black-Briar then quickly exit out of the conversation and enter the item menu then drop the items. The quest log will show "Find 20 <item name> for Ingun Black-Briar (0/20)". However as soon as Ingun is told "That was the last of the ingredients" the quest will update accordingly.

You can use this quest to earn the Hero of the People achievement quickly as every time you update your personal inventory from fewer than 20 to greater than or equal to 20 of any of the three ingredients, you will receive a quest objective update. You can therefore remain in a container menu and repeatedly shift these items back and forth in order to quickly unlock said achievement.

quick: Talk to Grosta about her missing husband.
Locate Leifnarr in Broken Helm Hollow.
Return to Grosta for your reward.

walkthrough.heading: The Angry Wife
paragraphs: Heartwood Mill, a remote lumber mill located where Lake Honrich turns into Treva River, seems less busy than other mills with only Grosta working the mill and her son Gralnach fooling around on and off the road. If you talk to Gralnach, he will explain his father disappeared without a trace and left him and his mother alone with a mill to run. Talking to Grosta will reveal her suspicion that Leifnarr ran off with another woman and that she can't run the mill by herself. She then explains how Leifnarr left to trade wood and grain with some merchants near the Morrowind border, specifically a place called Broken Helm Hollow, and will mark the place on your map.

walkthrough.heading: Merchants from Morrowind
paragraphs: When you arrive at Broken Helm Hollow, it quickly becomes evident that Leifnarr was set up, as two leveled bandits will guard the cave entrance. Dispose of them both and head inside then proceed down the narrow tunnel and into the main area of the dungeon. There, you will encounter two more leveled bandits around the fire, as well as the bandit chief who resides up the southeastern slope. The boss chest is unlocked, but beware the corresponding swinging mace trap. Locate and read the Two-handed skill book Battle Of Sancre Tor, then find the pull chain straight south from the first set of bedrolls. Pull the chain and watch the rock wall disappear. Inside lies the dead body of Grosta's husband with an arrow through his chest. The room also consists of several severed limbs and blood spatters, along with a random spell tome and a weapons rack with lower level equipment. Activate the body to get the quest update, then leave the cave.

walkthrough.heading: The Grieving Widow
paragraphs: Once you travel back to Heartwood Mill, you will have no choice but to tell Grosta she is now a widow, which will make her regret her suspicions about Leifnarr being unfaithful to her.

For bringing her closure at last, Grosta will reward you with a leveled enchanted weapon, and her thanks. As a result of her friendship, you are now allowed to take the limited supplies from her house without penalty. You may also cut lumber freely at her mill for your player-built house, if you have Hearthfire installed.

stages.text: Objective 5: Report Leifnarr's death to his family
Objective 10: Find Leifnarr
Objective 20: Return to Grosta

notes: Although she expresses sorrow when you tell her of her husband's death, Grosta's ordinary dialogue does not change and she continues to say that all men are pigs after this quest has been completed.
Leifnarr's body is unnamed, identified only by the generic title of "Nord".
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.0, fixes this bug.

There are two ways to begin this quest, and one of them breaks the quest. If you talk to Grosta and agree to help find her husband Leifnarr, the quest will activate stage 10 and then stage 20 once you find his corpse, allowing successful completion of the quest. But if you find the corpse first without talking to Grosta, the quest will activate stage 15, "Report Leifnarr's Death to his family", but no dialogue option will be added to Grosta to allow you to do so and there will be no map marker to tell you where to find her. There are a few workarounds:
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.0, fixes this bug.
Enter SetStage FreeformHeartwoodMill 20 into the console. This will set quest stage to "Find Leifnarr" and allow you to reactivate Leifnarr's corpse. You may then complete the quest normally.
Enter CompleteAllObjectives FreeformHeartwoodMill into the console. This forces the quest to be completed.
Killing Grosta will fail the quest and thus remove it from your journal.
If Leifnarr's body is activated after completing the quest, the quest will restart in the breaking way shown above with stages 10 and 15 set to one and the other stages set to zero.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.0, fixes this bug.

Absent the patch, the quest can be completed repeatedly by forcing the stages 20 and 30 to completion using console commands. (SetStage FreeformHeartwoodMill 20 and SetStage FreeformHeartwoodMill 30) The player will be rewarded each time with a weapon having a random enchantment.

quick: Speak to the quest giver.
Challenge them to a brawl.
Win the brawl.
Speak to them again.

paragraphs: If you talk to one of the quest givers they will eventually challenge you to a brawl. The dialogue and circumstances vary from person to person and are listed in the table above. Accepting the challenge means that you place a 100 gold bet on the outcome. You must then brawl them and win. Standard brawling rules apply and use of things such as hostile magic, shouts, and weapons will instantly change it from a brawl to a criminal assault.

Brawling should be relatively easy if you're wearing any armor and have gained at least a few levels. Only low level players on higher difficulties may have issues with winning a brawl. If you are having problems, use some potions and spells with lingering effects and don't forget about racial powers. It may be of use as well to read more in-depth information on unarmed combat. You do not gain any experience from the unarmed combat during a brawl, although you may gain experience in armor skills.

You can only win a brawl with any given person once. If you lose the brawl, you will not get your wagered money back, although you will be able to get a rematch. If you win the brawl, you will get your wager back and receive an additional 100 gold.

notes: There are other quests that simply involve brawling such as Bloody Nose that are in fact separate from this quest, despite being nearly identical in nature.
If you have less than 100 gold when asking for a bet, the combatant may say things like "Come back when you actually have 100 gold."
When you win your wager back and receive an additional 100 gold, a "Gold (200) Added" message will appear on the top left of the screen.
When you engage in a brawl, spectators may say things like these:
"Twelve septims on the big one!"
"Fight! Fight!"
"Drive that snowback to the ground. Come on!"
"You just going to stand there and take it? Fight back."
"Who taught you to fight? Keep those hands up!"

When you engage in a brawl, viewing NPCs become immersed and tend to run around the fight. This can be quite annoying, as they can potentially run between you and your combatant which can lead you to accidentally punching one of the excited onlookers, which counts as an assault. Also, if you run away from the fight and exit through any doors, the first four NPCs who witness your fight will keep following you and will still think you are in a brawl until you fast travel.
Certain considerations apply to the brawl itself:

Although your opponent may say "No magic," you can in fact use magic on yourself, such as armor, healing, or ward spells. However, using spells on your opponent, even beneficial healing spells, will count as assault.
Wearing the Ebony Mail or using a cloaking spell will also count as assault. However, wearing Ahzidal's Armor of Retribution does not.
You can use a shield bash to "punch" your opponent.

Winning the brawl will raise the disposition of the challenger. This will allow you to take low-value items they own, and they may become available as followers or potential marriage partners. See the individual NPC pages for details.

Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the thane quest for the quest giver's hold (with the exception of quest givers who live in Orc strongholds).

Only one radiant quest of a similar type can be assigned at any given time. However, the dialogue to start the brawl is part of the quest, and the quest starts silently when you approach a location containing a quest giver. If two quest givers are near each other (e.g., Cosnach and Chief Burguk), the quest may start for one and block the dialogue to brawl with the other. Besides winning the brawl, the quest will also silently stop after some time away from the location.

Sometimes your opponent may draw their weapon and attack you like in a normal fight. In this case, your only options are to yield or kill them (except Rolff, who is essential), and it is unlikely you will be able to properly complete the quest even if you try again.
Having the Fists of Steel perk may cause your opponent to remain in bleedout mode after you win the fight. Unequipping your Heavy Armor gauntlets will resolve this.
Engaging in a brawl for this quest can cause the Gray Cowl of Nocturnal to permanently lose its ability to detect life and trigger guard hostility.
Engaging in brawls for this quest while wearing the Ebony Mail can inflict the armor's poison damage effect on your opponent, leading to assault bounties.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2.4, fixes this bug.

paragraphs: Talk to Wulf Wild-Blood in Skaal Village. He will ask you to find his brother, Torkild. Torkild will appear randomly while wandering Solstheim. While speaking with him, he will turn into a werebear and you will be forced to kill him. Afterward, search his body and take the letter to Wulf from him.
Return to Wulf Wild-Blood in Skaal Village and give him the letter. He will thank you, and give you a one point skill boost to several combat skills: Archery, Block, Heavy Armor, and One-handed.

notes: Sometimes target ref id is not properly registered so you can't find him anywhere and even movetoqt command returns with no active target. To fix this issue and for Map Marker to show up, just type in the console: setstage DLC2WB01 15

If you cannot find Torkild, there are eight places where he can appear. The one near Glacial Cave is probably the best choice, since the spawn point is close to the cave and you can fast travel there every so often and re-check.
One possible circuit to check all eight places:
While the quest At the Summit of Apocrypha is active, you cannot give the letter to Wulf.
If you enter werewolf form to fight Torkild and choose to feed on him, you may temporarily be unable to search him. If you wait or fast travel elsewhere, you should be able to obtain the letter.

It is possible Torkild will already be dead upon finding him (e.g. something else killed him before you were able to talk to him). This should not cause any problems with the quest, as you can still take the letter off his body. When talking with Wulf afterward the dialogue will still be about him turning into a werebear and you having to kill him.
The Unofficial Dragonborn Patch, version 1.0.5, fixes this bug.
The letter to Wulf may be removed from your inventory prematurely. This will not affect the quest.

notes: It seems that at one point, Gisli was considered as a steward for Solitude, this may explain her inclusion as one of the possible "friends" who are almost always found at the Blue Palace.

Script notes indicate that Erikur would've been aware that it was you who assassinated Elisif. How he would be aware of this is never specified.

quick: Speak to Madesi in his stall in Riften.
Gather one mammoth tusk, one gold ore, and two flawless sapphires.
Return to Madesi.

paragraphs: Speak with Madesi and ask him about his jewelry. You will learn that he is running low on supplies due to heavy bandit presence on the roads and needs help gathering some components. He requires two flawless sapphires, one mammoth tusk, and one piece of gold ore.
Flawless sapphires, like all gems, can be randomly found or mined. One guaranteed sample can be stolen from the shelves in the Inner Sanctum of the Temple of Dibella in Markarth.

Mammoth tusks can be looted from slain mammoths, as well as bought from hunters and certain merchants. Three guaranteed samples can be found in the College of Winterhold's Arcanaeum; eight guaranteed samples can be found in Halted Stream Camp. The closest one is in Black-Briar Meadery, where it can be stolen from the shelves of a cupboard in Indaryn's bedroom.

Gold ore can be found randomly in containers or in buildings, but an easy place to find some gold veins is in Kolskeggr Mine. There's also Lost Prospect Mine; while the latter is closer, it doesn't have as many veins as Kolskeggr Mine. Alternately, one can just use the Transmute spell to turn one Iron Ore into one Gold Ore.

You can return the items to Madesi as you find them, or all at once. He will give you 100 gold for each item returned (i.e., 200 for the two sapphires). Once you've returned them all, ask Madesi if he needs anything else and he will thank you with a leveled necklace.

notes: Completing this quest counts towards your eligibility for becoming Thane of the Rift.

On a purely money-making basis, this quest is a financial loss. Even at the lowest speech level, you can sell flawless sapphires (including to Madesi himself) for more then the quest reward of 100 per sapphire. At higher speech levels, you can sell a mammoth tusk for more than 100 gold. Purchasing the items for this quest will make the money loss even worse.
Madesi will accept stolen goods in fulfillment of this quest, which may be useful if you are trying to avoid dealing with fences or spending a perk point on the fence perk.
You cannot toggle the objective in your journal for individual items; doing so will instead toggle all 3 items at once or the remaining two if you delivered one.

Halted Stream Camp is the location of a bounty quest, possible location of a Dungeon Delving quest from Amren, and possible location of the Amulet of the Moon quest, making it easy to complete multiple quests at once if you choose to find your mammoth tusk there.
There are no quest markers for delivering the items back to Madesi.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.1, fixes this bug.
The quest may continue to prompt the objective to bring Madesi his items if the objective to do so is in your quest journal.
The Unofficial Skyrim Legendary Edition Patch, version 3.0.9, fixes this bug.

quick: Speak to Avrusa Sarethi.
Collect 20 Jazbay Grapes.
Return to Avrusa Sarethi.

paragraphs: Avrusa Sarethi needs a large amount of jazbay grapes in order to cultivate nirnroots. She's running low and unable to search out the ingredient herself, as she is preoccupied with her energetic sister and farm chores. She asks you to hunt down twenty grapes for her current nirnroot crop. As Avrusa notes, jazbay grapes are somewhat hard to come by. The plants are indigenous to the volcanic tundra region of Eastmarch, and while desolate, the tundra is fairly easy to traverse with a few lesser animals and non-hostile giants.
There are a few locations where it can be found in greater quantities than usual. Along with the quantities available, they are:
49 around Steamcrag Camp (Eastmarch)
47 around Witchmist Grove (Eastmarch)
35 around Eldergleam Sanctuary (Eastmarch)
33 around the Atronach Stone (Eastmarch)
31 around Bonestrewn Crest (Eastmarch)
26 around Kynesgrove (Eastmarch), especially along the road heading southeast
25 around Mistwatch (Eastmarch)
24 around Broken Limb Camp (Eastmarch)
23 around Cronvangr Cave (Eastmarch)

Once you have collected twenty samples, head back to Avrusa who will thank you for your aid and reward you with five random potions. You can return to Sarethi Farm periodically to harvest Nirnroot and Crimson Nirnroot.

quick: Speak to Ingun Black-Briar.
Gather 20 Deathbells, 20 Nirnroot and 20 Nightshade.
Return them to Ingun.

walkthrough.heading: The Black Sheep
paragraphs: Ingun Black-Briar has fallen far from the Black-Briar tree. Instead of learning the family business with her brother, Sibbi, she can be found devising alchemical recipes in Elgrim's Elixirs. The quality of her experiments seem to indicate a dark nature in this well-to-do girl, as she will allude to when speaking to her. Indeed, the ingredients she has depleted from Elgrim's stores are used to make some very powerful poisons.

walkthrough.heading: Helping Out
paragraphs: Whether you speak to Ingun in Elgrim's Elixirs or find her walking through Riften, rouse her from her musings and ask her if she is an alchemist. She will reply: "I'm aspiring to earn that title, yes. However, the road ahead is paved with loose cobbles and deadly pitfalls. Master Elgrim says I'm a natural; that I have a unique talent. But I fear his approval masks his intolerance for my mistakes. My errant formulas have cost Master Elgrim a fortune in ingredients; some of which are almost irreplaceable."

You are a helpful sort, so ask: "What sort of ingredients do you need?" Ingun will tell you: "To restore Master Elgrim's supply I would need 20 deathbell, 20 nightshade and 20 nirnroot. Am I sensing that you may be interested in gathering these rare ingredients for me?" Answer in the affirmative. Ingun will be pleased: "That means more time for my experiments and less time in the field. Much appreciated."

walkthrough.heading: Notable Harvest Locations
paragraphs: Ingun needs you to hunt down 20 Deathbells, 20 Nirnroot, and 20 Nightshade.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: Ingun will reward you with leveled amount of gold (listed in the table below) for each set of ingredients brought to her.

After you have delivered and been paid for all three samples, it will behoove you to see what else you can procure from her. Hint to her: "That was the last of the ingredients." To which she will reply: "Yes, Master Elgrim will be pleased I've restored his stock of these rare ingredients. I feel I owe a bit more than some meaningless coin for all your diligence. Here, this key unlocks my supply chest at Elgrim's Elixirs. Feel free to take what you need from time to time. I'll be refilling it once every few days or so." The chest is found in the back of Elgrim's Elixirs, and she will restock it with 2 - 5 random leveled potions every few days. She will also remind you of this each time you exit conversation with her as she will say: "Don't forget to check to check your supply chest from time to time." The chest will require the key Ingun gave you each time it resets.

notes: It is possible to give the items to Ingun Black-Briar then quickly exit out of the conversation and enter the item menu then drop the items. The quest log will show "Find 20 <item name> for Ingun Black-Briar (0/20)". However as soon as Ingun is told "That was the last of the ingredients" the quest will update accordingly.

You can use this quest to earn the Hero of the People achievement quickly as every time you update your personal inventory from fewer than 20 to greater than or equal to 20 of any of the three ingredients, you will receive a quest objective update. You can therefore remain in a container menu and repeatedly shift these items back and forth in order to quickly unlock said achievement.

quick: Speak to Marise Aravel.
Find five ice wraith teeth.
Return to Marise.

paragraphs: Wander around Riften and you can find Marise Aravel and her food store at the market. She will introduce her food to you with pride: "My food is the best in all of Skyrim; always as fresh as the day it was collected." If you ask her the reason for this, she will tell you she picked up a trick from a butcher in Elinhir, a small town over the border in Hammerfell. Grinding up ice wraith teeth and using it as a preservative is the key to keeping everything fresh. Then she will ask you to bring five of the teeth to her to replenish her supply. If you ask her where to find ice wraiths, she will warn you of potential danger before suggesting that you travel to Ancient's Ascent. She will also add a marker for the location to your map.

You may buy ice wraith teeth from Alchemy shops, most of which have a 21% chance of carrying 1-4 samples. Five samples can be found in the Hall of Attainment or Jorrvaskr Living Quarters and four in the White Hall. If you prefer to hunt some ice wraiths, you may be able to find them in the wilderness of Winterhold. You can find ice wraiths in the following locations, although for Forsaken Cave, the path to High Hrothgar, and Tolvald's Cave it will depend on the Dragonborn's character level whether you find ice wraiths or different creatures:
Ancient's Ascent, recommended location, actually in Bonechill Passage
Forsaken Cave, outside by the entrance and in the natural cave area just inside
The Midden, down the steps, past the skeleton sunk into the floor, in the icy room (does not respawn)
Throat of the World, the path to High Hrothgar
Tolvald's Cave, outside by the entrance and in the first part of the first zone
Weynon Stones, two ice wraiths will ambush you there

Once you have the ice wraith teeth, return to Marise. She will be quite happy: "Perfect, just perfect! These should help keep my stock fresh for quite a while." She will reward you with an apprentice-level Alteration spell tome (either Magelight or Stoneflesh) and five pheasant breasts. The spell tome is selected when you give Marise the ice wraith teeth, so if you save beforehand, you can reload until you get your preference.

stages.text: (Only displayed if you don't already have the teeth) Objective 10: Find 5 Ice Wraith Teeth for Marise (<Global=FFR07TeethCount>/5)

notes: After completing this quest once, you may receive the first quest objective in your journal again. The counter does not increase upon adding ice wraith teeth to your inventory, and the objective is stuck in your quest log permanently.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2.1, fixes this bug.
Collect 10 or 15 Ice Wraith Teeth instead so that once you turn in 5, the counter maxes out at 5 again (thus successfully completing the quest).

walkthrough.heading: Amren's Family Sword
paragraphs: When you encounter Amren, he may be arguing with his wife Saffir. If asked about the argument, Amren will tell you about his father's sword:
Volunteering to retrieve the sword for him triggers the start of the quest.

When you return the sword, Amren gives you a one point bonus in both Block and One-handed, commenting, "Here, my father had a favorite sword and shield technique. Let me teach it to you, in honor of his memory."

paragraphs: If you talk to Shahvee you may have the option to ask her, "Your people have bad luck?" In response she will tell you:
Volunteering to retrieve the amulet triggers the start of the quest.

When you return the amulet, Shahvee gives you a one point bonus in both Light Armor and Lockpicking, commenting, "Before I came into Zenithar's calling, I confess I was a thief. But I learned a few things in my time that might help you survive. Let me show you."

notes: Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the thane quest for the quest giver's hold.
It is impossible to do both quests at the same time, e.g., if you do the quest for Amren, you are unable to do it for Shahvee until you have completed the quest for Amren.

Shahvee's Amulet can spawn in Uttering Hills Camp, a location that also has a chance for Annekke Crag-Jumper or Brunwulf Free-Winter's personal quests. If they do, none of these quests can be taken at the same time. Waiting 30 days outside their map cells will allow one of the other quests to be taken.
You may be unable to receive this quest from Shahvee, even if none of the other quests are active.

The quest for Amren also conflicts with the miscellaneous quest that can be obtained from the dead Treasure Hunter World Interaction. If you have this uncompleted radiant miscellaneous quest in your quest log, then you will not be able to see the dialogue option to receive Amren's quest when talking to him.

quick: Meet and talk to Anska in High Gate Ruins and agree to help her.
Protect Anska as you fight through the ruins.
Defeat Vokun.
Retrieve Anska's scroll.

walkthrough.heading: Anska
paragraphs: High Gate Ruins is a remote Nordic ruin on the snowy tundra east of Solitude, near the shores of the Sea of Ghosts. When you enter, it soon becomes clear that someone visited the ruin recently, as the residing draugr have already been killed. Proceed into the first room and you will meet the person responsible, a Nord wizard named Anska. When approached she will introduce herself and ask if you are there to help her as she has finally located Vokun's Crypt. She then explains her goal, namely to locate a special scroll that could link her family blood all the way back to the legendary Ysgramor. She will also briefly describe Vokun as "Some old priest buried here long ago.", hinting at her lack of research and explaining her need for help. She fears the old priest could awaken and prove too powerful a foe, so she wants you to lead her through the ruin and help her fight the opposition. Accept her request and the quest will start.

walkthrough.heading: High Gate Ruins
paragraphs: Anska is not your average follower and you will have to escort her safely through the ruin; she is, however, capable of taking care of herself using a variety of leveled wizard spells, so keep an eye out and stay upfront as you proceed into the dungeon. Take the northern tunnel to a huge chamber infested with leveled draugr. Claim some minor loot from the chest in the alcove, then head upstairs and locate the iron door leading north where three more draugr will attack. Go through the room with the alchemy lab and a few useful potions. The next tunnel contains a pressure plate triggering a spike wall, so make sure Anska gets through unharmed. A lever puzzle awaits in the next room, so take a thorough look at the symbols above the southern ledge. From left to right, they are: Eagle—Whale—Fox—Snake. Look around the room for the levers, all of them on pedestals with corresponding symbols. The two first levers are upstairs while the last two are on the ground floor. When all four levers are pulled in the right order, the grate in the middle of the room will disappear, so head downstairs and enter the catacombs through the door.

Only one draugr will attack you in the first section of the catacombs and a slide will lead you down to another catacomb area with more draugr. A chest can be found in an alcove, but watch out for the pressure plate and the corresponding darts. Before long, you will reach a room with a leveled soul gem resting on a weight sensitive plate, which releases two draugr from the adjacent coffins if triggered. The locked door to the right contains a chest behind it. Continue into a hallway filled with ancient carvings and numerous pressure plates on the floor, triggering darts or spear traps, then proceed into another puzzle room. Facing the lever, two stone walls cover hidden doors, so pull the lever and watch the wall to the right disappear, then fight the boss-leveled draugr guarding another lever. Pull that lever and the door to the left will open and release yet another boss-leveled draugr. Pull the lever behind him, then head through the now-opened entrance to the east and into Vokun's throne room.

walkthrough.heading: Vokun
paragraphs: Before the throne room, a hallway offers a few potions. As soon as you open the next door, the dragon priest Vokun will burst out of his sarcophagus and use his staff of fireballs to attack you from a distance. Anska will keep her distance from Vokun, but will use her ranged attacks to help out. Defeat the priest and claim his unique mask and his staff from the remains. Proceed to the chamber to the east, where you will find a word wall with a word for the Storm Call Shout. The nearby table holds the sealed scroll for Anska, so pick it up and hand it to her. She will be overwhelmed with joy and hand you the unique spell tome for learning the spell Conjure Flaming Familiar as a reward. Additionally, a boss-leveled chest can be found on the upper level to the north, in an alcove right next to the shortcut back to the first zone of the ruin. Anska will stay behind and try to decipher the scroll indefinitely.

stages.text: Find Anska's scroll and return it to her for a reward.
Help Anska retrieve the scroll from High Gate Ruins.
I have the scroll, I should return it to Anska for my reward.
High Gate Ruins is clear and Anska has rewarded me with a powerful new fire spell.
I have failed to protect Anska, now I'll never know what her scroll was for.

notes: Be careful about bringing other followers with you, since Anska's use of Destruction magic can cause them to attack her if she hits them by mistake, or if they hit her.
This quest only counts towards the Sideways achievement if Anska survives.

Should you choose not to hand over the scroll to Anska right away, she'll continue to follow you around, but only within close proximity to the ruins. In other words, she can't be used as a "free" follower. If you withhold the scroll from her and head outside, then later give her the scroll, she will return to the ruins and remain in Vokun's throne room indefinitely.

It is possible to clear the dungeon without Anska's help. To do this, avoid talking to her when you enter the dungeon. Once Vokun is dead, she will run up to you and allow for the quest to finish normally.
Anska is not considered an essential NPC, and can be killed prior to starting the quest. This prevents the start of the quest and the acquisition of the Flaming Familiar spell.
Area of effect spells such as Fire Storm or Unrelenting Force can cause objects, including the scroll, to fly around the room, potentially becoming lost.
On entering the Catacombs, Anska will comment on the soul gem well before you reach it, and before it is in your line of sight.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2, fixes this bug.
Similarly, she may comment on Vokun's presence and the scroll beyond him ("There it is! On the table!"), before the door to his throne room is even open.
You may be stuck with the sealed scroll, should you pick it up after failing the quest.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.1, fixes this bug.
Upon killing Vokun, Anska may just stand in battle pose, not finishing the quest.
This can be fixed by opening the console, targeting Anska, and using the recycleactor command. She will then vanish, re-enter the room, run toward Vokun's tomb, and you can now speak to her.
The scroll may be left in your inventory after you complete the quest (you can remove it at that stage though, since it is no longer a quest item).
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.1, fixes this bug.

Leaving the reward room without taking the scroll will lead you to be locked out of the room. Even if you return to the throne room, the gates will be locked and cannot be opened anymore since the priest is already dead.
If Anska is killed, the quest does not fail.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.3, fixes this bug.

quick: Speak to the residents of Darkwater Crossing.
Travel to Darkwater Pass.
Search the cave for Derkeethus.
Free Derkeethus from his prison.
Escort Derkeethus out of the cave.

walkthrough.heading: Darkwater Crossing
paragraphs: If you talk to the residents of Darkwater Crossing (for example Sondas Drenim, a miner in nearby Goldenrock Mine), you will soon hear of an Argonian named Derkeethus who recently went to explore the pools around Darkwater - and who hasn't been seen in a long time. The residents will not be able to say for sure where Derkeethus is, but he has actually run into trouble inside Darkwater Pass.

Locating Darkwater Pass can be difficult. The easiest route from Darkwater Crossing is to cross the bridge that spans the river to the southwest of the settlement. At the crossing, take the right path. Just before you reach the second bridge and Fort Amol, a stone marker to the left of the road will indicate a dusty path heading west up the mountainside. Follow the path as it curves sharply south, and onward through the trees along the cliff's edge. Eventually you will come to a large pool fed by three large waterfalls. Drop into the pool and turn directly around to the north - an iron door in the cliff wall in front of you leads to Darkwater Pass.

walkthrough.heading: Darkwater Pass
paragraphs: Follow the low tunnel past an unlocked chest, and you will reach a small cavern. Watch out - a Falmer will drop out of a Falmer hive in the wall immediately to your right as you enter. Follow the path up into a larger cavern. A Falmer waits immediately ahead outside a tent, and yet another may drop from a hive above and to the left. In the north wall is an opening into a pillared chamber where three chaurus reside. Head past this chamber and up the stairs to reach a small room with a trap door in the center. Look down through the bars to see Derkeethus pacing about in his cell below. Be mindful of the Falmer in the adjoining room with an arcane enchanter (step in here and two more Falmer will drop from the hives up near the ceiling).

Northeast from the center of the trap door, there is a lever on the wall. Pulling this lever lowers a section of wall, revealing a spiral staircase heading down. A corridor in the west wall leads south to a small circular room called Darkwater Pit. As soon as you approach, Derkeethus will engage you in conversation and ask you to help him escape. The Darkwater Pit Key is in the left Burial Urn just inside the gate, but the gate is the standard barred prison cell door with sufficient gaps to allow you to reach through and take the key from the burial urn. If he has lockpicks in his inventory, Derkeethus may have already escaped his cell and be waiting somewhere in the corridor. If this has happened, it may alert the Falmer in the arcane enchanter room.

Although there is still more of Darkwater Pass to explore, the easiest way to get Derkeethus out is to head straight back the way you came - particularly as he will not crouch into a sneaking stance when you do during this quest, and there are some nasty traps and Falmer further up the cave.
Once you have led Derkeethus to safety, he will thank you for saving him. You can now recruit him as a follower if you wish. If not, you can recruit him at any time from Darkwater Crossing.

stages.text: One of the fisherman from Darkwater Crossing has gone missing, allegedly kidnapped by a group of Falmer nearby. Objective 10: Find Derkeethus.
Objective 20: Get Derkeethus out of the cave.
I rescued Derkeethus from the Falmer of Darkwater Pass, and he's returned to his home in Darkwater Crossing.

notes: Derkeethus will only continue to follow you if you remain close to him. If you move too far away he will turn around and return to the pit he started in.

On rare occasions Derkeethus may appear on the trail between the upper and lower entrances to Darkwater Pass, begging for help escaping the cave. Just lead him to the lower entrance. He will thank you and promptly vanish. He may then be found at Darkwater Crossing.
This quest can sometimes clash with a Companions quest where an NPC needs to be rescued, potentially giving you two temporary followers.
Residents may only talk about Derkeethus going missing and give no quest or objectives. Locating his cage in Darkwater Pass should bring you to quest stage 20.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.1, fixes this bug. (details)
Derkeethus may not follow you once freed from his prison. Attempt normal resolutions - waiting, talking, leaving and returning, or reloading the game.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.1, fixes this bug. (details)

quick: Talk to Inge Six Fingers.
Locate Finn's Lute in Stony Creek Cave.
Return for your reward of a 1-point increase to all Stealth skills.

walkthrough.heading: A Unique Lute
paragraphs: Right after the Burning of King Olaf ends the quest Tending the Flames, talking to the otherwise authoritarian Inge Six Fingers will be somewhat wistful. When asked, she will tell you that a year ago, thieves broke into the College and stole her most precious item: the very first eight course lute ever created, namely Finn's Lute. As the Dean of Lute, Inge has been devastated ever since, but recently learned the location of the thieves, specifically Stony Creek Cave, a cave in southeastern Eastmarch.

walkthrough.heading: Stony Creek Cave
paragraphs: A small pond hides the entrance to the cave, complete with a dock and a boat. Upon entering, the sight of a waterfall and a dead Breton hanging from a tree trunk hints at things to come. Follow the only available path upstream and fight the expected bandits trying to protect their treasure. When the path splits in two, head right and beware of the swinging mace trap right before the chamber with the bandit leader. Pick the fight and search the body for Treasure Map X, then look around the area for interesting items, including a copy of the Illusion skill book Mystery of Talara, Part 4, an unusual gem, along with a few ingredients and an alchemy lab. Finally, open the chest and claim the lute and some valuable loot.

walkthrough.heading: An Unexpected Lesson
paragraphs: Before exiting the cave, it is possible to investigate the rest of the cave which will net you another fight against a bandit, along with a locked treasure chest, two moonstone veins and a waterfall hiding a shortcut from Kagrenzel. Exit the mine the way you came and return to the Bards College. Back at the College, Inge Six Fingers will be overwhelmed with joy. As she is unable to pay what the lute is worth, she will instead teach you a few tricks she has picked up over the years, and raise each of your Stealth skills by one point. This includes Alchemy, Light Armor, Lockpicking, Pickpocket, Sneak, and Speech.

stages.text: Thieves stolen [sic] Finn's Lute from the Bards College over a year ago. Inge Six-Fingers has asked me to recover the lute from their stronghold. Objective 20: Find Finn's Lute
Objective 40: Give Finn's Lute to Inge

notes: After you turn in the quest, the lute will remain in your inventory, still marked as a quest item.
The Official Skyrim Patch, version 1.4, fixes this bug.
You can remove the quest item using the Console and the following console code: Player.removeitem 000DABAB 1
Finding the lute before the quest is assigned may result in the lute being stuck your inventory as a quest item even after finding Inge Six Fingers and telling her you have found it.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2.1, fixes this bug.
Finding the lute early may also result the quest objective becoming stuck in your journal, even after returning the lute and receiving your reward.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2.1, fixes this bug.

To resolve this, click on the "I've found Finn's Lute" option in dialogue when you speak to Inge, rather than the "Why are you sad?" option. It works out just as if you had accepted the quest and then found it.
Alternatively, you can use the console code setstage BardsCollegeLute 40 after accepting the quest, which will update it to telling you to give Inge the lute, allowing the quest to proceed as normal.

quick: Obtain quest from Korir, the Jarl of Winterhold.
Journey to the target location.
Retrieve the Helm of Winterhold.
Return to Korir with the helm.

paragraphs: When asking the Jarl of Winterhold, Korir, for work, you may be asked to find the missing Helm of Winterhold, which was worn by Jarl Hanse in the First Era:

Once you've agreed to find it, head to the location marked on your map, and head to the boss chest, where you will find the helm. The location will be randomly selected from the following: Driftshade Refuge, Fort Fellhammer, Hela's Folly, Hob's Fall Cave, Ironbind Barrow, Pride of Tel Vos, Saarthal, Snow Veil Sanctum, Yngol Barrow, Yngvild.
After you have retrieved the helm, return to Korir to receive your reward.

stages.text: Objective 10: Find Helm of Winterhold inside <Alias=Dungeon>
Objective 15: Return Helm of Winterhold to Korir

notes: The journal entry for Driftshade Refuge is listed as Driftshade Sanctuary.

If the location of the helm is at Hela's Folly, you will need to steal the helm from a locked chest. If you are caught by Deekus, he will take everything you stole from the chest except the helm. If arrested by a guard, they will also not take the helm, as its status as a quest item supersedes its stolen status.

You cannot get this quest if Korir is not Jarl of Winterhold. Fortunately, it is only a prerequisite for becoming Thane while Korir is Jarl: if he is replaced, his replacement Kraldar will give you the title without completing this quest or any other.

The helm can be pickpocketed back off Korir if you are skilled enough. It will no longer be a quest item, but appears to retain its Stolen status even if sold to a Thieves Guild fence and repurchased (at least, this was the case with Mallus Maccius in Skyrim Special Edition).

Unlike many "named" objects, there is nothing much special about the Helm of Winterhold. Once it stops being a quest item, it has the exact same properties and sale price as an unenchanted Steel Helmet.

As of the latest version of Skyrim Special Edition, this also means it can be tempered with a Steel Ingot and the Steel Smithing perk. It can even be enchanted. The latter is not possible while it is still a quest item.
If this quest sends you to Yngol Barrow, it breaks the associated quest, causing Yngol's Shade, the Helm of Yngol, and the skeleton it rests upon not to appear as intended.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.4, fixes this bug.
This quest commonly conflicts with Purity of Revenge, causing one or the other to be unable to start until the other is completed.
The Official Skyrim Patch, version 1.9, fixes this bug.
The quest may, through unknown conditions, become repeatable: pointing you to different locations every time it is given.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2.6, fixes this bug.

If you have initiated this quest but subsequently went on to finish the Reunification of Skyrim questline for the Imperial Legion - or if Winterhold changes hands during Season Unending in the Main Quest line - Korir will be replaced as the jarl and be relocated to Brunwulf Free-Winter's house in Windhelm. If you try to give him the helm after Brunwulf becomes Jarl of Windhelm, he is continuously locked up in the house, and picking the lock will only result in him telling you you're trespassing. There is no way to finish the quest and you are stuck with the helm in your inventory, as it cannot be dropped since it's a quest item.

The quest can be completed by attacking and luring Korir outside, calming him, and then speaking with him before he heads back inside. This will incur a bounty. Trying to engage him in conversation just as you are leaving will also lead to him following you outside.

Alternatively, open up the console, click on the jarl and then type Addtofaction 0005A1​A4 1 into the box. This adds an NPC to the player ally faction, which will make a normally hostile NPC be non-hostile. This should allow you to complete the quest.
You can also finish the quest by typing setstage Favor158 20. This will also remove the helm from your inventory.
Jarl Korir may not give a dialogue option to start this quest.
Some reports suggest that the quest is flagged as completed as soon as one gains access to the College.
This quest can only be started the first time you visit Winterhold, if you fast travel away before initiating the quest then you won't be able to start it.
Starting the quest via console does not work. You can bypass this quest and still become Thane of Winterhold on PC with player.setrelationshiprank 1c1b5 2.

notes: The journal entry for Driftshade Refuge is listed as Driftshade Sanctuary.

You cannot get this quest if Korir is not Jarl of Winterhold. Fortunately, it is only a prerequisite for becoming Thane while Korir is Jarl: if he is replaced, his replacement Kraldar will give you the title without completing this quest or any other.

If this quest sends you to Yngol Barrow, it breaks the associated quest, causing Yngol's Shade, the Helm of Yngol, and the skeleton it rests upon not to appear as intended.

If you try to give him the helm after Brunwulf becomes Jarl of Windhelm, he is continuously locked up in the house, and picking the lock will only result in him telling you you're trespassing. There is no way to finish the quest and you are stuck with the helm in your inventory, as it cannot be dropped since it's a quest item.

The quest can be completed by attacking and luring Korir outside, calming him, and then speaking with him before he heads back inside. This will incur a bounty. Trying to engage him in conversation just as you are leaving will also lead to him following you outside.

Alternatively, open up the console, click on the jarl and then type Addtofaction 0005A1​A4 1 into the box. This adds an NPC to the player ally faction, which will make a normally hostile NPC be non-hostile. This should allow you to complete the quest.
You can also finish the quest by typing setstage Favor158 20. This will also remove the helm from your inventory.
Jarl Korir may not give a dialogue option to start this quest.

This quest can only be started the first time you visit Winterhold, if you fast travel away before initiating the quest then you won't be able to start it.
Starting the quest via console does not work. You can bypass this quest and still become Thane of Winterhold on PC with player.setrelationshiprank 1c1b5 2.
