Unfortunately, the gambler was already dead by the time I arrived. It seems he incurred some debts, and sold his armor to a collector in Riften. I killed the collector in order to take the armor from her. Objective 60: Retrieve the armor

I've heard stories of former bandits living as fugitives across Tamriel. At the barracks in Riften, I found information on an Imperial wagering on the pit fights at Cragslane Cavern. Unfortunately, the gambler was already dead by the time I arrived. It seems he incurred some debts, and sold his armor to a collector in Riften. After some effort, I managed to get the custom armor from the collector.

notes: Armor Collector carries Orders that can be pickpocketed.

quick: Talk to Temba Wide-Arm.
Acquire ten bear pelts.
Return to Temba Wide-Arm.

walkthrough.heading: Damn Bears
paragraphs: Temba Wide-Arm really does not like bears. She is a Nord woman who has sunk all of her money into a mill in Ivarstead. Even in passing you will hear her complaining to anyone within earshot how the bears are running her business into the ground. If you stop to chat she will explain that bears are ruining the trees by scratching up the trunks, rendering them useless as lumber. She is sorely in need of help with the bear problem and offers payment if you bring her ten bear pelts, thus thinning out the bear population.

walkthrough.heading: Filling the Order
paragraphs: Temba will accept any combination of bear pelts, cave bear pelts, or snow bear pelts; it doesn't matter to her as long as they are ursidae.

There are two bear dens in the vicinity of Ivarstead: Honeystrand Cave to the south past the river, and Pinepeak Cavern to the north near the steps leading up to High Hrothgar. There are also a number of bear pelts in Broken Oar Grotto, a cave north of Solitude. Giants frequently carry bear pelts, and you can also buy bear pelts from general goods merchants, Khajiit caravans, and hunters in the wild.
Once you bring the ten pelts to her she will be surprised that you came through for her and will reward you with a random leveled enchanted war axe.

stages.text: (Only displayed if you don't already have 10 bear pelts) Objective 10: Gather 10 bear pelts for Temba Wide-Arms [sic] (<Global=FFI03BearCount>/10)

notes: If you are carrying more than ten bear pelts, she will take them all, and it seems you cannot pickpocket them back.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.6, fixes this bug.

You can get the quest reward and keep the pelts by putting the bear pelts in a container immediately after you tell her that you got the pelts. Be warned however, that doing this will cause the quest to be stuck in your journal indefinitely.

paragraphs: If you talk to one of the quest givers, they will have one or more dialogue options to sell them crops — one for each sellable crop that you currently have in your inventory. Each quest giver accepts specific crops that are grown on that farm, as listed in the above table. Several crops besides wheat are included in the quest. The "quest" consists of selecting one of the dialogue options, thus selling crops to the farmer.

The implication is that you are being paid for harvesting crops from the farm, but in reality gathering or harvesting the crops is irrelevant. The farmers will accept vegetables from any source — those on the farm that they had previously harvested, ones that you found deep in an ancient tomb, ones that you pickpocketed from the farmer, or ones that you stole from the farm's kitchen table. In short, "Sell Vegetables" would be a more appropriate title than "Gather Wheat".
There are several key differences between selling crops to farmers for this quest and selling crops to normal merchants:

Farmers always take all samples of the specified crop that are in your inventory. If you want to sell only a portion of your crops, store that portion elsewhere before talking to the farmer, then pick it back up when you're done.
Farmers will purchase any stolen samples.
The amount purchased is not limited by the farmer's available gold.

The farmers always pay you the base value of the crops, regardless of your Speech skill and perks. This is the only way for low-level characters to receive money for various vegetables that cost 1 gold.
You never gain any Speech experience for the sale.
After harvesting, crops will regrow when the farm respawns after ten days.

The reward for completing this "quest" is however much money you earn for the sale of your collected vegetables. This is not leveled, as it is the base value of the crops that is being used. Thus, your "reward" depends upon number of crops and the type of crop sold.

notes: This quest does not have any stages or objectives.
This quest can be repeated indefinitely.
You cannot sell crops to either resident of Loreius Farm, despite them also being farmers.

Money you earn from gathering crops is fixed and is not affected by your Speech skill. This makes the quest one of the few ways to make money without increasing any skills, which will help control your level. This is useful when wanting to train in a certain skill as many times as possible. It is also one of the few ways to earn money without doing any questing, merchanting, or crafting.
Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the thane quest for the quest giver's hold.
There is no one in the game that will buy carrots, green and red apples, and tomatoes, most likely because they don't exist as an actual plant (such as potatoes) in the game world in the base game.

In the Hearthfire add-on, you can plant and grow wheat, cabbage, potatoes, leeks, gourds, and carrots in a greenhouse or garden of your player-built property, and you can sell the wheat, cabbage, potatoes, leeks, and gourds to the people listed above. Unfortunately, there still is no one who will buy carrots off of you, and you also cannot plant nirnroot.
Selling wheat to Tulvur at Hollyfrost Farm allows you to take low-value items freely from the House of Clan Cruel-Sea.
Selling crops to Katla will allow you to ride the horses at Solitude Stables for free, due to her being in the same ownership faction as the stablemaster.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.1.2, addresses this issue. This has been adjusted to set ownership correctly.

quick: Talk to Talen-Jei about his plans to marry.
Find three flawless amethysts he wishes to place on his engagement ring.
Return to Talen-Jei.

walkthrough.heading: A Proper Setting
paragraphs: Upon speaking with Talen-Jei in Riften, he will reveal his affection for Keerava, the innkeeper at The Bee and Barb. He wishes to marry her, but his "meager earnings" haven't allowed him to obtain the gems needed to complete the setting for a proper engagement ring. If you offer to help, he will tell you he needs three flawless amethysts. There are nine guaranteed gems found in eight different locations. Starting at level 12, you may also buy them from merchants at a base cost of 180 gold, find them as random loot, or get them randomly while mining. When you return to Talen-Jei with the gems, he will thank you, and reward you with a random leveled potion.

stages.text: Objective 10: Get 3 flawless amethysts for Talen-Jei (<Global=FFRiften06Found>/3) (re-displayed as each amethyst is acquired or removed)

notes: After this quest and Taking Care of Business, whether you threatened Keerava or not, Talen-Jei's dialogue may become inconsistent, he will call you his friend in greeting, but tell you to 'just get out of here' (The Bee and Barb) when saying goodbye. This is despite his deposition with you being 1 (friend).
You may be able to do this quest even if Keerava is dead.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.5, addresses this issue. It will now be unavailable if she is dead, and will now fail if she dies after it has begun.

quick: Talk to General Tullius after clearing out Fort Hraggstad.
Go to Beirand.
Pick Heavy, Medium, or Light Imperial armor.

walkthrough.heading: You're In the Army Now
paragraphs: After successfully clearing the bandits from Fort Hraggstad, your usefulness has been proven to Legate Rikke. Your oath has been sworn; you are officially an Imperial soldier and protector of the Empire. It's time you look the part. General Tullius tells you to go to Beirand, the smith, to get outfitted with your own Imperial armor. Talk to Beirand and choose your preferred weight:
When you are properly outfitted, Beirand will admonish you: "Now, that's it. One free outfit per soldier. You lose that, or get it banged up, you'll need to pay like everyone else."

stages.text: Objective 1: Get Imperial gear from Beirand

notes: It is not possible to do this quest if you first join the legion by giving the Jagged Crown to General Tullius.
Note that the Medium option contains one heavy armor piece (shield) and the rest are light armor pieces.
Although Beirand tells you that you'll need to pay if you lose or damage the Imperial armor set he gave you, you can forge a new set yourself.
Official Skyrim Patch 1.9 makes it possible to forge Imperial Light Armor.
After the completion of this quest, Beirand is no longer essential.
Beirand's inventory will carry less items after this quest.
If you join the Stormcloaks (either initially or by defecting after The Jagged Crown), this quest is never shut down which leaves Beirand in a perpetual essential alias.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.1.3, fixes this bug.

quick: Find Gharol at Dushnikh Yal.
Deliver the sword to Lash gra-Dushnikh at Karthwasten.

walkthrough.heading: A Mother's Pride
paragraphs: Gharol is a blacksmith living in Dushnikh Yal, the Orc stronghold southeast of Markarth. If you're permitted to enter the stronghold, you may talk to her about her weapon business. She will tell you that while she occasionally trades with the outside world, Orcs infuse their weapons with their private emotions: "An Orc blade is a very personal thing. Anger, regret, pride. All these things are put into our steel." In the conversation you will discover that Gharol's daughter, Lash, chose to leave the stronghold, breaking with Orc custom and bringing shame and grief to her mother. Gharol tells you that she has forged a sword to channel her feelings about her daughter's betrayal, and to send her daughter a message. Then she will ask you to honor her with a task: bring the sword to her daughter in Karthwasten; Lash will know what it means.

walkthrough.heading: Message Received
paragraphs: Travel to Karthwasten and deliver the sword to Lash. She will reply, "So that's it, then. 'Don't come back.' Thank you. Here. You honored my mother's task and should be rewarded." The forsaken daughter will reward you with leveled gold and ask you to leave her alone.

stages.text: Objective 10: Deliver Gharol's sword to Lash

quick: Read Heretic Dossier: Blacksmith's Confessional at the Temple in Raven Rock.
Travel to Fahlbtharz Forge.
Kill Hand Kenro Hlan.
Travel to Ashfall's Tear.
Talk to Matriarch Drevlan and start three new tasks Her Word Against Theirs, Careless Curation, Buyer Beware.
Complete three new tasks above.
Return to Ashfall's Tear and clear the temple from Ash Zombies attacking
Talk to Matriarch Drevlan and get Tribunal Armory Key

paragraphs: To begin this quest, read the Heretic Dossier: Blacksmith's Confessional at the Temple in Raven Rock. It can be found on a table in the first room on the right on the lower floors of the temple.

You will then have to travel to Fahlbtharz and enter the Forge. Inside you will find Hand Kenro Hlan, he will be hostile and you will have to kill him. Once he is dealt with, search his body to find a note, unenchanted weapon, Kenro's Helmet and Kenro's Robes. Picking up these items will also start Trueflame (quest).
You will then need to head to Ashfall's Tear, once inside you will find a ALMSIVI puzzle. The correct order for the stone pillars is ASV.
If you decide to wear Kenro's helmet and robes and infiltrate the temple ranks, the ordinators at the door will not be hostile, however, if you are not wearing these, they will attack on sight.

walkthrough.heading: Joining the Heretics
paragraphs: If you disguise yourself, you can peacefully talk to Matriarch Drevlan and either persuade or prove yourself by fighting Almalexia's Hands:

If you manage to persuade her you will have to pray at the nearby Shrine of Almalexia next to the large statue at the temple entrance. Doing so acts as praying at any other shrine, curing diseases and replacing any active blessing with Almalexia's Blessing. This blessing grants +10 to the Heavy Armor skill and +10% damage with One-Handed weapons for 8 hours. Once you've prayed at the shrine, you've joined the heretics and can continue on to the next stage of the quest.

If you want to prove yourself through combat, you will have to fight Hand Kydren Indobar until he submits, then Hand Ethra Mavandas, Watchman Sindras and finally Vesparth the Toe. After this you will need to speak to Drevlan again:
After this point, you are now accepted. You are free to switch back to your other apparel if you want. Speak to Drevlan again to continue.
She will then hand you a note detailing your task and the location of the other masks. Reading the note will begin three quests:
Her Word Against Theirs: Spread the word of the Goddess Almalexia.
Buyer Beware: Ambush a meeting to retrieve the Mask of Vivec.
Careless Curation: Find the missing Curate to retrieve the Mask of Sotha Sil.
Once you return to the temple you will have to clear out the ash zombies that are attacking the temple, once they are dealt with you will need to speak to the Matriarch:
She will reward you with the Tribunal Armory Key, ability to craft Her Hand Armor Set and Indoril Armor Set is also gained, it requires Elven Smithing perk.

walkthrough.heading: Destroying the Heretics
paragraphs: If you decide to destroy the heretics, you can disguise yourself still in order to speak to Matriarch Drevlan, or you can just deal with them the traditional way.
If you choose the traditional way, you will have to first fight the two ordinators that guard the first door into the temple.

You will then have to fight everyone gathered in the ritual room past the statue. There is a narrow straight tunnel before the room. It is possible to fight everyone in the room one on one at this choke point.

You will still be able to complete the other Ghost of the Tribunal Quests by looting the bodies for notes. There is no key to the armory however and this prevents you from obtaining Skullcrusher. The other cases are unlocked however.

You will still have to fight the Ash Zombies and if you return to Ashfall Tear after that, you will find the Reclamation Priest with three Redoran Guards investigating the scene while sadly saying "Almsivi" to themselves. They will ask what you want but no dialogue will be available.
You will have all four masks, not replicas, but they have no associated magical qualities.

Objective 149: Defeat Almalexia's Hands in single combat (0/4)

notes: Disposition with heretics can be elevated in 3 ways, either finishing three tasks, or combating against 4 potential followers, or persuading Matriarch Drevlan and receiving Almalexia blessing, followers will become available as soon as their disposition toward you are elevated.
3 ways above can lead to complete "(Optional) Earn the Matriarch's trust and join the temple heretics", then you can equip whatever armor instead of Kenro's Helmet and Robes

If you choose to duel the 4 combatants and you have an active follower with you, they will sometimes aggro onto your follower (the follower will not retaliate due to the duel). Once the 4 duels have been won and you speak to Matriarch Drevlan to progress the quest, your follower will attack the 4 combatants, turning all of the heretics hostile and preventing you from siding with them. It is not possible to dismiss your follower after you initiate the first duel. Some potential fixes are:
Reload a previous save from before initiating the first duel, then dismiss your follower.
Kill your follower.
Exit the cave without speaking to Matriarch Drevlan, then do a quest that force-replaces your current active follower (unconfirmed if this works).

It is highly recommended to complete this quest and its sequel, Ashen Heart, first if you wish to recruit Vesparth the Toe to become your personal steward. If not, and you accidentally hit her, this will make you an enemy of the Tribunal Temple and all of its members will be hostile to you. If Vesparth is already a steward at this point, she will not turn hostile. However, you will lose the ability to recruit her as a follower and she will only have negative greetings.
It is still possible to complete both quests if this occurs, but it requires you to pacify the Tribunal Temple members.
This will happen even if you have the Black Book ability, Companion's Insight, active.

The dragon encounters are not in the Random Quest Encounters section because they are not a direct result of perceived actions during the Dragon Rising quest; rather, they are simply possible after the completion of that quest.
Random vampire attacks on settlements (added by Dawnguard) are disabled in Special Edition and the Nintendo Switch version of the game.
Some random encounter trigger boxes have their script properties set to the wrong holds.
The Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 4.1.1, fixes this bug. (details)
Even though random nighttime vampire attacks in settlements and cities is supposed to be disabled in the Special Edition, they can still happen after using Auriel's Bow on the sun.
Multiple random encounters may spawn in the same spot (such as bandits fighting a conjurer, plus Vigilants of Stendarr fighting skeletons) at the same time.

quick: Travel to Castle Dour and read the Emperor's letter.
Locate the camp southeast of Fort Greymoor and defeat the Alik'r mercenaries.
Take the key from Majid and recover the cursed Lord's Mail.
Go to Kynareth's shrine at the Temple of the Divines to claim the Lord's Mail.

walkthrough.heading: Mission from the Emperor
paragraphs: Head to Castle Dour in Solitude to intercept a letter from the Emperor. The Letter to General Tullius can be found on the ground floor of Castle Dour in the room to the north of General Tullius's map room. You are only required to read the letter to start the quest; taking it counts as theft, so be sure that you are not seen if you decide to take it with you. The letter reveals that the Lord's Mail, a legendary Imperial Legion artifact, has been stolen by a band of Alik'r mercenaries who were last seen south of Fort Greymoor in Whiterun Hold.

The Alik'r camp is actually located southeast of Fort Greymoor, and is home to two generic Alik'r mercenaries led by Majid the Mad. Taking on all three at once can be a tough fight, so prepare accordingly. Once the mercenaries lie dead, recover the Key to Alik'r Mercenary Chest from Majid's body and use it to open the nearby chest. Inside, you will find a cursed version of the Lord's Mail along with a set of instructions titled Majid - Please Read. The note warns that the cursed armor should not be worn; indeed, if you equip it you will be subjected to a constant 50-point reduction to your Health, Stamina, and Magicka.

walkthrough.heading: Blessing of Kynareth
paragraphs: In order to remove the curse from the Lord's Mail, you will need to seek the blessing of its mythic creator, Kynareth. This will necessitate a return to Solitude to visit the Shrine of Kynareth in the Temple of the Divines. Upon activating the shrine, you will be informed that "The Lord's Mail has been cleansed". This concludes the quest and rewards you with a set of heavy ebony armor with poison resistance, magic resistance, as well as a unique area effect that inflicts 5 points of health absorbance per second on nearby opponents. For the purpose of the Matching Set perk, it counts as Imperial armor.

stages.text: A letter from the Emperor pertaining to an Imperial artifact was found at Castle Dour. I should read it and find out what it's about. Objective : Read the Emperor's Letter

I've found a letter addressed to General Tullius from the Emperor of Tamriel instructing that The Lord's Mail, a treasured Imperial relic, be found and reclaimed. A band of Redguard mercenaries are rumored to have taken it. I should locate their whereabouts and see if I can obtain the artifact. Objective : Confront the Alik'r Mercenaries
I've confronted the Alik'r mercenaries and found a locked chest. I just need to find the key... Objective : Retrieve the Lord's Mail
I've retrieved The Lord's Mail, the legendary Imperial armor. Before it can be worn, it must be cleansed at the shrine of Kynareth in Solitude. Objective : Cleanse the Lord's Mail in Solitude
The Lord's Mail has been retrieved, blessed by Kynareth, and can now be worn safely.

notes: For historical information on the Lord's Mail, see the lore article.
The Alik'r mercenaries wear unique Redguard clothing items.

If playing on Survival Mode, you will need to disable Survival Mode in order to complete the quest and get the Lord's Mail. The easiest way is to disable Survival mode outside of the temple then re-enable it once you've cleansed the armor. For some reason, it won't work when you have to pay to use the shrine.

quick: Talk to Wujeeta about her job.
Give her a healing potion.

paragraphs: If you walk near Wujeeta, she will cry about losing her job and beg for help. Talk to her, and she will reveal that she has an addiction to skooma and that she wants to cure herself. She will ask for a healing potion in order to heal herself. If you probe further she will mention where she got the skooma from, "I got mine off of a merchant ship in Solitude", which ties in with another quest.

You have three options: agree to give her a potion, agree to find one for her, or refuse to help. If you refuse to give her a potion, the option remains to agree to give her one. If you agree to give her a potion, the lowest type of standard healing potion (e.g. Potion of Minor Healing) in your inventory will be removed, and she will reward you with a leveled unenchanted ring while thanking you, "Your kindness will never be forgotten".
Dialogue is closed at this point and the first part of the next quest is immediately added to the miscellaneous quests.

stages.text: Objective 10: Give Wujeeta a healing potion

notes: Healing spells do not work and she does not recognize crafted healing potions. She can only take a standard healing potion.

This is the first of three quests that are required to unlock the option to become Thane of the Rift for Laila Law-Giver or Maven Black-Briar. There are additional requirements noted on that quest's page.
Raising Wujeeta's disposition with this quest will allow you to freely take items from the fish barrels inside Riften Fishery and around the nearby fishing boats.

Wujeeta is not essential, and if she dies before this quest and the next are complete, you cannot become Thane of the Rift unless the Imperials take control of the Rift, either through negotiation or force.

quick: Talk to Farengar Secret-Fire.
Talk to Arcadia.

walkthrough.heading: The Only Show In Town
paragraphs: Farengar Secret-Fire is a dedicated court wizard serving Jarl Balgruuf the Greater at Dragonsreach in Whiterun. Most of his time is spent studying and advising the Jarl on the current dragon threat. However, he does have time to assist the locals in town. If you ask him if he is the only wizard in town, he will acknowledge that while, technically, he is alone in his craft, the town also holds other practitioners. And, since he's on the subject, he remembers he has some frost salts he'd promised to pick up for local alchemist Arcadia, the proprietor of Arcadia's Cauldron. He asks if you wouldn't mind delivering the frost salts; Arcadia will surely compensate you for them. When you tell him you will help him out, he will respond with a disparaging remark, but will hand you the frost salts, a quest item not to be dropped.

walkthrough.heading: He'll Never Know What Hit Him
paragraphs: Head to Arcadia's Cauldron and enter during regular business hours, specifically between 8am and 8pm, or even when she strolls around the main trading room in the evening; as always, she will claim you have a fatal disease in hopes you will buy one of her potions, but will be grateful for the salts. She then reveals she needs the salts for a love elixir meant for the unsuspecting Farengar, and will then hand you three potions as compensation. Additionally, as you have now earned her friendship, almost all the various ingredients and potions in her shop are free to take.

stages.text: Objective 10: Give the Frost Salts to Arcadia

quick: Have Eorlund Gray-Mane mend Wuuthrad.
Return Wuuthrad to Ysgramor's Tomb.
Make your way through the tomb.
Meet Kodlak.
Fight one final spirit.
Release Kodlak.

walkthrough.heading: The Funeral
paragraphs: After the events of Purity of Revenge, Vilkas will run towards the Skyforge to participate in the late Harbinger Kodlak Whitemane's funeral. The ceremony is to be held near Eorlund Gray-Mane's smithy. All of the Companions will be present, along with the Jarl, steward and the local priestess of Kynareth. Kodlak is placed above the forge, and the ceremony ends with Aela the Huntress lighting the fire, symbolizing a final goodbye:

After the ritual, Eorlund will seek you out, asking for the fragments of Wuuthrad and Kodlak's secret fragment from his chambers. Retrieve the fragment from the end table in his room. Kodlak's Journal, also in the end table, offers some insights on him and his visions. Return to Eorlund with the fragment. When he accepts it, he will inform you that your Shield-Siblings have gone to the Underforge for a gathering and suggests you join them:

walkthrough.heading: Wuuthrad Finally Returned!
paragraphs: In the Underforge you will find the three members of the Circle, Farkas, Vilkas and Aela, talking around the blood fountain, all of them frustrated and discouraged. They all know that Kodlak died without being granted his only wish, namely to be freed of his lycanthropy so he could spend his afterlife in Sovngarde. While they know of a way to cleanse his soul, it requires them to enter the Ysgramor's Tomb and perform a ceremony:

Vilkas: "The old man had one wish before he died. And he didn't get it. It's as simple as that." Aela: "Being moon-born is not so much of a curse as you might think, Vilkas." Vilkas: "That's fine for you. But he wanted to be clean. He wanted to meet Ysgramor and know the glories of Sovngarde. But all that was taken from him." Aela: "And you avenged him." Farkas: "Kodlak did not care for vengeance." Vilkas: "No, Farkas, he didn't. And that's not what this is about. We should be honoring Kodlak, no matter our own thoughts on the blood." Aela: "You're right. It's what he wanted, and he deserved to have it." Vilkas: "Kodlak used to speak of a way to cleanse his soul, even in death. You know the legends of the Tomb of Ysgramor." Aela: "There the souls of the Harbingers will heed the call of northern steel. We can't even enter the tomb without Wuuthrad, and it's in pieces, like it has been for a thousand years."
At this point, Eorlund Gray-Mane enters with the repaired Wuuthrad on his back:

Eorlund: "And dragons were just stories. And the elves once ruled Skyrim. Just because something is, doesn't mean it must be. The blade is a weapon. A tool. Tools are meant to be broken. And repaired." Vilkas: "Is that? Did you repair the blade?" Eorlund: "This is the first time I've had all the pieces, thanks to our Shield-Brother/Shield-Sister here. "The flames of a hero can reforge the shattered." The flames of Kodlak shall fuel the rebirth of Wuuthrad. And now it will take you to meet him once more."
He will then address you personally:
He will then hand you the weapon and speak to the other members:
Your allies will then take off towards the legendary Ysgramor's Tomb.

walkthrough.heading: Ghosts of the Companions
paragraphs: As soon as you enter the tomb, Vilkas will approach and warn you about the dangers that lie ahead. He also says he will take no part in the task, as he has too much grief in his heart. Activate the Ysgramor statue, which will take Wuuthrad from your inventory, and place it on the statue to lower the wall. You may reclaim Wuuthrad by activating the statue again, and the wall will remain open. Followed by Aela the Huntress and Farkas, two skeevers greet you as you head north into the tomb. Continue down, and follow the path around until you are heading west into the next chamber with several Companion ghosts who taunt and warn of your impending death. They attack with Ancient Nord Bows, Swords, and Battle Axes, but their loot will disappear quickly if not searched immediately. Now head south until you enter a large room, with more tombs encircling a pond. Here one or two more ghostly apparitions test your courage before moving deeper into the tomb. Going west up the small stairs past the tombs, you encounter a spider web to the south that must be broken through to continue. It is here that Farkas reveals that, "Ever since Dustman's Cairn, the big crawly ones are my weakness". Consequently, he will proceed no further and instead runs back to join Vilkas at the statue. With Aela the Huntress as your only ally now, hack your way through the spider webs and face a Giant Frostbite spider, and many poison-spitting frostbite spiders. Follow the stairs down past the white caps into the next area. Two more companion ghosts await you, and after finishing them off, search the draugr laid out on the tables for valuables, and a potion of stamina beside the wrapped body. Be sure to search the draugr skeletons in their tombs for leveled weapons and armor. Heading east up the small stairs, open the next iron door and you'll enter an area with draugr tombs to your right, but a closed gate to your left. Activating the pedestal will open the closed gate. Enter this chamber heading north, where four more ghosts await shooting arrows, and wielding both one and two-handed weapons. Dispose of them, and find the Two-handed skill book The Legendary Sancre Tor in the center of the room next to the burial urns. Up the stone stairs and through this final iron door.

walkthrough.heading: The Trip to Sovngarde
paragraphs: You will find the ghost of Kodlak Whitemane warming his hands near the Flame of the Harbinger. After explaining that the room is, in fact, swarming with the ghosts of his predecessors, whom you can't see, he will ask you if you still own the Glenmoril Witch heads. He will then ask you to toss one into the Flame, in an attempt to cure him of his werewolf curse. After doing so, Kodlak's wolf spirit will be released and immediately attack. After the battle, Kodlak will thank you and name you the new leader of the Companions. He will then travel to Sovngarde and finally find his peace, completing the quest.

walkthrough.heading: Harbinger of the Companions
paragraphs: You can now speak to Aela, who will recognize your new position and tell you she is going to stay in the tomb for a while longer, for further studies. If you linger there, Vilkas and Farkas will arrive and also say they want to stay. All three will then become available as followers.

You can cure yourself of lycanthropy before you leave the tomb if you wish. If you don't, you will be required to cure two other Companions of their lycanthropy before you will again have the option to do so. Consider that choosing to remain a werewolf is the only way to access the quest Totems of Hircine, which grants unique abilities you may use while in beast form. You may come back to cure your lycanthropy later. To cure yourself now, throw another Glenmoril Witch head into the fire. Your wolf spirit will emerge. Kill it to rid yourself of being a werewolf permanently. If Aela, Vilkas or Farkas are around, they will aid in the fight.

After you've finished, continue up the spiral wooden stairs and locate the chest on the northeastern ledge to claim the Shield of Ysgramor, along with some other valuable loot, then exit through the nearby door by activating a chain. Go up the stairs, and through another short hallway before arriving at another wall with a chain. Pulling the chain opens the wall to the first chamber in the tomb as well as the wall on the opposite side. Before leaving the tomb, you can take Wuuthrad from Ysgramor's statue if you didn't earlier. Exit the tomb through the Western (W) passageway, which was previously inaccessible. Follow the set of stairs outside up the mountain to discover a word wall which teaches part of the Animal Allegiance shout. Directly north (to the right) of the word wall is a gold ore vein.

walkthrough.heading: Achievements
paragraphs: One achievement is unlocked when you complete this quest and finish the questline:
Glory of the Dead (30 points/Silver)

stages.text: I should attend the funeral of Kodak Whitman [sic], the late Harbinger of the Companions. Objective 10: Attend Kodlak's funeral
Eorlund needs the fragments of Wuuthrad to prepare them for remounting in Jorrvaskr. Objective 15: Give the fragments of Wuuthrad to Eorlund
Objective 17: Retrieve Kodlak's fragment
Objective 18: Give the final fragment to Eorlund
As a member of the Circle, I need to convene in the Underforge to determine the next steps for the Companions following the death of Kodak Whitman [sic]. Objective 20: Meet the Circle

The Companions believe there is a way to cleanse Kodlak's soul of the taint of the beast. We're going to the ancient Tomb of Ysgramor to perform the ceremony. Objective 30: Go to Ysgramor's Tomb with the Circle
Objective 35: Return Wuuthrad to Ysgramor
Objective 40: Get to the burial chamber
Objective 50: Speak to Kodlak
Objective 60: Put witch head into fire
Objective 65: Defeat the wolf spirit
Objective 70: Speak to Kodlak
I helped grant Kodlak Whitemane the glory of Sovngarde, and took his place as Harbinger of the Companions.

notes: Once the funeral ceremony has begun, you won't be able to use the Skyforge until the quest is finished.
Once the quest is finished, everything in the Harbinger's room at Jorrvaskr becomes free to take.
Aela and Farkas, as quest-specific followers, behave differently than "permanent" followers:
Neither of them will enter sneak mode when you do, and when either can see you, the sneak eye remains open.
If you get too close to them while sneaking, they will yell "Stay away from me!" as if you were going to pickpocket them.
Accidentally attacking either of them might turn them hostile.
Aela, Farkas, (and Vilkas after he speaks to you at the entry) will only repeat "For Kodlak!" during the quest, and won't have any dialogue options, including skill training.

You can bring any other follower with you and they will help clear the tomb. However, at the final fight they may ignore Kodlak's wolf spirit as if it were invisible to them. If you choose to cure yourself, they will fight your released spirit normally.
The ghosts' remains cannot be looted and will disappear immediately.
It's possible to pickpocket the ghosts' armor and weapons with the Perfect Touch perk before they engage in combat or after casting Pacify on them.
All ghosts wear a full set of Ancient Nord Armor and wield one of the various Ancient Nord weapons.

The first time you talk to Eorlund after the quest, he will tell you about a strange change he has observed with the Skyforge: "You know, since Kodlak's funeral the Skyforge feels more... awake. It's always been said that the souls of the heroes of old are what give Skyforge steel its strength. But I think the forge knows the greatness of Kodlak's soul. I can't really explain, but it feels like it's... young. I'll wager it could now forge metal the likes of which hasn't been seen since eras long forgotten. I'm eager to try."
Although Farkas, Vilkas, and Aela are presumably supposed to lose their essential statuses after this quest, they remain essential even then.
The quest may not start if you are in combat with Eorlund Gray-Mane
The Official Skyrim Patch, version 1.9.26.0.8, fixes this bug.
To start the quest, first select Eorlund and enter kill in the console, followed by enter setstage C06 0 and finally resurrect.
Kodlak's ghost may not appear when entering the final chamber.

Using the console command setstage C06 60 will allow you to put the witch's head in the fire, at which point Kodlak's wolf spirit will appear. After defeating the spirit, Kodlak may still not appear, at which point the console command setstage C06 200 will end the quest as usual, with Aela exclaiming that she heard Kodlak pronounce you leader.
If you leave the Underforge while the circle is talking after the funeral, the dialogue may not continue when you return.

If you follow the Circle members heading to Ysgramor's Tomb after Wuuthrad has been assembled, the group may eventually get stuck running back and forth between Dawnstar and the mountain range about halfway towards Driftshade Refuge.

If Eorlund isn't around: Go to the Skyforge and execute the following commands (note that player.placeatme does not work): "prid 1A683" then "resurrect" then "moveto player". Talk to him to continue the mission.
If enough time has passed since Skjor's death in The Silver Hand to allow his body to be deleted, this quest may not start.

The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.6, addresses this issue. Bethesda mistakenly included a mandatory alias for Skjor despite the fact that he's killed off before the questline gets this far. His alias is now marked as optional to allow the quest to start.
Serana may be seen using the Skyforge while Kodlak's funeral scene is underway.

The Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 4.2.6, addresses this issue. Her AI package will now disable sandbox behavior until you retrieve the final Wuuthrad fragment from Kodlak's room after Eorlund asks you to retrieve it.
Kodlak's corpse may be seen without his Wolf Armor equipped during the funeral scene.
The Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 4.2.6, fixes this bug.
If you leave during the funeral and then begin the Battle for Whiterun, the funeral may be over when you return, and you won't be able to continue the quest.

quick: Find Joften's notes on Golden and Dark Smithing.
Read Joften's notes.

paragraphs: While investigating the first Saints camp for Balance of Power, you will slay the Saints Bandit Leader. In his corpse is a note called Notes on the Blacksmith, which gives details about the blacksmith Joften and his ability to forge Golden & Dark equipment. However, it would appear the bandits lost patience with Joften, who became increasingly insane, and ended up killing him. His notes, however, are hidden and would likely reveal his secrets. The only hint given was that as a child, Joften used to play in the area around Half-Moon Mill, so the bandits had intended to investigate there.

Head to Half-Moon Mill and search under the bridge to find a chest containing Joften's Notes as well as other loot. Reading the journal will complete the quest and allow you to craft Golden/Dark equipment once you have the Daedric Smithing perk.

The chest and the note will be there regardless of whether the quest has been started, so if the player did not loot the note that starts the quest and the Saints Bandit Leader's corpse despawned, they can still learn Golden and Dark smithing.

quick: Speak with Tolfdir.
Listen to Tolfdir.
Follow Ancano.
Speak with Quaranir.
Find the Augur of Dunlain.
Report to Savos Aren.

walkthrough.heading: An Orb Worth Noting
paragraphs: After your conversation with Urag gro-Shub about the newly recovered books, the librarian suggests you speak with Tolfdir about the findings. Tolfdir can be found in the Hall of the Elements, in deep rumination about the orb from Saarthal, or the Eye of Magnus. Let him know about your findings and he will begin to discuss the Eye with you. He will explain how the markings seem to be unique, as they do not appear to be Elven, Daedric, or Ayleid. Ancano will interrupt Tolfdir's musings and demand that you follow him to meet a mysterious visitor who has asked to speak with you.

walkthrough.heading: A Moment in Time
paragraphs: Follow Ancano to the Arch-Mage's quarters and you will meet Quaranir, another representative from the Psijic Order. Quaranir will freeze time in order to speak privately with you. He will explain that you must prevent anyone from using the Eye of Magnus, as he fears the consequences its misuse will bring. He will suggest that you seek out the Augur of Dunlain within the College, who may be able to give you better guidance. Quaranir will then unfreeze time and leave, confusing Savos and angering Ancano. Speaking to the various mages about the Augur will lead you to either Tolfdir or Mirabelle Ervine for more information. Tolfdir will tell you about the Augur immediately, but you must pass an easy-level Speech check to convince Mirabelle. Either way, you will learn that the Augur is a former student at the College, but something befell him as a result of his own ambitions. He can now be found in The Midden in his altered state.

walkthrough.heading: The Unearthing
paragraphs: You can access the Midden from a trap door in the northern corner of the courtyard or by the stairwell in the Hall of Countenance. Making your way to the Augur of Dunlain is relatively easy; you will likely encounter a few ice wraiths and frostbite spiders, along with a small number of draugr and skeletons. Proceed into The Midden Dark and continue until you reach a locked door. When you approach it, the Augur will warn you from the other side that your efforts will only end in disappointment. The door will then open.

walkthrough.heading: The Augur
paragraphs: The Augur will inform you that others (including Ancano) have previously sought information about the Eye of Magnus without realizing the dangers it poses. While the Augur speaks only of disaster for the Thalmor, he seems encouraged by your path and offers to help you further. He will then inform you that you will need the Staff of Magnus to avert the disaster the Psijics warned you about, and urges you to share this information with Savos Aren.

walkthrough.heading: More than a Mere Apprentice
paragraphs: Speak to Savos and inform him of the Augur's message. It takes a bit of convincing to get Savos motivated and interested in this turn of events. Eventually, he will direct you to Mirabelle Ervine for more information on the Staff and then give you the Mage's Circlet, impressed with your performance thus far.

stages.text: Urag has asked me to mention the Night of Tears book to Tolfdir. Objective 10: Speak with Tolfdir
I've mentioned the Night of Tears book to Tolfdir, who seems distracted by the orb from Saarthal, and has some additional thoughts about it. Objective 15: Listen to Tolfdir
While discussing the Saarthal orb with Tolfdir, Ancano interrupted and insisted I follow him. Objective 20: Follow Ancano

Ancano interrupted my conversation with Tolfdir to insist that I speak with someone claiming to be from the Psijic Order, who is waiting in the Arch-Mage's quarters in the College. Objective 30: Speak with Quaranir

I've been led to the Arch-Mage's quarters by Ancano, who was insistent that I speak to someone claiming to be from the Psijic Order. The monk, named Quaranir, has informed me that the "Eye of Magnus" is dangerous and that to learn how to deal with it, I need to speak with The Augur of Dunlain within the College. I should ask my fellow members where to find him. Objective 40: Find the Augur of Dunlain

I've been led to the Arch-Mage's quarters by Ancano, who was insistent that I speak to someone claiming to be from the Psijic Order. The monk, named Quaranir, has informed me that the "Eye of Magnus" is dangerous and that to learn how to deal with it, I need to speak with The Augur of Dunlain within the College. He can be found in the Midden, beneath the College.

After speaking with Quaranir from the Psijic Order and being warned of the danger of keeping the Eye of Magnus at the College, I sought out and talked to the Augur of Dunlain, who lives in the Midden underneath the College. The Augur told me that I'll need to find the Staff of Magnus, and to give that information to my superiors immediately. Objective 50: Report to Savos Aren

After speaking privately with a monk from the Psijic Order, I have been warned that the "Eye of Magnus" is potentially dangerous and must be dealt with. After consulting with the Augur of Dunlain beneath the College, I have brought word to the Arch-Mage that the Staff of Magnus needs to be located.

notes: After Quaranir freezes time but before you speak to him you can steal any item in the Arch-Mage's Quarters without acquiring a bounty.
If you follow Quaranir out of the College after he freezes time in the Arch-Mage's Quarters, he will walk through Winterhold and enter The Frozen Hearth.
After you receive the objective to "Report to Savos Aren", Atronach Forge Recipes will begin to appear in random loot.
When the Eye of Magnus appears in the Hall of the Elements, there is an option to "Activate Eye of Magnus" when you point your crosshairs over it in close proximity, but doing so has no effect.
When you enter the Arch-Mage's Quarters and go upstairs, time may stop yet Quaranir is not there, and you're stuck forever.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.7, fixes this bug.
Open the console and manually advance the quest by entering setstage MG04 40.
Using the console command prid 0002BA3D and then moveto player, will move him to the College, and the quest should proceed normally.

When the quest begins, you may be able to use the door linking the Arcaneum to the Arch-Mage's Quarters, even though the Arch-Mage's Quarters is supposed to be off-limits at that point. Entering prior to being told to go there by Ancano will freeze out the quest, requiring you to exit the game via the console.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.7, fixes this bug.

You may not get the next quest "Revealing the Unseen" after completing the quest. This appears to be permanent and cannot be fixed by reloading. As the quest does not load, Mirabelle will have normal dialogue and the quest is impossible to begin.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.9, fixes this bug.
When talking to Ancano after talking to Tolfdir, you may get locked in dialogue with him permanently, preventing you from doing anything.
Open the console and manually advance the quest by entering setstage MG04 30.
Ancano may not open the door to the Arch-Mage's Quarters and lead you there.

Open the console command and manually advance the quest stage by entering setstage MG04 30. The quest marker above Ancano's head should disappear. The door to the Arch-Mage's Quarters should be unlocked. You are now free to talk to Quaranir and continue the storyline.
The Augur of Dunlain may be unable to speak his expected lines if you go to the Midden before asking where he is. This is due to a set of bad conditions on the quest script.
The Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 4.2.8, fixes this bug.

quick: Talk to Adrianne Avenicci.
Go to Dragonsreach.
Talk to Proventus Avenicci.

walkthrough.heading: A Warmaiden's Gift
paragraphs: Adrianne Avenicci is a blacksmith who owns the smithy and weapons shop, Warmaiden's, in Whiterun. When asked if she works her forge all day, Adrianne will admit that she does, and that she recently forged a greatsword for Jarl Balgruuf the Greater in an attempt to impress him. However, she can't seem to find an opportunity to deliver it. She would like for the sword to be delivered to her father, Proventus Avenicci, the steward of Dragonsreach in Whiterun.

walkthrough.heading: Delivering the Sword
paragraphs: Proventus is generally found in the main chamber of Dragonsreach, beside the throne. Deliver the sword to him, telling him that it is from his daughter. He will remark, "From Adrianne? Ah, this must be that weapon for the Jarl. Poor girl, so eager to prove herself. I'll present it to Balgruuf when his mood is... agreeable." He will then reward you with twenty gold.

stages.text: Objective 10: Deliver the sword to Proventus Avenicci

notes: If you sided with the Stormcloaks in the Civil War and have completed Battle for Whiterun, Proventus will be in the Blue Palace's basement along with Balgruuf and Irileth. The quest is otherwise the same as if you had joined the Imperials.
As a quest item, the sword has zero weight. It can be tempered, but not enchanted, making it a potentially useful item to hold onto early in the game.

If you place Balgruuf's Greatsword on a weapon rack or plaque, the quest can still be completed by talking to Proventus, and the sword will disappear from the rack/plaque. However, the slot the sword occupied can never be used again.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.1, fixes this bug.
Proventus Avenicci equips the greatsword that was intended to be for Balgruuf.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.0, addresses this issue. It will now simply be taken from you instead and placed in a display case in Balgruuf's quarters as was implied.

quick: Speak to Mjoll the Lioness in Riften.
Find Grimsever in the Dwemer ruins of Mzinchaleft.
Return to Mjoll.

walkthrough.heading: Mjoll the Lioness
paragraphs: Mjoll the Lioness lives in Riften where she spends her time speaking out against the Thieves Guild and talking to her faithful follower Aerin about the evils in the world. Acting on her convictions, she has taken on the responsibility of patrolling the town, which she does every day; from 9am she can be found in the Market, at noon she will be inside The Bee and Barb, and from 6pm she patrols the streets of Riften until midnight. Once you reach level 14, however, Mjoll will have more on her mind than just the Thieves Guild. In her younger days, she traveled and adventured all over Tamriel but lost her favorite blade Grimsever when she ventured into the ancient Dwemer ruin of Mzinchaleft. The dangers of the ruin nearly took her life as well, so she retired from adventuring and settled down in Riften. She admits that she feels defenseless without her blade and has a hard time finding a replacement. You can then offer to help her and, while she will refer to it as a 'fool's errand', she will also let you undertake the task, adding a map marker for Mzinchaleft.

walkthrough.heading: Mzinchaleft
paragraphs: Mzinchaleft is a large Dwemer ruin located in the snowy tundra east of Morthal, northwest of the Hall of the Vigilant. Bandits now inhabit the first zones of the ruin and you will encounter up to six of them guarding the entrance. Fight them, locate the door and prepare for a very long dungeon crawl. Once inside, head down the first two slopes and fight the two bandits residing near the campfire. Proceed through the tunnels until you reach a room with two bandits and a cauldron. Dispose of them and claim some minor loot from the chest. At the intersection, kill the bandit and claim Maluril's Room Key from his body, then use it to unlock the gate. During the Dark Brotherhood quest Kill Maluril, the quarters behind the door will be occupied by Maluril but, during this quest you will find them empty. Read through the Speech skill book A Dance in Fire, v7 then backtrack to the intersection and proceed in a southern direction. In the next chamber you will witness two Dwarven spheres dispose of some bandits before coming after you. Fight them all and keep heading south, following the path as it twists and turns, and disposing of the various automatons along the way.

Before long, you will reach an area with a handle and two gates, and several more handles behind the gates. Pull the only available handle and the gate to the east will open. Pull the new handle and the gate to the south will open. Pull the new handle and backtrack to the previous handle and pull it again. Go into a newly opened chamber to the south and pull the handle. Head south yet again and pull the handle, then backtrack to the previous handle and pull it again. Return to the very first handle and pull it. This opens the two gates to the southeast, giving you access to a valve. You'll find an unlocked chest and a master-locked chest in the room with the valve. Activate the valve and the path will now be clear and provide access to the next zone, Mzinchaleft Depths.

walkthrough.heading: The Depths
paragraphs: When the elevator brings you down into the Mzinchaleft Depths, the first thing you will notice is a dead Falmer and the recognizable sound of a chaurus on the other side of the locked door. The door hides a very large multi-leveled chamber filled with Falmer enemies and plenty of secret areas, so make sure to raid every corner before leaving through the door to the east. Two Falmer enemies wait in the next chamber, so dispose of them and proceed forward, into a tunnel-like system with more Falmer. Watch out for a tripwire triggering a claw trap as you enter the next room and fight even more Falmer and a chaurus. The tents contain minor loot and a dead bandit. Find the tunnel to the north and open a gate to another huge chamber with a fountain in the middle. Fight the inevitable Falmer enemies and head up the bridge to the north. At the top, fight another Falmer and locate the button and activate it. This will open the path in the southwestern part of the chamber. More Falmer wait on the other side, including a boss, so finish them off and head up the stairs to the north and the entrance to the third and final zone, Mzinchaleft Gatehouse.

walkthrough.heading: Grimsever
paragraphs: In the Gatehouse, you will only have to go around the corner before you will encounter the Dwarven Centurion that nearly killed Mjoll the Lioness back in the day. It will attack right away and will be accompanied by a Dwarven Sphere. After the battle, locate Grimsever, which is lying on a table. Find the boss-leveled chest behind bars to the north and pull the nearby handle to gain access. Lastly, if you have the attunement sphere, you can gain access to Blackreach from here. When all is said and done, open the western door and activate the handle to be brought back outside, emerging from an alternate entrance west of the main entrance.

Back in Riften you will find Mjoll patrolling as usual. When you hand her the blade, she will be overly impressed: "Astonishing. To think you actually were able to reach it and yet return to tell the tale. Rarely in my travels have I encountered those who possess skills equal to your own. I see I still have much to learn. If you'd permit me, I'd be honored to accompany you in your travels for a time." Alternatively, if you told her of your hopes to join the Thieves Guild, she will instead say: "When you told me of your intent to join the Thieves Guild, I honestly didn't think we'd have much to speak about ever again. Yet here you are with my weapon that you could have easily sold or kept for yourself. Forgive me for my hasty opinion of you, I see that I was wrong and that there's much I can learn from you. If you'd permit me, I'd be honored to accompany you in your travels for a time." Either way, she will then be available as a follower and a potential candidate for marriage.

stages.text: Objective 10: Locate Grimsever
Objective 20: Return to Mjoll

notes: Grimsever cannot currently be found in Mzinchaleft before Grimsever's Return has been triggered. Contrary to older versions of the game, entering or clearing Mzinchaleft beforehand does not cause the sword to spawn. Its usual location will remain empty until the quest has been triggered.
Grimsever is a one-handed Glass Sword though Mjoll is more proficient in two-handed weapons.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2.3, addresses this issue. Grimsever is now a Glass Greatsword to match her skills better.

After completing the quest, Mjoll will be available as a follower, at which point you can "trade" inventory with her and take Grimsever back. Any smithing upgrades made to Grimsever before giving it back to Mjoll will be lost, though you can upgrade it again.

If you are already level 14 or above when you first interact with Mjoll, you must also gain another level after your initial conversation and return to her before the dialogue option to begin this quest becomes available.

The boss fight presents a considerable challenge for a level 14 character, but you don't actually have to defeat the Centurion to get Grimsever. You can make a run for it, pick up the sword on the fly and head straight for the exit.
You will need to level up via skill increases to or beyond level 9 for the quest to be eligible to start. You cannot be console-commanded to an arbitrarily high level and start the quest.
If Mzinchaleft has already been discovered or cleared before Grimsever's Return is started, or you exceed the level requirement the quest may fail to trigger, with its aliases remaining empty.

If the quest cannot otherwise be started, it can be bypassed with the console. Use setstage FreeformRiften09 200 to mark the quest as complete, then prid 00019DF7 to select Mjoll and setrelationshiprank 00000014 1 to set her relationship with the player to Friend. Finally, use additem 00053379 1 to give Mjoll a copy of Grimsever. This reproduces the quest's relevant rewards, allowing Mjoll to be recruited or married normally.
Mjoll might not give you the quest to retrieve Grimsever despite fulfilling the above criteria, and Grimsever may not appear in the Mzinchaleft Gatehouse as stated above.

You may use the console to make her your friend with player.setrelationshiprank 00019DF7 4, allowing you to recruit her as a follower. After using her as a follower for a few days, she may give you the quest, and Grimsever should spawn.
You can use the console code player.additem 00053379 1 to give yourself the sword, then talk with her and give it to her. This may result in two copies of Grimsever being present in the game.

An internal conflict with the first scripted conversation between Mjoll and Aerin about "another run-in with the Thieves Guild" upon entering Riften means that you must level up -after- the scripted conversation has occurred (to level 14 or later) before Mjoll will offer the Grimsever quest.

quick: Talk to Temba Wide-Arm.
Acquire ten bear pelts.
Return to Temba Wide-Arm.

walkthrough.heading: Damn Bears
paragraphs: Temba Wide-Arm really does not like bears. She is a Nord woman who has sunk all of her money into a mill in Ivarstead. Even in passing you will hear her complaining to anyone within earshot how the bears are running her business into the ground. If you stop to chat she will explain that bears are ruining the trees by scratching up the trunks, rendering them useless as lumber. She is sorely in need of help with the bear problem and offers payment if you bring her ten bear pelts, thus thinning out the bear population.

walkthrough.heading: Filling the Order
paragraphs: Temba will accept any combination of bear pelts, cave bear pelts, or snow bear pelts; it doesn't matter to her as long as they are ursidae.

There are two bear dens in the vicinity of Ivarstead: Honeystrand Cave to the south past the river, and Pinepeak Cavern to the north near the steps leading up to High Hrothgar. There are also a number of bear pelts in Broken Oar Grotto, a cave north of Solitude. Giants frequently carry bear pelts, and you can also buy bear pelts from general goods merchants, Khajiit caravans, and hunters in the wild.
Once you bring the ten pelts to her she will be surprised that you came through for her and will reward you with a random leveled enchanted war axe.

stages.text: (Only displayed if you don't already have 10 bear pelts) Objective 10: Gather 10 bear pelts for Temba Wide-Arms [sic] (<Global=FFI03BearCount>/10)

notes: If you are carrying more than ten bear pelts, she will take them all, and it seems you cannot pickpocket them back.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.6, fixes this bug.

You can get the quest reward and keep the pelts by putting the bear pelts in a container immediately after you tell her that you got the pelts. Be warned however, that doing this will cause the quest to be stuck in your journal indefinitely.

quick: Talk to your fellow inmates.
Ask Grisvar the Unlucky for his spare shiv.
Obtain a bottle of Skooma.
Swap the Skooma for Grisvar's spare shiv.

walkthrough.heading: So what are you in for?
paragraphs: Before throwing you into Cidhna Mine, the guards were careful enough to remove all of your equipment, leaving weapon-based characters at a distinct disadvantage. If you chat to your fellow inmates, however, you will learn that Grisvar the Unlucky has a spare weapon, and might be willing to let you have it.

walkthrough.heading: If you want to get ahead, get a shiv
paragraphs: Grisvar admits to having an extra shiv but isn't keen to part with it. He is something of a Skooma addict, and has heard that Duach has got a bottle of the good stuff. Grisvar claims to be "shaking just thinking about it", and wants you to obtain the bottle for him.

walkthrough.heading: Distilled Pleasure
paragraphs: Grisvar isn't as discerning as his request makes him seem, and will accept any bottle of Skooma. Several of the mine's inmates possess bottles of Skooma but Duach is often to be found on his own, making it easier to pick his pockets or kill him quietly. You can also try to pass a Speech check with Duach or beat him in a brawl to make him hand over his bottle. However you obtain the Skooma, take it back to Grisvar.

walkthrough.heading: Forlorn hope
paragraphs: The Skooma is warmly received, and Grisvar gladly hands over his spare shiv. He asks you to promise you won't ever use it on him - and it's perhaps just as well that no option to accept the promise is offered.

stages.text: Objective 10: Talk to Grisvar about getting a shiv
Objective 20: Get a bottle of Skooma for Grisvar
Objective 30: Bring Grisvar the Skooma
Objective 30: Bring Grisvar the Skooma

quick: Travel to Bloodchill Cavern.
Speak to the waiter.
Sit at the table and read the note.
Defeat either the vampires or the guests and Dawnguard.
Speak to the survivor to receive leveled gold and the key to your new home.

walkthrough.heading: Player as a Non-Vampire
paragraphs: When you arrive at the manor, a number of guests are milling around the front door listening to a bard. Just inside, another reveler is drinking and dancing. Proceed down the hallway to the waiter. No matter what you say, the outcome will be the same; with him handing you a dinner menu (Version 1) and directing you and the other guests to your seats.

Sit down at the table, in a place of honor across from the door. Once you sit down, read the note on your plate named Please Read Aloud to gain some insight into this mysterious dinner party and proceed with the quest. After you read the last page of the letter, the waiter will approach Galtius across from you and bite him from behind, killing him. As the other guests rise from their seats in a panic, the bard in the room, the waiter, and two gargoyles will attack.

Deal with them, and be careful of the waiter: his lightning attacks are strong enough to one-shot lower-level players. Resist magic gear and followers might help. Once all the vampires and their stone minions are dead, speak with the "survivor." Some of the other guests may have survived your battle but the one to speak with is the Orc Durian, who is revealed to be a member of the Dawnguard:

He will then hand you a leveled amount of gold but no key, and you will become the official owner of the manor. This completes the quest. The doors along the entry hallway will open and you can begin using your new base.

If there are any surviving guests besides Durian, they will return to sit at the dinner table amidst the carnage. Once you leave and reenter the cave, all of the bodies and debris will be cleaned up (including the vampiric bard near the entrance, which was presumably dispatched by Durian on your way into dinner), any surviving guests will have left, and the dinner table will be cleared out of the trophy room to allow your unimpeded access.

walkthrough.heading: Player as a Vampire
paragraphs: If the player is a vampire, things play out a little differently. When you arrive at the manor, pass through the guests and speak to the waiter at the end of the hall. After choosing one of four options, the waiter will give a generic response and hand you the dinner menu (Version 2). He will then turn and lead you to the banquet table.

Once there, sit and read through the feast note Please Read Aloud. After doing so you are instructed to begin the feast, by drinking the blood of the already enthralled Parven. At that point, the waiter will approach Galtius and bite him from behind, killing him. After Galtius's death Parven will also terminate and the Dawnguard will enter the building, initiating battle.
After disposing of the Dawnguard and the remaining guests, speak to the waiter once more.

At this point the waiter will give you the key to the manor and some leveled gold, completing the quest. Three more dialogue options are given; all will end the conversation. The doors along the entry hallway are now open for use, and when you leave and reenter the cavern all of the destruction from your fight will be cleared away.
