If the ruins are cleared out before the quest is given to kill the bandit leader, the ruins may not repopulate, causing this quest to not be completable.
To fix this, approach the boss and open the console. After clicking on him, type resurrect 1. This will bring him back to life and allow you to complete the quest.

Another fix is to open the console and type setstage bq01 100 (if started by the steward) or setstage bq01 101 (if started by the Jarl). This will clear the bandit leader and point you to collect the bounty.

quick: Speak with an innkeeper, jarl, or steward to receive the bounty.
Kill the dragon at the indicated location.
Speak with the jarl or steward of the hold to receive your reward.

walkthrough.heading: Here There Be Dragons
paragraphs: After your adventures at Whiterun's Western Watchtower during Dragon Rising, a proliferation of dragons are about. In your travels, ask an innkeep, jarl or steward for some work. You may learn that a dragon has been harassing travelers and citizens around its lair, and the jarl of the hold has put out a bounty on the dragon. You are an enterprising sort, with newly acquired dragon soul absorbing powers and shouts, so take up the job.

walkthrough.heading: The Dragon Hunter
paragraphs: Seek out the offending dragon in its lair. There is a wide variety of dragon that you may encounter in each lair you visit. Once defeated, and the dragon soul is absorbed, be sure to remove the dragon bones and dragon scales. These are quite valuable in the local shops, and can be used to make and improve dragonbone and dragonscale armor.

walkthrough.heading: The Bounty
paragraphs: Once the dragon is dead, you will be directed to the jarl or steward of the hold to receive your payment.

stages.text: Objective 10: Kill the dragon located at <Alias=BountyLocation>
Objective 100: Collect bounty from <Alias=Steward> Objective 101: Collect bounty from <Alias=Jarl>

notes: If you are tasked to kill a dragon at a lair that you have already cleared, the dragon there will respawn. However, killing a respawned dragon (whether it has respawned because of this quest, or naturally after 10 or 30 days) will probably result in not getting a dragon soul.
You need to have completed Dragon Rising first before receiving this quest.
The dragon at Mount Anthor may not spawn, and the quest target will point to an incorrect location.
Use the console command setstage BQ04 100 to skip to the next stage, or setstage BQ04 200 to jump directly to quest completion.

quick: Speak with Skald, the Jarl of Dawnstar.
Kill the giant at the given camp.
Return to retrieve the bounty.

paragraphs: The Jarl of Dawnstar, Skald, will ask you to deal with a giant to send a message to all the other giants in the hold, for although they are not a problem now, the jarl believes they will be in the future. The giant can be found at one of three camps (above) and can be taken down by any means necessary.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: Once the giant is dead, return to Skald for your reward of gold:
Completing this quest is required to start the Thane of the Pale quest and Purchase land in Dawnstar if Skald is still Jarl.

stages.text: Objective 10: Kill the giant in <Alias=GiantCamp>
Objective 15: Return to Skald

notes: The quest has a minimum level of 22. If you are not level 22 yet, then you cannot receive this quest from Skald. If Brina is jarl (or Skald has been removed from power and then reinstated), this quest is not required to become Thane.

This quest requires a giant to kill. If you have cleared all of the giants from all of the giant camps, then you cannot receive this quest from Skald. To solve this issue, wait or sleep indoors for 30 days and all giant camps will have been respawned.
This quest cannot be started if you have a bounty in The Pale.
The dialogue for starting this quest might not appear. A probable reason is you might have another Favors quest running that tasks you to kill a certain enemy. This prevents this quest from starting.
Another possible fix is to fast travel to a non-cleared giant camp in The Pale and back to Dawnstar, which may make the dialogue option available.
Sometimes the quest objective will not be removed from the journal.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.0, fixes this bug.

quick: Get the bounty letter from an innkeeper, Jarl, or steward.
Go to the giant camp and kill the giant.
Return to the Jarl or the Jarl's steward for the reward.

paragraphs: Speaking with any innkeeper, Jarl, or Jarl's steward about work may lead them to give you a letter of bounty requesting you to kill a giant. This will give you a miscellaneous objective to kill the giant in a specific camp. Head to the camp specified in the letter and kill the marked giant (there may be multiple giants, but you only have to kill the marked one). Once the giant is killed, you can return to the Jarl or steward for your 100 gold reward.

stages.text: Objective 10: Kill the giant located at <Alias=BountyLocation>
Objective 100: Collect bounty from <Alias=Steward> Objective 101: Collect bounty from <Alias=Jarl>

notes: Sometimes the Jarl may request to kill another giant in a camp previously cleared. This is not a bug. New giants will be spawned and will be correctly associated with markers, killing and quest updates.
The objective "Collect bounty from Skald" may not clear from quest list. This bug is due to the quest pointer completing stage 100 when you talk to Skald instead of stage 101.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.0, fixes this bug.
A possible workaround is to use the console command setObjectiveCompleted BQ03 101 1 before turning in the quest to Skald, to clear the journal entry. Then just talk to Skald to get your bounty.

quick: Speak to Siddgeir, the Jarl of Falkreath.
Travel to the assigned dungeon.
Kill the bandit leader.
Return to Siddgeir.

paragraphs: The normal prerequisite for this quest is Rare Gifts, a radiant quest which can be given by six different people. If you have received that quest from any of the other five, then you cannot receive it from Siddgeir, and you must complete the other version before you can get it from Siddgeir. It is advisable that, if possible, Siddgeir's version of Rare Gifts should be completed soon after leaving Helgen, as the mead he wants can be found near the exit to the keep.

If you have Hearthfire installed, then at level 9 a courier will deliver a letter from the Jarl of Falkreath. Reading it will trigger the Falkreath version of Build Your Own Home and, when this quest is running, talking to Siddgeir will allow you to start the Bandit Leader quest without any prerequisites.
After completing the prerequisite quest or receiving the letter from Siddgeir, talk to him in order to initiate this quest.
Once you have reached the assigned dungeon, you will only have to kill the bandit leader of that dungeon; killing the lesser enemies is not mandatory, but would make your job easier.

notes: If you kill Captain Hargar during the quest Lights Out!, or by clearing out the grotto without the quest, then Ahtar will give you another Bandit Leader as the target provided they haven't been killed already and you have USSEP 3.0.1 installed. The quest Harsh Master can have identical quest objectives.
Version 3.0.1 of the Unofficial Skyrim Patch adds the missing bandit camp keywords to Orphan's Tear and Ironback Hideout, resulting in them also becoming possible targets for this quest.

Post completion of the main Dragonborn storyline, Fanari Strong-Voice may not give you the option to "Kill The Bandit Leader" for the Skaal.

If you are sent to Gallows Rock after you have already completed the Companions quest The Silver Hand, then the previously-killed generic Silver Hand members, as well as the unique Krev the Skinner, will all have respawned.

The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.1, addresses this issue. This version makes sure that Krev doesn't respawn, while Version 2.0.9 makes sure that no Silver Hand respawn at all, and that the dungeon will be reset to its original state.

If you are sent to Uttering Hills Camp and you have already completed Summerset Shadows for the Thieves Guild, you will be unable to complete this quest, as the bandit leader Linwe will already be dead, but there will be an objective arrow pointing to him as if he still needs to be killed.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.3, fixes this bug.

Selecting Linwe's body in the console then typing resurrect will bring him back to life as soon as you resume the game. Killing him again will then count for the quest completion. (Doesn't work if you have already received the favor quest, as resurrecting Linwe—before or after entering the cave—doesn't put the quest arrow back on him and killing him again doesn't complete the quest)
If Linwe's body has already disappeared, typing setstage Favor104 15 in the console will advance the quest.

If setstage Favor104 15 doesn't help you, type the following commands: prid C5688 and then kill. This should select the original quest target and kill him for you, advancing the quest to the next stage.

If prid C5688 doesn't help you, type the following commands: prid C5675, then disable, and then type prid C5675, then enable, and finally resurrect. This should place Linwe at the empty chair where the quest marker is pointing. Additional Summerset Shadow thieves should spawn as well.
If all previous codes don't work, try prid 7d67a, then resurrect and finally kill.

quick: Talk to Jarl Igmund to initiate quest.

Once you travel to the dungeon you will most likely have to deal with most leveled Forsworn before you can eliminate the leader.

notes: If Raerek is in a room with an adept lock, wait until he is sitting by the Jarl to receive your reward. He is there by 10am.

Upon the initial meeting with Jarl Igmund, he may not have the dialogue option to start this quest available. Exiting Understone Keep and fast travelling somewhere else (e.g. Karthwasten) and back may resolve this.

quick: Speak to Kjar onboard his ship at the Windhelm docks.
Travel to the random location and kill the bandit leader.
Return to Kjar for your reward.

paragraphs: Kjar, ship master of The North Wind currently anchored at the docks in Windhelm, will ask you to hunt down and kill a runaway crew member. The sailor had formed a group of bandits, who are currently hiding out in one of seven random locations. Travel to the location and kill the bandit leader there. Return to Kjar, who will give you a year's salary (a leveled gold reward).

stages.text: Objective 10: Kill the leader of <Alias=BanditCamp>
Objective 15: Return to Kjar

notes: The quest Kill the Bandit Leader can have identical quest objectives.
This quest is known to generate the boss NPC prior to actually getting it from Kjar, which would result in you killing the boss NPC and then being told to return to someone you never visited.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.3, fixes this bug.
If you have completed the mission and later reenter the same location once it is repopulated, it can give you the completion again, allowing you to collect a bounty for re-killing the rogue crewman.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.1, fixes this bug.
The bandit boss is prematurely made available to kill before Kjar actually offers the quest.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.1.0, fixes this bug.

If you are sent to Uttering Hills Cave, and have already completed Summerset Shadows for the Thieves Guild, you will be unable to complete this quest, as the bandit leader is replaced by Linwe and the former is nowhere to be seen.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.4, fixes this bug.
You can return the cave to its previous occupants by typing prid c5675 in the console, followed by disable.
You can still progress through the quest by typing "c5688".kill in the console.
You can progress through the quest by typing SetStage FreeFormShipsWindhelm 15 in the console.

Oddly, since the Jarl's Longhouse in Winterhold is marked as being owned by the Winterhold crime faction, once you finish the quest, you will have helped someone in the hold, allowing you take things from the longhouse without it being considered theft.

The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.1.3, addresses this issue. (details) Kjar is now part of the Eastmarch crime faction, and a new faction was created specifically for the residents of the longhouse in order to set ownership correctly.

notes: If you kill Captain Hargar during the quest Lights Out!, or by clearing out the grotto without the quest, then Ahtar will give you another Bandit Leader as the target provided they haven't been killed already and you have USSEP 3.0.1 installed. It can be either the Bandit Leader at Ironback Hideout or Orphan's Tear respectively. You can however, depending on luck, have Noster One-Eye's miscellaneous quest to retrieve his helmet, Ahtar's "Kill The Bandit Leader" and Lights Out! all running concurrently and all objectives are located within Broken Oar Grotto.
Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the thane quest for the quest giver's hold.
The quest Harsh Master can have identical quest objectives.
Version 3.0.1 of the Unofficial Skyrim Patch adds the missing bandit camp keywords to Orphan's Tear and Ironback Hideout, resulting in them also becoming possible targets for this quest.
Brunwulf Free-Winter only gives the quest when he's not a Jarl. However, if Brunwulf gives you the quest and the Empire captures Windhelm later on, you can still finish it after he becomes Jarl.
The Solstheim locations for this quest contain Reavers instead of regular bandits. Your journal will still say "bandit leader", though.
Post completion of the main Dragonborn storyline, Fanari Strong-Voice may not give you the option to "Kill The Bandit Leader" for the Skaal.

If you are sent to Gallows Rock after you have already completed the Companions quest The Silver Hand, then the previously-killed generic Silver Hand members, as well as the unique Krev the Skinner, will all have respawned.

The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.1, addresses this issue. This version makes sure that Krev doesn't respawn, while Version 2.0.9 makes sure that no Silver Hand respawn at all, and that the dungeon will be reset to its original state.

If you are sent to Uttering Hills Camp and you have already completed Summerset Shadows for the Thieves Guild, you will be unable to complete this quest, as the bandit leader Linwe will already be dead, but there will be an objective arrow pointing to him as if he still needs to be killed.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.3, fixes this bug.

Selecting Linwe's body in the console then typing resurrect will bring him back to life as soon as you resume the game. Killing him again will then count for the quest completion. (Doesn't work if you have already received the favor quest, as resurrecting Linwe—before or after entering the cave—doesn't put the quest arrow back on him and killing him again doesn't complete the quest)
If Linwe's body has already disappeared, typing setstage Favor104 15 in the console will advance the quest.

If setstage Favor104 15 doesn't help you, type the following commands: prid C5688 and then kill. This should select the original quest target and kill him for you, advancing the quest to the next stage.

If prid C5688 doesn't help you, type the following commands: prid C5675, then disable, and then type prid C5675, then enable, and finally resurrect. This should place Linwe at the empty chair where the quest marker is pointing. Additional Summerset Shadow thieves should spawn as well.
If all previous codes don't work, try prid 7d67a, then resurrect and finally kill.

quick: Speak to Kjar onboard his ship at the Windhelm docks.
Travel to the random location and kill the bandit leader.
Return to Kjar for your reward.

paragraphs: Kjar, ship master of The North Wind currently anchored at the docks in Windhelm, will ask you to hunt down and kill a runaway crew member. Return to Kjar, who will give you a year's salary (a leveled gold reward).

Travel to the dungeon.
Kill the Forsworn Leader.
Return to Jarl Igmund in Understone Keep to collect the gold reward.

paragraphs: Travel to Understone Keep in Markarth and speak to Jarl Igmund to initiate the quest in which you have to kill a Forsworn Leader. He will direct you to a dungeon in The Reach, which is where the Forsworn Leader is hiding. You must travel there and face the leader.
Once you travel to the dungeon you will most likely have to deal with most leveled Forsworn before you can eliminate the leader.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: Once you have dealt with him/her, return to Understone Keep to collect your reward from Jarl Igmund.

stages.text: Objective 10: Kill the leader of <Alias=Dungeon>
Objective 15: Return to Igmund

notes: If Raerek is in a room with an adept lock, wait until he is sitting by the Jarl to receive your reward. He is there by 10am.

It is possible to accept this quest and then find that all NPCs are non-aggressive towards you at the site. If this is the case feel free to kill or pickpocket any non-named NPCs (normally simply named "Forsworn") because none of the other NPCs will attack you.

Upon the initial meeting with Jarl Igmund, he may not have the dialogue option to start this quest available. Exiting Understone Keep and fast travelling somewhere else (e.g. Karthwasten) and back may resolve this.
If you complete the No One Escapes Cidna Mine quest line before ever speaking to Jarl Igmund, he may not ever give the dialogue option to start the quest. No known fix.

quick: Speak to Siddgeir, the Jarl of Falkreath.
Travel to the assigned dungeon.
Kill the bandit leader.
Return to Siddgeir.

paragraphs: The normal prerequisite for this quest is Rare Gifts, a radiant quest which can be given by six different people. If you have received that quest from any of the other five, then you cannot receive it from Siddgeir, and you must complete the other version before you can get it from Siddgeir. It is advisable that, if possible, Siddgeir's version of Rare Gifts should be completed soon after leaving Helgen, as the mead he wants can be found near the exit to the keep.

If you have Hearthfire installed, then at level 9 a courier will deliver a letter from the Jarl of Falkreath. Reading it will trigger the Falkreath version of Build Your Own Home and, when this quest is running, talking to Siddgeir will allow you to start the Bandit Leader quest without any prerequisites.
After completing the prerequisite quest or receiving the letter from Siddgeir, talk to him in order to initiate this quest.
Once you have reached the assigned dungeon, you will only have to kill the bandit leader of that dungeon; killing the lesser enemies is not mandatory, but would make your job easier.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: Return to Siddgeir to collect your reward of gold.

stages.text: Objective 10: Kill the leader of <Alias=BanditCamp>
Objective 15: Return to Siddgeir

notes: Siddgeir is the only Jarl of Falkreath who gives this quest, which is the last prerequisite he requires before starting the Thane of Falkreath quest. If Dengeir is jarl, then he will already consider you a friend, and start that quest without any further prerequisites.
The quest will not be available if you have another "kill the leader" bounty quest active.
The target location and boss are radiantly chosen the first time entering the Falkreath location, usually long before Siddgeir gives the quest.

if you have the concurrent quest Kill Helvard, remember never to turn in the killing bandit quest right after killing Helvard, or you will lose the chance to elevate Jarl's relationshiprank to 2, thus never be able to receive the next quest to become a thane nor be authorized to buy the property Lakeview Manor, the right method is either to turn in the killing bandit quest before killing Helvard, or go somewhere else after killing Helvard, then come back to turn in the killing bandit quest, the reason behind is about relationshiprank, the relationshiprank mechanism is also mentioned in Kill Helvard page.
If you start this quest after Rare Gifts, before you reach level 9 and then get a letter from a courier, a sidequest to see jarl will remain active forever.

If you did not talk to Farengar Secret-Fire during the Bleak Falls Barrow quest yet, you will not get the option to ask the jarl for any jobs, nor will you be able to tell him you got the letter. This will block you from becoming a thane and thus accessing Lakeview Manor until you progress the main quest. If you want to evade starting Dragon Rising to avoid enabling dragons in Skyrim but still want access to Lakeview Manor, you can progress the Bleak Falls Barrow quest to the point where you need to give Farengar the tablet and stop there. This will make Siddgeir give you this quest and you will be able to progress normally to became the thane.

If you start or complete this quest while having a "kill the leader" bounty quest active for the same location, the kill will just act as if you completed that quest, and not credit you for this quest.

quick: Speak to Sybille Stentor.
Kill the Master Vampire in Pinemoon Cave.
Return to Sybille Stentor for your reward.

paragraphs: Speak to Sybille Stentor in the Blue Palace throne room and ask what her problem is. She will tell you about a local nest of vampires which you should wipe out.

Make your way to Pinemoon Cave, west of Solitude. It is a very small cave with only four chambers, and an assortment of vampires and wolves. You only need to kill the Master Vampire to complete the quest. He can be found in the third chamber, a large room with pews facing an altar. The Master Vampire can be found on the altar area. However, he has two companions who will also attack if you are detected. They will reanimate a corpse of a Nord which lies on a table in the southern part of the chamber.

If you do clear out the cave, there is a locked chest next to the altar. Also do not forget the fourth chamber, the sleeping quarters, which contains the Illusion skill book Incident at Necrom and another chest.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: Exit the way you came in and return to Sybille Stentor for your reward, which is jewelry and a single free skill boost in Illusion.

stages.text: Objective 10: Kill the leader of Pinemoon Cave
Objective 15: Tell Sybille the vampire is dead

notes: Because this is a favor quest which affects Sybille's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the Thane of Haafingar quest.

paragraphs: Kjar, ship master of The North Wind currently anchored at the docks in Windhelm, will ask you to hunt down and kill a runaway crew member. The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.1, fixes this bug.

The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.4, fixes this bug.

It can be either the Bandit Leader at Ironback Hideout or Orphan's Tear respectively. You can however, depending on luck, have Noster One-Eye's miscellaneous quest to retrieve his helmet, Ahtar's "Kill The Bandit Leader" and Lights Out! all running concurrently and all objectives are located within Broken Oar Grotto.
Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the thane quest for the quest giver's hold.
The quest Harsh Master can have identical quest objectives.
Version 3.0.1 of the Unofficial Skyrim Patch adds the missing bandit camp keywords to Orphan's Tear and Ironback Hideout, resulting in them also becoming possible targets for this quest.
Brunwulf Free-Winter only gives the quest when he's not a Jarl. However, if Brunwulf gives you the quest and the Empire captures Windhelm later on, you can still finish it after he becomes Jarl.
The Solstheim locations for this quest contain Reavers instead of regular bandits. Your journal will still say "bandit leader", though.
Post completion of the main Dragonborn storyline, Fanari Strong-Voice may not give you the option to "Kill The Bandit Leader" for the Skaal.

If you are sent to Gallows Rock after you have already completed the Companions quest The Silver Hand, then the previously-killed generic Silver Hand members, as well as the unique Krev the Skinner, will all have respawned.

The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.1, addresses this issue. This version makes sure that Krev doesn't respawn, while Version 2.0.9 makes sure that no Silver Hand respawn at all, and that the dungeon will be reset to its original state.

The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.3.3, fixes this bug.

Selecting Linwe's body in the console then typing resurrect will bring him back to life as soon as you resume the game. Killing him again will then count for the quest completion. (Doesn't work if you have already received the favor quest, as resurrecting Linwe—before or after entering the cave—doesn't put the quest arrow back on him and killing him again doesn't complete the quest)

quick: Speak to Serana.
Confront Harkon with Auriel's Bow.
Slay Harkon.

paragraphs: Vampire Side: After obtaining Auriel's Bow, Serana tells you that it is time to confront her father. Head back to Volkihar Keep. Once inside, it is not possible to initiate dialogue with any of the other vampires, who will instead direct you to Lord Harkon. He can be found upstairs in the Volkihar Cathedral, where he awaits you and Serana in his Vampire Lord form. When you confront Lord Harkon, he will begin by insulting you for your disloyalty towards him. When Serana tells him that she will not let herself be sacrificed and that you are on her side, Lord Harkon will give recognition to your persuasive abilities by saying that "This dragon has fangs". He makes a final insult to Valerica, and chides Serana for becoming more like her mother. At this point, Lord Harkon will demand that you give him Auriel's Bow. If you refuse to give it to him, he will attack you. Likewise, if you give him the bow, he will betray you and attack. Because both dialogue options end in him attacking you, it is not recommended to give him Auriel's Bow, as it can be very useful during the battle.

Dawnguard Side: The Dawnguard side of this quest is much like the Vampire side, except that after acquiring the bow, Serana will tell you to head back to Isran. Once at Fort Dawnguard, talk to Isran, who will gather the rest of the Dawnguard. If you chose to become a vampire in order to gain access to the Soul Cairn, Isran will refuse to speak with you until you have been cured. After a short speech, everyone will head out to Castle Volkihar. Once you arrive there, the Dawnguard, including one armored troll, will start the attack on the castle, beginning with four vampires (Rargal Thrallmaster, Modhna, Namasur, and Stalf), a few Gargoyles and one Death hound who defend the outdoor approach to the castle. When they have been defeated, you will then lead the charge into Castle Volkihar, fighting the remaining vampires (Hestla, Salonia Caelia, Fura Bloodmouth, Orthjolf, Vingalmo, Garan Marethi, Ronthil, and Feran Sadri) and the other Death Hound. After all the vampires have been killed, follow Isran to a gated off doorway with a pull chain to the right of it. Pull it to raise the portcullis, then head up the steps and through the doors into the Volkihar Cathedral, where you will find Lord Harkon. Alternatively, you can ignore the vampires inside the castle and go directly to the Cathedral. The conversation with Lord Harkon on the Dawnguard side is somewhat different than the conversation on the Vampire side, mainly in the tone of the conversation and in Lord Harkon's dialogue with the player. Instead of insulting the player for their lack of loyalty, Lord Harkon will admit that it was only a matter of time before Serana would one day return with hatred in her heart. He then questions the player's allegiance to Serana by asking if she and Valerica are next after dealing with him. No matter what dialogue options you choose, Lord Harkon will eventually demand that you give him Auriel's Bow, where you are faced with the same choice. Giving him Auriel's Bow is not recommended for the same reasons listed above.

It might be a good idea to time your assault against Castle Volkihar so that it occurs during the day so you can take advantage of Sunhallowed Arrows used on the sun to help take down the vampires who attack outside. To make sure the assault takes place during the day, you can travel to a nearby location (example: Icewater Jetty), wait until morning (if you arrive there at night), and continue to the castle from there. If you have the Clear Skies shout, you can use it to clear away the clouds and snow to make the vampires who attack outside easier to eliminate.

walkthrough.heading: Fighting Lord Harkon
paragraphs: Fighting Lord Harkon is the same regardless of whether you are a vampire or a member of the Dawnguard. If you are not prepared, Lord Harkon can be a difficult opponent to defeat. If you gave him Auriel's Bow, then you will be at a slight disadvantage. As soon as he exits dialogue with you, Lord Harkon will immediately summon skeletons and gargoyles to kill you, and will continue to do so throughout the fight. However, Serana is quite capable of handling them on her own, which leaves you to focus solely on Lord Harkon. Lord Harkon will continuously move throughout the room, firing Vampiric Drain at you and will frequently turn into a swarm of bats. As you deplete his health, Lord Harkon will turn into a swarm of bats and will materialize at the altar. As he hovers over the altar, he will create an impregnable shield of Blood Magic until he regains his health. If you have Auriel's Bow, equip it and fire at the shield, which will destroy it. Try not to waste Sunhallowed arrows during this fight, as Lord Harkon will do this repeatedly, and any arrow fired from Auriel's Bow will penetrate the shield. When his health is low, he will begin to frequently turn into mist; simply follow him until he re-materializes. Once the killing blow is struck, Lord Harkon will turn into a swarm of bats and materialize by the altar one final time, where he makes a final cry to his daughter's betrayal, and then melts into a pile of red ash. Alternatively, at the beginning of the battle, you will be free to move around when Lord Harkon is speaking to Serana, and you can even slay him outright with high enough sneak-attack damage. Again, Lord Harkon will turn materialize by the altar one final time, where he makes a final cry to his daughter's betrayal, and then melts into a pile of red ash.

After the battle is over, Garan Marethi (if you are a vampire) or Isran (if you are a member of the Dawnguard) will enter the room, and will commend you for defeating Lord Harkon. He will then explain that there will be a new beginning for the Volkihar vampires or the Dawnguard, thus completing the Dawnguard questline. Serana will tell you that she will stay at Castle Volkihar or Fort Dawnguard, but will accompany you on your travels should you ask her.

walkthrough.heading: Aftermath
paragraphs: While you do not corrupt Auriel's Bow bringing it to its full potential, you can still use it to block out the sun once per day with Bloodcursed Elven Arrows. While the sun is blocked out, you will not suffer from any of the penalties of sun damage during the day. After one day, the sun will return and you will need to shoot it again. Bloodcursed arrows are necessary for this function.
A dialogue option with Serana will open up that allows you to turn Elven arrows into Bloodcursed arrows.
The blacksmith associated with your chosen faction will stock an additional 200 Elven arrows, which you can convert into Sunhallowed or Bloodcursed arrows.
Certain Volkihar Clan or Dawnguard side quests will become available.

If you sided with the vampires, Garan Marethi will ask you if you want him to restore the entrance to the courtyard the next time you talk to him. The repair is free, and will be complete the next time you enter the keep.
On the Vampire side, you will be new owner of the castle, and will now be able to take everything for free without being flagged for theft.
On the Dawnguard side, you can ask Serana to transform you into a Vampire Lord or convince her to give up her vampirism.
On Lord Harkon's body you will find one of the sets of Vampire Royal Armor and Harkon's Sword, a unique katana. If you gave him Auriel's Bow, you can retrieve it from there as well.

If you return to the Soul Cairn, Valerica will be amazed at Harkon's defeat and return to Castle Volkihar. She will return to her lab, where she will restock it, and offer potions and ingredients for free. She will also give you advice on how to survive if you return to the Soul Cairn. The garden in the courtyard will be upgraded as well. Unfortunately, she won't provide blood for Bloodcursed Elven Arrows.
Random encounters with members from the opposing faction in hold capitals and the wilderness will be less frequent. Random vampire attacks on settlements will only occur during an eclipse.

walkthrough.heading: Achievements
paragraphs: One achievement is unlocked when you complete this quest:
Kindred Judgement (40 points/Silver)

stages.text: Objective 10: Speak to Serana

With Auriel's Bow in my possession, I need to rally the forces of the Dawnguard before I attempt to confront Harkon and put a stop to the prophecy. Objective 20: Speak to Isran(Available only if Dragonborn are joined in Dawnguard.)

With Auriel's Bow in my possession, it's time to confront Harkon and reshape the prophecy as I see fit. Objective 30: Confront Harkon with Auriel's Bow(Available only if Dragonborn are joined in Volkihar Clan.)
Objective 30: Confront Harkon with Auriel's Bow
Objective 40: Slay Harkon

notes: Killing Lord Harkon is necessary regardless of which faction you side with.

During the battle, the music normally heard when battling dragons will play. If you let the battle go on long enough, one or two tracks of ordinary battle music will play, before being replaced again by Dragon music.
If completed for the Dawnguard, everything in Volkihar Keep will still be labeled as owned and thus stolen if taken. Everyone's corpses, except for Harkon's, will never despawn, even those outside.
It is possible, if the Sneak skill is high enough and with high enough sneak attack damage, to kill Harkon during his dialogue with Serana without any major combat.

If you dual-cast Pacify on the vampires during the Dawnguard version with the Master of the Mind perk active, they won't lower their weapons/spells, but will instead tell you to present Auriel's Bow to Lord Harkon, as if you sided with them. Unfortunately, you won't be able to buy Heal Undead from Ronthil this way.

The Dawnguard version of this quest may appear to freeze when Isran is summoning everybody: they will all stay there in a circle and apparently do nothing. This happens because one of the Dawnguard members has been relocated in some way (such as acting as steward at a homestead), and they are traveling to their spot in the circle. Isran will not start his speech until they arrive; waiting for several hours will allow the missing Dawnguard member to arrive to the meeting more quickly, which will then proceed as intended.
Isran's speech after killing Lord Harkon will mention that the Dawnguard will now dedicate itself to protecting Auriel's Bow, but he never asks for it, and there is no way to give it to him.

Isran's disposition towards Serana will change over the course of the questline, displaying some decently scripted character development. When Serana first arrives in Fort Dawnguard Isran refers to her as an "it" rather than a person, and refuses to even refer to her by her name. This attitude seems to cast Isran in a dark light initially, as the conversation takes place between the player and the other involved characters together in a bloody torture room in Fort Dawnguard. In this quest, when Isran questions whether Serana will be able to commit patricide for the greater good, not only does he refer to her by her actual name, but he even uses the pronouns "she" and "her", suggesting that he has grown to respect Serana for her personal sacrifices made for their cause. With Harkon's defeat at the end of the quest, Isran will completely change his tone and express sincere gratitude towards her. He will even allow her to stay in Fort Dawnguard even if you do not take her as a follower, regardless of her vampire status.

Isran may not give his speech to begin the Dawnguard side of this quest. This is usually caused by the members of the Dawnguard failing to assemble. Taking a Dawnguard member as a follower and leaving them somewhere (or having them join the Blades), or Florentius wandering off or not making it back to the Keep after recruiting him are the most common reasons.

Waiting usually fixes this. You may need to wait 24 hours or longer for everyone to show up, but sometimes waiting in 1-hour increments a few times will allow the speech to proceed even though the missing members are still missing.

You may be unable to enter Volkihar Keep despite the gate being up and the door unlocked. This may be due to having earlier trouble with Bloodline and having used a work-around to progress forward in that quest.

Use the command player.moveto 02003ba8. This will place you inside the keep in a room with a fireplace, with a door that opens to the upstairs level of the main hall where Isran should be found fighting.
When Lord Harkon's health is reduced to zero, he may become invincible, forcing you to reload a previous save from before entering Volkihar Cathedral to begin the fight again.
Save the game and move your character, then reload the game. When it has been reloaded, Harkon's death scene will play.

If that doesn't work, try disabling and re-enabling the Actor through the CC. Make sure you've already saved the game prior to that. It usually results in one ultimate death blow needed to finally bring him down and initiate the death sequence.
Sometimes Lord Harkon will not take any damage from any attacks. Reloading a previous save will fix this. Saving before entering the final room of Castle Volkihar is recommended.

If in stealth mode and unseen by Harkon during his dialogue with Serana, instead of speaking to you he will simply pause. Since you cannot leave the cathedral, the game will essentially be frozen. You have to either be seen by Harkon, which will trigger him to commence his dialogue with your character, or you can attack him. If you attack, you won't get the dialogue options, but the battle will play out normally.

It is best to avoid using dragon shouts during the final battle. All sorts of bugs and collisions can occur, and on the PC, it may freeze or crash to desktop. When transitioning into bat form, hitting Harkon with Unrelenting Force may blast him into the scenery.
If his script is already buggy and you work at it long enough, it is possible to summon Durnehviir into Volkihar Cathedral during the final battle. The game will immediately crash.
Serana may stay locked in combat after Harkon dies, making it so dialogue is unavailable. Attack Serana until she goes down (or exit the room and initiate conversation), and she will speak.
If you exit the room and initiate conversation with Serana, her dialogue will be normal, but the other NPC may leave and you will lose the chance to speak to Isran or Garan.
After entering Volkihar Cathedral to confront Lord Harkon, the Vampire Lord and the Revert Form powers no longer function.
To fix this issue, open up the console, select your character (by clicking on it or typing prid 14) and type resurrect.

Sometimes after you've used Auriel's Bow, it can cause your weapons to malfunction, resulting in you not being able to use them. This prevents you from being able to attack with either weapons or magic. Reloading the latest saved game or transforming into a werewolf will fix this.
This quest will not start on the Vampire side if either of the two hireable Death hounds have been killed and their bodies have been removed from the game.
The Official Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 1.6.1130.0, fixes this bug.
You can start the quest manually using setstage DLC1VQ08 10.
The bodies of the Volkihar vampires are never cleaned up once this quest is completed on the Dawnguard side.
The Unofficial Dawnguard Patch, version 2.0.0, fixes this bug.
If the armored troll survives, it never disappears from the castle once this quest is completed on the Dawnguard side.
The Unofficial Dawnguard Patch, version 2.0.9, fixes this bug.
This quest can stall on the Vampire side if Stalf and/or Salonia Caelia have been dead long enough for their bodies to be removed from the game, even though you killed them yourself a long time ago.
The Unofficial Dawnguard Patch, version 2.1.0, fixes this bug.
After defeating Harkon, you may be unable to interact with Isran. You may interact normally with him back in Fort Dawnguard.
The chest found after defeating Harkon may remain empty.
Sometimes (very rarely) the Volkihar Cathedral Boss Room will not load after defeating all vampires in the Volkihar Keep
On PC this can be fixed using console command coc DLC1VampireCastleBossRoom

You may sell the two Elder Scrolls to Dexion Evicus for 6000 gold after completing this quest, but only if allied with the Dawnguard. Since they will always remain quest items, this is the only way to remove them from the inventory.
The Unofficial Dawnguard Patch, version 1.2.2, addresses this issue. (details) It adds the necessary dialogue in order to sell them while sided with the vampires.
Gunmar and Sorine deliver their post quest greetings more than once due to the lack of a "say once" flag even though this isn't an issue with Isran.
The Unofficial Dawnguard Patch, version 2.1.3, addresses this issue. Tracking variables have been added to prevent Gunmar and Sorine from doing so. It is unknown why they weren't added to it as well.
Agmaer, Beleval and Ingjard may be absent during the assault on Castle Volkihar in the Dawnguard version.

The Unofficial Skyrim Legendary Edition Patch, version 3.0.1, addresses this issue. They never got the packages added to their aliases in the quest even though all of the markers, packages, and other conditions had been set up for them.
Celann may be given 15 crossbows in his inventory, which is clearly an error as it was a copypasta matching the amount of steel bolts he's given.
The Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 4.3.7, fixes this bug.

quick: (Optional) Read Ahzidal's Descent.
Investigate Kolbjorn Barrow and speak to Ralis Sedarys.
Agree to help Ralis fund his excavation by donating 1,000 gold and wait for a message from him.
Visit Kolbjorn Barrow and defeat the draugr.
Find a way deeper into the barrow, and then speak to Ralis again.
Donate 2,000 gold to fund the excavation of Kolbjorn Barrow and wait for another message from Ralis.
Return to Kolbjorn Barrow, clear the draugr, and search for missing miners.
Speak to Ralis, fund 3,000 gold to his excavation, and await another message.
Return to Kolbjorn Barrow and clear the draugr.
Speak to Ralis, fund 5,000 gold to his excavation, and await another message.
Return to Kolbjorn Barrow and locate Ralis.
Defeat Ahzidal and confront Ralis; decide what to do with him.

walkthrough.heading: A Strange Partnership
paragraphs: Just northeast of the Old Attius Farm is Kolbjorn Barrow. Outside Kolbjorn Barrow is a lone Dunmer named Ralis Sedarys. Go up and talk to him and he'll explain that he is a treasure hunter and has come with news that he has located a treasure in the barrow, but he cannot afford to excavate it alone and requests a donation of 1,000 gold, with a promise of a share of any treasure discovered.

walkthrough.heading: First Visit
paragraphs: A few days after you give him the money, a courier will give you a note about the barrow. Head off over to the barrow, and Ralis will explain that the draugr have been disturbed, and they have killed all the miners. He asks you to go in and kill the draugr and then find a way further into the barrow. After you have killed the draugr, take the Skull off the altar to open the next area, Go into the next room and pick up the Ahzidal's Boots of Waterwalking. (If the skull has been knocked off the pressure plate on the altar during the fight it must be lifted back onto the plinth and removed once more, or you can "walk" onto it and off by getting on the altar). Go back and talk to Ralis. He'll then ask for 2,000 gold to hire some more miners.

walkthrough.heading: Second Visit
paragraphs: Several days afterward you'll get another note asking you to come back to the barrow. There are more draugr and two of the miners are missing. He asks that you locate the missing miners and to kill the remaining draugr. Before you get to Mireli, there is a gate with 4 handles arranged vertically to the right of the gate. Do not pull the third (from the top), as it releases a dart trap. Pull the switches in the following order: first, second, fourth, first. In the last section of the mine near the corpse of Mireli is a handle (near the floor on the other side of the wall with candles, a soul gem and coins) that can be turned to reveal a secret room where Ahzidal's Ring of Necromancy can be found. Note that although you will hear the sounds of a nearby word wall, it will not be accessible until a later visit.
Ralis now wants 3,000 gold to hire some mercenaries.

walkthrough.heading: Third Visit
paragraphs: You will receive a third letter a few days later, asking you to return to the barrow. When the courier delivers the letter, he will tell you "Another letter from Ralis. He's starting to scare me a little", a portent of things to come. Ralis will tell a similar story as last time: that there are yet more draugr, and that this time they have killed all the mercenaries that he hired. Enter the barrow and kill the draugr. To access Ahzidal's Gauntlets of Warding, pull the chain to the right of the iron doors that lead to the staircase into the newly excavated section, then backtrack around the corner where they will be sitting on a pedestal that was previously unavailable. Then, head down the stairs, avoiding the trap, and kill the new draugr. When you reach the open chamber, you must ensure all the pressure plates are lit for the gate to open and reach Ahzidal's Ring of Arcana. (The Light Foot perk does not prevent you from lighting the pressure plates.) The timing is a bit tight; if you can't get it, using Slow Time seems to work, or you can run along the joint between two rows of tiles, depressing both rows at once, for a total of three runs across the grid. You can also circumvent the puzzle entirely with Telekinesis. A pit filled with deep water surrounds the plinth that the ring is on. At the bottom you can find a coin purse, a burial urn and a leveled battleaxe. Once you're done here, head up the stairs and back out of the barrow to talk to Ralis who now wants 5,000 more gold. He will then send you one last note, which simply reads "You're needed."

walkthrough.heading: A Poor Investment
paragraphs: When you get the final note, return to the barrow and look for clues at the camp, then head into the barrow and clear it out. You are finally able to reach the word wall which teaches a word for the Cyclone shout. On reaching the room with all the pressure plates on the floor, follow the passage to the left. A gate will close behind you will have to fight three draugr. The gate blocking access to Ahzidal's Armor of Retribution can be opened by rotating the two animal totem pillars until the whale symbols are facing you, then pulling the lever on the floor. Rotate the two animal totem pillars until the eagle symbols are facing you and pull the lever on the floor again to open the gate you came in, and the gate over the spiral staircase. At the bottom of the staircase, the gate blocking access to Ahzidal's Helm of Vision can be opened by rotating the two animal totem pillars until the snake symbols are facing you, then pulling the chain next to the door. There is a giant pool of oil encompassing almost the entire room, so it is recommended that you intentionally ignite it safely from the staircase as pulling the chain with an incorrect pillar arrangement will cause several flame spout traps to blast the area in front of the gate. Removing the helm from its pedestal will activate another flame spout trap that is aimed back towards the gate. You may use Telekinesis again, but the flame jet will still travel far enough to ignite the oil. There is a Stalhrim source to the left of the helm chamber.

After battling several leveled draugr, you will eventually find Ralis completing the ritual to awaken a dragon priest named Ahzidal. Defeat Ahzidal, loot his eponymous mask, then speak to Ralis, who will explain that he was under a spell. You can then choose to kill him or let him live, in which case he will become available as a follower. If you kill him, you may loot Hoarfrost, a unique ancient Nordic pickaxe, from his corpse. You can also take it from him if you spare him.
You can find the Black Book Filament and Filigree at the end of the exit tunnel.

stages.text: Outside Kolbjorn Barrow, I met Ralis Sedarys, an explorer who came to Solstheim in search of relics within the barrow. But when he arrived, he found it buried by the ash. He had all but given up on excavating it, but if I can supply the funds, he offered to make me a partner in his expedition. Objective 40: Fund the excavation of Kolbjorn Barrow (1000 gold)

Ralis Sedarys came to Solstheim in search of the Relics of Ahzidal, powerful items said to have been sealed in Kolbjorn Barrow, but found it buried by ash. I agreed to fund his expedition to excavate the Barrow. He set to work, saying he'd send a courier when he had progress to report. Objective 75: Wait for a message from Ralis
I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' expedition to excavate Kolbjorn Barrow. I should visit the site and see how the work is going. Objective 100: Visit the Kolbjorn Barrow Excavation

I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' expedition to excavate Kolbjorn Barrow, but work on the dig has come to a halt. The excavation had reached a dead end when Draugr within the tomb awoke, killing several miners and causing the rest to flee. Objective 130: Clear the Draugr from Kolbjorn Barrow Objective 140: Find a way deeper into the Barrow

I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' expedition to excavate Kolbjorn Barrow, but work on the dig has come to a halt. The excavation had reached a dead end when Draugr within the tomb awoke, killing several miners and causing the rest to flee. I defeated the Draugr, but now need to find a way past the dead end.

I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' expedition to excavate Kolbjorn Barrow, but work on the dig has come to a halt. The excavation had reached a dead end when Draugr within the tomb awoke, killing several miners and causing the rest to flee. I found a way past the dead end, but must deal with the Draugr before work can continue.

I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' expedition to excavate Kolbjorn Barrow, but work on the dig has come to a halt. At his request, I defeated the Draugr and found a way past the dead end. Objective 150: Speak to Ralis

I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' expedition to excavate Kolbjorn Barrow, but in order to continue, he needs more gold to hire replacements for the workers that have been killed. Objective 160: Fund the next phase of the excavation (2000 gold)
I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' expedition to excavate Kolbjorn Barrow. He told me to return in a few days to see how work was progressing. Objective 175: Wait for a message from Ralis
I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' expedition to excavate Kolbjorn Barrow. I should return and see how the work is going. Objective 200: Return to Kolbjorn Barrow

I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' expedition to excavate Kolbjorn Barrow, but work on the site has stopped. Most of the miners were killed by another wave of Draugr attacks, and two more are unaccounted for. Objective 230: Clear the Draugr from Kolbjorn Barrow Objective 240: Search for the missing miners

I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' expedition to excavate Kolbjorn Barrow, but work on the site has stopped. Most of the miners were killed by another wave of Draugr attacks, and two more are unaccounted for. I dealt with the Draugr, but still need to locate the missing miners.

I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' expedition to excavate Kolbjorn Barrow, but work on the site has stopped. Most of the miners were killed by another wave of Draugr attacks, and two more were unaccounted for. I found the bodies of the missing miners, but still need to deal with the Draugr threat.

I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' expedition to excavate Kolbjorn Barrow, but work on the site has stopped. At his request, I dealt with the Draugr and found the bodies of the missing miners. Objective 250: Speak to Ralis

I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' expedition to excavate Kolbjorn Barrow, but the ongoing Draugr attacks means he needs more gold in order to hire more miners and guards to protect them. Objective 260: Fund the next phase of the excavation (3000 gold)
I agreed to continue funding Ralis Sedarys' excavation of Kolbjorn Barrow. He told me to return in a few days to see how work was progressing. Objective 275: Wait for a message from Ralis
I agreed to continue funding Ralis Sedarys' excavation of Kolbjorn Barrow. I should return and see how the work is going. Objective 300: Return to Kolbjorn Barrow

I agreed to continue funding Ralis Sedarys' excavation of Kolbjorn Barrow, but Draugr have attacked the miners again, and only a few managed to escape. Ralis asked if I could wipe them out so the excavation could continue. Objective 330: Clear the Draugr from Kolbjorn Barrow
I agreed to continue funding Ralis Sedarys' excavation of Kolbjorn Barrow, but Draugr again attacked the miners. Once again, I slew the Draugr so work could proceed. Objective 350: Speak to Ralis

I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' expedition to excavate Kolbjorn Barrow, but once again, he needs more gold to hire increasingly reluctant miners and guards to work on the site. Objective 360: Fund the next phase of the excavation (5000 gold)
I agreed to continue funding Ralis Sedarys' excavation of Kolbjorn Barrow. He told me to return in a few days to see how work was progressing. Objective 375: Wait for a message from Ralis
I agreed to continue funding Ralis Sedarys' excavation of Kolbjorn Barrow. I should return and see how the work is going. Objective 400: Return to Kolbjorn Barrow

I agreed to continue funding Ralis Sedarys' ill-fated excavation of Kolbjorn Barrow, but when I returned to his mining camp, I found only blood and corpses. Ralis himself was nowhere to be seen. Objective 410: Locate Ralis

I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' ill-fated excavation of Kolbjorn Barrow, but when I returned to his mining camp, I found only blood and corpses. Deep within the barrow, I found Ralis performing a ritual to release Ahzidal, the Dragon Priest that had been sealed there.
Objective 450: Defeat Ahzidal

I agreed to fund Ralis Sedarys' ill-fated excavation of Kolbjorn Barrow, but when I returned to his mining camp, I found only blood and corpses. Deep within the barrow, I found Ralis performing a ritual that released Ahzidal, a powerful Dragon Priest I fought and defeated. Objective 475: Confront Ralis

Ralis Sedarys came to Solstheim hoping to find the Relics of Ahzidal and release their maker from his imprisonment in Kolbjorn Barrow. When he found the barrow buried by the ash, he convinced me to fund its excavation, using the miners as blood sacrifices for his rituals. I saw through his lies and decided to kill him for his crimes. Objective 480: Kill Ralis

Ralis Sedarys came to Solstheim hoping to find the Relics of Ahzidal and release their maker from his imprisonment in Kolbjorn Barrow. When he found the barrow buried by the ash, he convinced me to fund its excavation, using the miners as blood sacrifices for his rituals. I saw through his lies and killed him for his crimes.

Ralis Sedarys came to Solstheim hoping to find the Relics of Ahzidal, but fell under the spell of their maker, a powerful Dragon Priest entombed in the barrow. He convinced me to fund its excavation, but was compelled by Ahzidal to use the miners as ritual sacrifices. Ralis had no control over his actions, so I allowed him to live and depart the barrow in peace.
Objective 10: Speak to Ralis Sedarys at Kolbjorn Barrow
Objective 20: Investigate Kolbjorn Barrow

notes: In total you will require 11,000 gold to complete the excavation.
The time between each investment and the next courier message is three full days (72 hours).
If you visit between messages, there will be miners and possibly guards working. They have generic dialogue reflecting the current state of the quest.

Throughout the quest, a series of journals can be found, giving insight into Ralis' state of mind. Take care when reading them as the disappearance of the camp will not occur if you take his journals from the camp prior to the final condition. They may also be stuck in your inventory permanently if you do so. The disappearance condition is that Filament and Filigree is read and Ahzidal is obtained, the two actions' order doesn't matter.
You can find Ahzidal's unique heavy armor set and rings:
Ahzidal's Boots of Waterwalking are available after the first phase of digging.
Ahzidal's Ring of Necromancy may be found after the second phase.
Ahzidal's Gauntlets of Warding and Ahzidal's Ring of Arcana can be acquired after the third phase.
Ahzidal's Armor of Retribution and Ahzidal's Helm of Vision become available after the fourth phase.

The Ring of Arcana may not be on its plinth when you get to it—shouts from the draugr in the adjacent chamber can knock it into the pit of water. If this occurs, equipping the Telekinesis spell can help you locate it (due to its longer range compared to the standard cursor).

You may hear the chanting of the nearby word wall after the second phase has occurred, but you won't be able to access it until the fourth phase. You might be able to access it during the third phase if you stand close enough to the wall.

The grate that opens to allow you to descend to meet Ahzidal on your final visit is controlled by the familiar pillars and is well-marked. The eagles on the opposite wall must be set on the corresponding pillars.

The iron gate blocking the pedestal that holds Ahzidal's Armor of Retribution is not so obvious, however. As you enter the room, on the walls to either side there will be pull chains just to the right of an arch-way. If you pull the chains, this will activate rotating doors which will reveal that behind the arch-ways are two more pillars, each with the sign of the fish. The pillars behind the chairs need to be matched to these to open the gate and obtain the armor. Setting both pillars to the Eagle (and activating the lever) will open the door downstairs. The pillars here perform an uncharacteristic double-duty by opening two separate portals.
The fastest way to complete this quest would be to commit a murder, and serve the jail time rather than pay a bounty. This will cause seven in game days to pass each time, allowing quick completion.

Ralis may hire the miners, but never get anywhere with them - despite the passage of days (or even months), the courier never arrives, and when you check the dig site, they haven't reached the entrance.
Check the site once, talk to Ralis, then sleep in a bed on Solstheim for 24 or 48 hours. Repeat for each stage.
If the courier never arrives with Ralis' letters, you can bring him to you by bringing up the console, and typing and entering prid 00039FB7 .
Then type and enter moveto player
Finally, you can talk to the courier to trigger his letter delivery dialogue.

Upon entering Kolbjorn Barrow for the second time, the door by Mireli might drop down prematurely and lock you out of the room instead of locking down your retreat. Manually reopening the door will not help as it will just become an invisible barrier blocking your entrance. To reach Mireli and complete the quest, go back to the big hollow room and jump onto the platform. Alternatively, reload to a save before having entered the barrow for a second time.

Upon entering Kolbjorn Barrow for the fourth and final time, you are instructed to find Ralis Sedarys (stage 410). At some point before reaching the chamber with Ralis and Ahzidal, the quest may immediately progress to confronting Ralis (stage 475). It is possible that Ralis will be flagged as hostile towards the draugr and Ahzidal (or vice versa), and a brawl will ensue before you reach the chamber. Since Ralis is considered an essential NPC until you choose the dialogue option to kill him, upon reaching the chamber you will find Ralis chanting, as if to summon Ahzidal, but Ahzidal and the draugr are already dead. Approaching Ralis will trigger the normal dialogue (choose to kill or spare him). If he is spared, he will continue chanting as he runs away. He will still be chanting when approached at The Retching Netch.

Once you finish the quest, the excavation site is supposed to clear up once you're far enough away. However, the script controlling this incorrectly polls the alias on Ralis when it should have been polling a static object at the site. This can result in the possibility that the registered update would fail to be renewed, leaving the quest open forever.
The Unofficial Dragonborn Patch, version 2.0.3, fixes this bug.

Ralis' journals can be found on a table outside of the barrow excavation. Taking them after completion of the quest will permanently mark them as quest items, and it will be impossible to ever remove them from your inventory.
The Unofficial Dragonborn Patch, version 2.0.3, fixes this bug.
You can remove the journals from your inventory by storing them in Ahzidal's ash pile, but they will still be marked as quest items.

They may be removed via the console by typing Player.removeitem xx018108 1 and repeating for the IDs xx01810F, xx018110, xx018111, and xx0181CB. The xx on each ID will vary; see this page for details.

Ralis' journals can also be permanently marked as quest items if you complete the quest and leave the barrow without collecting the Black Book. This glitch actually seems to depend on the passage of time. Completing the Black Book quickly may cause the glitch to not be fixed. Waiting a few extra hours before leaving the dungeon should fix it.
Upon entering Kolbjorn Barrow for the third time, one of the draugr that you must kill may be outside of the map.
Leaving and reentering Kolbjorn should fix this issue.

If you haven't picked up Ahzidal's Ring of Necromancy yet during the 2nd investment, it will disappear during the 3rd investment if you try to go back and grab it. It can be retrieved if you return to barrow after the third investment but before receiving the next letter.
If Ahzidal is killed as he rises from the ground, his corpse and ash pile may be below the ground and not lootable.

Upon entering Kolbjorn Barrow for the fourth time, the doorway leading to the lower section of the tomb may be blocked by rubble. Though this rubble can be walked through, as it has no collision, it can make it difficult to find where to go.
At the second phase, you may find the third phase area accessible instead of being sealed off, allowing you to get Ahzidal's Gauntlets of Warding and the Ring of Arcana early.
All of the generic miners present, both male and female, have "opposite gender animations" marked.

quick: Talk to either Pavo Attius or Skaggi Scar-Face.
Clear out Kolskeggr Mine.
Claim your reward.

walkthrough.heading: Two Survivors
paragraphs: Upon arriving at Left Hand Mine outside of Markarth, you may overhear a discussion between Skaggi Scar-Face, who is in charge of the mine, and Pavo Attius. Pavo and his fellow miner Gat gro-Shargakh are the only survivors of a Forsworn invasion of Kolskeggr Mine. Skaggi is visibly upset by this news; he gives the two survivors permission to stay at Left Hand Mine, and vows to send word to the Jarl. If you speak with Skaggi, he expresses his concern over the increasing Forsworn threat and the timeliness of a response from the Jarl. If you agree to clear out the mine, he will be grateful, but skeptical about your ability to survive. Speaking with Pavo will also initiate the quest and he will also offer the same sentiments about the Jarl's response and your success in the mine. The quest may not start and dialogue options may not be available if The Forsworn Conspiracy is not completed and your bounty in Markarth is high.

Make your way to the mine, which will be marked on your map if you haven't previously discovered it. Several Forsworn will be standing guard at the mine's entrance, with more inside. Once you've killed them all, head back to Left Hand Mine.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: Speak to Pavo with the news of your success. He will be suitably impressed at your accomplishment and reward you with a leveled amount of gold. He and Gat then return to work at Kolskeggr Mine.

stages.text: Objective 10: Clear the Forsworn from Kolskeggr Mine
Objective 20: Tell Pavo that Kolskeggr Mine is cleared

notes: Once Pavo returns to Kolskeggr Mine, he will offer to buy gold ore from you. His services are of limited use, however (see bugs below).

Even after fulfilling the quest and letting the miners reclaim control of Kolskeggr Mine, the Forsworn will respawn the next time you visit the cell. They will kill the miners off if you aren't quick enough. It's possible to save them; just make sure that you quickly dispatch the two Forsworn near the bridge. The miners and a guard will easily dispatch the one at the top.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2.4, fixes this bug.
You may be able to repeat this quest when the Forsworn there respawn, as long as you stay away from Kolskeggr Mine and avoid triggering the event in which the miners try to reclaim control.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.1, fixes this bug.
Pavo stays inside the barracks, and will not talk as you are trespassing.
The Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 4.1.8, addresses this issue. After the quest is completed, he will sandbox outside 12 hours per day.
Stronghold Orcs may fail to recognize you as Blood-Kin after completing this quest.
