It was a trap! The Emperor was actually Titus Mede II's double, and Commander Maro said I had been betrayed by someone within the Dark Brotherhood. Despite his deal, Maro has sent troops to destroy the Sanctuary. I must return there and help my Family! Objective 70: Return to the Sanctuary

After learning the Emperor was actually Titus Mede II's double, and being confronted by Commander Maro, I learned Maro had betrayed the betrayer, and sent troops to destroy the Dark Brotherhood Sanctuary. I returned there, to lend aid to my fellow Family members.

notes: The stew's name, Potage Le Magnifique, means "the magnificent soup" in French.
If you look inside the soup pot while Gianna delivers it to the Emperor, you will see an empty pot.
You will be blamed for the emperor's death even if you kill him in a stealthy way that would normally avoid incurring a bounty.
Two Penitus Oculatus Agents outside Castle Dour are never disabled after you finish the quest.
The fact that Gianna is surprised and disappointed when you present yourself as the Gourmet if you're an Orc is ironic, as the real Gourmet was an Orc.

In Anniversary Edition or Special Edition with The Gray Cowl Returns! Creation installed. It is possible to use the Gray Cowl of Nocturnal to avoid the bounty from the Solitude Guards. Wearing the cowl during the bridge encounter allows you to kill members of the Penitus Oculatus with no bounty. Guards are not hostile when you remove the cowl afterwards but members of the Penitus Oculatus might still remain hostile. Scripted bounty for murder goes to the Gray Cowl. When the headpiece is taken off, guards will have no suspicion on the Dragonborn.
Without Creation Club content, it's still possible to finish the quest without ever incurring any bounty (or other negative side effects), by utilizing glitches.

After exiting the dining room, glitch through or over the wall of the bridge, to avoid triggering the encounter with Maro. After finishing the quest, plan a marriage and re-visit the bridge. Your character will get stuck around the spot where the Maro encounter would have triggered. By in-game waiting until you miss your wedding ceremony, you'll re-gain control over your character.

This alternate method may also work : After exiting the dining room, cast a Destruction spell with a large area of effect (e.g. Fireball) a couple of times in both the upper and lower doors across the bridge, and slowly walk across. You'll be stopped as if Maro was talking, but you'll quickly exit back out, not getting attacked by the Penitus Oculatus or getting the bounty. You can then easily leave. As long as you don't kill the men you won't get a bounty. You will need to leave the city by foot as the guards are scripted to be hostile, which prevents fast-travel. Killing any single Solitude guard undetected may remove the bounty.
If you wait before entering the Emperor's Tower, you can overhear a conversation between two Penitus Oculatus agents:
Penitus Oculatus Agent 1: "The city is crawling with Imperial Legion, and you know what? I'm still nervous."
Penitus Oculatus Agent 2: "Lazy and useless, the lot of them. They can't even keep the Stormcloaks in line. No way I trust them with the Emperor's life."
Penitus Oculatus Agent 1: "You worry too much. The Emperor's never been safer. You think assassination attempts are planned overnight? We discovered the plot. End of story."
Penitus Oculatus Agent 2: "I suppose. But what about the old man? Son killed, family name ruined...and he acts as if nothing even happened. Think's he's even fit for duty?"
Penitus Oculatus Agent 1: "I'm going to pretend I didn't hear that. Commander Maro is the best that the Penitus Oculatus ever produced. You should be half the man he is."
Penitus Oculatus Agent 2: "You misunderstand. Its just...I feel for him, is all. To carry a weight like that. It's got to take its toll. That happened to me, I'd be a wreck."

Before being confronted by Maro on the bridge, you can use Whirlwind Sprint just before he appears to move freely while he is speaking. Attacking the guards before they turn hostile normally will cause Maro to vanish, and the guards will attack as normal. Note that you need to use all three words, otherwise you'll freeze in place like normal, and be forced to listen to Maro's speech.

If you do get a bounty, then as long as the three Penitus Oculatus men are dead, you can remove the bounty using your Thane status or Thieves Guild association (provided you have them available). However, even if you are a Thane of Haafingar, you will not be able to remove your bounty using your Thane status if Solitude is still under Imperial rule.

After escaping from Maro's men and exiting the tower, while battling Penitus Oculatus agents outside, a Solitude guard may approach you and demand you either pay your bounty or go to prison. If the prison option is chosen, the Penitus Oculatus agents will have disappeared from Solitude by the time your character is set free.

The prison option will prevent you from being killed and also avoids paying the bounty, at the cost of the time in prison with its negative effect on experience. Alternatively, you can pay the bounty, which allows free escape from the city, though any followers (including thralls) may still attack the guards if they were attacked first.
You should remove all items you own or want from the sanctuary before completing this quest, or they may be lost. However, the Unusual Gem located in Astrid's room will still be available.

Maro will have different dialogue based on your equipment when you arrive. If you are wearing a Chef's Hat or Chef's Tunic, he will say "Your clothes... of course... I should have realized..." Otherwise, he tells you "You are not dressed as I had expected." Regardless, he allows you to pass.
If you are in the form of a werewolf or vampire lord while crossing the bridge, you'll automatically change back when Maro appears.

The room in the tower that Maro walks out from is completely empty, and does not even contain stairs or any other means of leaving it. He just appears before his speech is given, and disappears when he leaves behind the wall. You can get to it by using Whirlwind Sprint near the highest point of the bridge, though if Gaius Maro is still there, he will default to common dialogue and you cannot damage him.

After the quest, the Emperor's Tower will still be freely accessible, both from the walkway escape exit and from the front door inside the castle courtyard. However, the door to the dining hall will be permanently locked from both sides. The tower is completely abandoned after this point, so you can take what you want without consequence. Be aware that the whole place respawns, however, so it cannot be safely used as a house.
If you are a member of the Stormcloaks and Solitude is the last city left to be taken, Ulfric and Galmar Stone-Fist won't start the assault yet due to the Emperor's presence.

After you tell Gianna to add the jarrin root to the recipe, if you quickly enter your menu you can drop it from your inventory; this allows you to retrieve it later. The quest will continue and the Emperor will still die of poisoning.
According to the recipe that exists in the game, carrots are a part of the "basic broth" that Gianna has already prepared. Yet, she will not object or even mention it if you suggest to add carrots.
Gianna may not talk to you if you are inflicted with certain diseases.
The Official Skyrim Patch, version 1.1, fixes this bug.
This quest may not start on completion of Recipe for Disaster.

Setting the stage through console does not work, as the stage always remains 0. The cause of the bug is currently unknown, and the easiest way to overcome it is to skip the quest entirely. To do this, move to a location away from the Dark Brotherhood Sanctuary, and use the console commands completequest db09 followed by setstage db10 10. This immediately starts you on the following quest.

The guards who arrive with Commander Maro may either remain there if you snuck past without killing them, or respawn if you did kill them. They stand still and scowl at you, and will never attack, though they do appear as red dots on the compass if you come near the sky bridge and prevent fast travel like any other enemy. You can kill them without incurring any additional bounties, and they will not fight back. If you have an aggressive follower with you, your follower may attack them; they still will not fight back.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.2.4, fixes this bug.

Their reference numbers are 643D4, 643D5 and 643D6. The problem can be fixed on the PC by entering the console (press "~") and typing prid 643D4 followed by disable, and then repeating for the other two numbers.

Looting the Emperor's dead body seems to cause a glitch where the world incorrectly loads and you travel on the land under the buildings' foundations, causing the quest to become stuck on "Escape from the tower".
To fix this, load from the previous autosave before cooking the Emperor's last meal, and do not loot the Emperor's dead body.
You can get around this on Special Edition if you pickpocket his robes off while he's still alive (requires associated pickpocket perks).

If you have a follower, you can ask them to stand in the way of the conversation between you and the cook; they may interrupt your conversation. This also happens if guards are chasing you after you clear Commander Maro but before you enter the Castle Dour.
To fix this, simply reload the last save.
After you finish the quest, the items stored in the containers in the sanctuary may disappear.

quick: Speak to Tolfdir.
Hunt down his missing alembic in the College.
Return to Tolfdir.

walkthrough.heading: Good Old Tolfdir
paragraphs: Tolfdir is an elderly mage and professor at the College of Winterhold and one of the first people encountered at the college. When you have completed Under Saarthal and have begun Hitting the Books Tolfdir will be residing at the college. If you run across him looking confused, ask him if he needs help.

walkthrough.heading: Tolfdir's Alembic
paragraphs: Embarrassed, Tolfdir will admit to misplacing his alembic. And, while he could indeed use a different one, he has a strange sentimental attachment to this particular piece of equipment. Help the professor out by finding this lost item. The alembic will appear in one of three randomly-selected locations in the Hall of Countenance:
On the top floor: in the northern room, on top of a barrel to the right of the central dining bench.
On the top floor: underneath the left display case in the enchanting room.
On the bottom floor: on a crate in the eastern room, with the big barrel in it.

However, even without the quest being activated, you will run across the alembic numerous times in your wanderings about the college. Simply return the alembic to Tolfdir when you speak to him, and earn the reward each time. Tolfdir will give you thirty gold and an empty petty, lesser or common soul gem for returning his misplaced property.

stages.text: ;player has accepted quest

notes: Finding Tolfdir's Alembic before triggering the quest will not change the quest dialogue or outcome; you can simply start the quest and give the alembic to Tolfdir to receive your reward.

Unlike previous titles where alembics were a major part of Alchemy, this is the only individual alembic that can be found in the base Skyrim game. The Farming creation adds a second one in the basement of Goldenhills Plantation. All other alembics in the game are permanently attached to alchemy stations.
Sometimes, the alembic will get dislodged from its normal location, possibly falling behind other objects or onto the ground nearby.
Version 1.0 of the Unofficial Skyrim Patch adds journal objectives to this quest.

Tolfdir may offer the dialogue option that initiates the quest after it has already been completed. Selecting this option will re-add the quest to your journal, but the Alembic will not respawn, leaving the objective permanently stuck in your journal.
Entering the console command player.additem "00026c31" 1 to give yourself a second alembic will allow you to complete the quest by speaking to Tolfdir as normal.

quick: Travel to the indicated location on your map.
Retrieve the Totem by any means necessary.
Return to the Underforge, then use one of the totem receptacles to complete the quest and receive your reward.

walkthrough.heading: Accepting the Quest
paragraphs: Asking Aela the Huntress, "Is there any work to be done?" will prompt her to tell you about the Totems of Hircine. She will say that she has located one and would be honored if you go with her to retrieve it. If you accept the quest, she will become your Shield-Sister and will replace your current companion.

walkthrough.heading: Retrieve the Totem of Hircine
paragraphs: Journey to the location given by Aela and kill the enemies lurking around. The location is radiant, and it can be any animal den, vampire lair, or warlock lair with a boss chest. The totem is most often found in the boss chest. Once you have the totem, Aela will approach and ask if you have it. When you tell her you do, she will tell you to bring it back to the Underforge. When you return to the Underforge, place the totem on the marked area—the quest will finish and you will receive a leveled amount of gold. You can now pray to the totem to receive a new power while in Beast Form, which replaces your old one.
There are three total totems, each granting a different ability in Beast Form.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: The Unofficial Skyrim Legendary Edition Patch, version 3.0.3, fixes this bug. (details)

walkthrough.heading: The Totems of Hircine
paragraphs: The totems are described in detail in the tome, The Totems of Hircine. By praying to these totems, you will be given a unique ability that replaces the older Howl of Terror; it is activated by pressing the shout button while in beast form. All abilities last for 60 seconds, though the duration can be increased by 15 seconds by equipping the Ring of the Moon before activating Beast Mode.
Totem of Fear: Causes Fear
Totem of Brotherhood: Summons 2 Pack Members
Totem of The Hunt: Grants Detect Life

stages.text: Aela has tracked one of the Totems of Hircine to <Alias=Dungeon>, and has come with me to retrieve it. Objective 10: Retrieve the Totem of Hircine
Aela and I retrieved a Totem of Hircine from <Alias=Dungeon>. Objective 20: Take the Totem to the Underforge

notes: If Dragonborn is installed, some radiant locations may be on Solstheim. If you are in Skyrim, you will not receive a quest marker pointing you to the quest location, but must travel to Solstheim first (at which point any quest markers you have to quests in Skyrim will disappear).

The location you are sent to may be an already "cleared" location, even if there are other non-cleared locations of the same type yet to be cleared or even discovered: the game does not, in this case, appear to prioritize new locations over known locations.
You can only trigger this quest if you are still a werewolf. If you have purified yourself, you are unable to do this quest.
If Whiterun is under attack, you cannot enter the Underforge until Whiterun is back to normal. It will tell you a key is needed to enter and that it cannot be lockpicked.

At the end of this quest, Aela will begin praying to the new totem in the Underforge. It is possible to ask her to follow you while she is praying; her dialogue will change, and she will allow you access to her inventory, but will not stop praying or move away from the totem.
Aela will not give these quests while she is an active follower, though she will give Animal Extermination quests.

As you and Aela recover each totem, once she tells you to return the totem to the Underforge, speaking to her will only cause her to say "This is not the time for talk. Let's get to the Underforge and see what this can do." You also won't be able to ask her for training in Archery until then.

If you have just dropped off a totem in the Underforge, Aela will be praying to it and only offer an Animal Extermination quest (dialogue option, "I'm looking for work"). Leave the Underforge, return, then talk to Aela again. Repeat until Aela (still in prayer) offers the next totem quest (dialogue, "Is there any work to be done?").

This quest is considered by the game as 1 even if it appears 3 times in the journal (once for each totem). This means that the counter for "Quests Completed" and "The Companions Quests Completed" will permanently increase by 1 only by the end of the third quest (it appears as increased by 1 every time you complete one of the three quests, but it will drop back in a few in-game cell loadings).
Although you receive the message that she has replaced your current follower, Aela might not replace them but instead join as a secondary follower, lacking the standard follower dialogue options.
This bug was observed with Serana (after completion of Kindred Judgment and cured of vampirism) as primary follower, so it may be due to an interaction with her unique framework.

If you've completed A Daedra's Best Friend, you may be taken to Haemar's Cavern and your system can lock up when entering Haemar's Shame. You won't be able to complete the quest and will have Aela as a follower, but with no dialogue options.
The Official Skyrim Patch, version 1.4, fixes this bug.

This also seems to happen if the totem is located in Morvunskar, and A Night To Remember has been completed. This can be worked around by carefully navigating around the point where the portal to the Misty Grove was placed earlier.
This can be resolved by manually advancing the quest with the console command setstage cr12 20.
Curing yourself of lycanthropy while this quest is active causes the Underforge door to become unresponsive. You cannot end the quest or get rid of Aela as a result.
You can finish the quest using the console command coc "WhiterunUnderForge" and placing the totem in its place, but Aela may stay inside, forcing you to use the command each time.
This quest may be unavailable if you marry Aela before all 3 totems are retrieved.
The Official Skyrim Patch, version 1.9, fixes this bug.
Aela is supposed to comment on each totem you find with unique dialogue. She repeats the first one because the dialogue doesn't check the totem count variable.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.4, fixes this bug.

While recovering a totem located in Ansilvund, it is possible that one of the swinging axe traps may knock Aela through a hole in the map, rendering the quest un-fulfillable. Aela may reappear at a later time although the trigger is unknown. Common factors such as fast traveling and waiting are worth trying. One method that has been found effective is to pray at one of the previously acquired totems. Aela may then appear at the entrance of the Underforge.

If Aela won't give you the first totem quest, check the status of this quest with the console command sqs cr12. If both Stage 0 and Stage 1 are marked as completed (with a 1 behind the respective stage), use the console command resetquest cr12. It is recommended to do this after handing in an Animal Extermination quest but before asking for more work.

If you do not complete all of the radiant quests of Aela the Huntress in the initial wave before advancing, you will be stuck doing Animal Extermination quests from her indefinitely, unable to collect the Totems of Hircine.

Firstly, use the console command setstage CR12 1. Then, get an Animal Extermination quest from Aela. Now use the console command setstage CR01 20 or setstage CR02 20 (depending on which version of the quest you're assigned), and return to Aela to finish the quest. Ask for work from her again and use the command setstage CR12 20 to complete the quest, and go to the Underforge to place the totem, which completes this quest. Repeat these steps 2 more times for the remaining 2 totems. The crucial part seems to be to Tab out of the conversation before Aela finishes her voiceline, when finishing the Animal Extermination quest. If you keep her dialogue open, she will have another Animal Extermination for you. If you close the dialogue before she finishes, she will have a dialogue for the Totems of Hircine quest. Alternatively, this can be fixed by marrying Aela, then again asking her for work after deciding on a place to live.
If Aela is chosen as your wife, after completing a totem quest she will stay and pray at the totem and will not return home.

This can be fixed on Xbox 360: You need lots of healing and dual-casting master illusionist abilities. Have her as a follower, take away all her weapons and give her a cheap sword. Then punch her enough times to get her to attack you (heal yourself as needed). Go through the front exit so you are outside of Jorrvaskr... she should follow you out and continue to attack you. Lead her off a good ways at which point, Dual-cast Calm on her and immediately talk to her and have her re-join you. Test her compliance by drawing a weapon or spell (she should do likewise, not just stand there - if she doesn't draw, restart the process). Once she's drawn a weapon, fast-travel to another location. She should now act normally, and if a spouse or steward, should remain at other locations when dismissed.

When obtaining the quest for the second totem, your quest marker may point to Jorrvaskr instead of the dungeon indicated in your quest log. The reason is that the quest item spawned on the floor in the main hall of Jorrvaskr instead of in the intended dungeon. The quest item will not be located anywhere in the dungeon indicated in the quest log.

The item is located in an inaccessible cell within Jorrvaskr. By the way, this problem may also occur for another totem (e.g., the third instead of the second totem). Furthermore, the quest log may offer nothing more than the direction to go collect the totem. Anyway, to resolve this problem, open the console and type movetoqt CR12 which will move the player to a small interior unlighted cell after closing the console. The totem will be found on the ground. Pick up the totem to advance the quest. Next reopen the console and type player.moveto 1A697 and the player will now move to a position beside Aela the Huntress. She should then ask the player if he or she has the totem and the quest can now carry on as normal.
Once you place the totems at their receptacles, praying at them may not affect you in any way.
Leave the Underforge then re-enter, wait 24 hours, or do another quest for Aela.

quick: Locate Auriel's Bow.
Speak to Gelebor.
Fill the Initiate's Ewer.
Kill Vyrthur.
Retrieve Auriel's Bow.

walkthrough.heading: Last of the Snow Elves
paragraphs: After learning the location of Auriel's Bow, travel to Darkfall Cave in the far northwestern reaches of Skyrim, just south-southwest of the Orc stronghold Mor Khazgur.

The cave is very dark, so you may wish to light your way using torches, the Vampire's Sight ability, or light spells. Follow the path, past a frostbite spider until you come to a bridge and what seems like a dead end. Once you try to cross back over the bridge, you will be forced, by either a rock trap or the bridge collapsing, into a very fast moving underground river that sends you downstream. Try to keep your head above the water, unless you have a waterbreathing ability. Eventually, you'll be thrown out of the current, and immediately attacked by a few frostbite spiders. Continue along the cavernous path, until you reach a small camp with a dead Breton; a note on her body sheds light on what happened: trolls.

From here you can either head down the path beyond the dead Breton, where after negotiating a falling boulders trap you will arrive in a chamber with two frost trolls. At the far western side is a stone shrine and Knight-Paladin Gelebor, one of the last two Snow Elves. Alternatively, you arrive immediately behind Gelebor by pulling the chain hidden behind the dead Breton's lean-to and taking the passage it reveals.

Speak to Gelebor, and he will offer you a deal: slay his brother, Vyrthur, who was corrupted by Falmer, and Gelebor will help you in obtaining Auriel's Bow. Vyrthur is hiding in the Inner Sanctum of the Forgotten Vale, a gigantic outdoor elven ruin with Ayleid-like architecture. In order to make your way there you must fill a jug, the Initiate's Ewer, with water from five wayshrines: the Wayshrines of Illumination, Learning, Radiance, Resolution, and Sight.

walkthrough.heading: Seeking Illumination
paragraphs: The first wayshrine, the Wayshrine of Illumination, is in Darkfall Passage, which can be accessed through the portal Gelebor opens. The Portal appears in the back of the shrine-like building that Gelebor raises from the ground. It may be invisible, with no Quest Marker pointing to it, but walking to the back of the shrine wall you will be able to activate the Portal none the less (see the Bugs section for more info).

The passage is just as dark as the cave, but is illuminated by tube worms, which look like odd pink flowers that retract into their tubes when you come near, whose faint pink light help to guide the way. Along the winding underground trek you will encounter several leveled falmer and chaurus; be sure to destroy any chaurus cocoons you come across before they have a chance to hatch. The shrine itself is in the final chamber of the passage, a radically different environment to the rest of the zone where vale deer and vale sabre cats inhabit a small forest. The Shrine is tended to by Prelate Sidanyis, who will activate it for you. Fill your ewer from the font and head through the portal to the Forgotten Vale.

walkthrough.heading: Resolving to Learn and See
paragraphs: The second wayshrine, the Wayshrine of Sight, can be found soon after emerging from Darkfall Passage into the Forgotten Vale and is tended to by Prelate Athring. It is to the north of the path that climbs up out of the entry vale through a set of stone arches, and west-northwest of the Forgotten Vale Cave. To find it, stop at the highest stone arch just before entering a narrow pass and head north along the cliff side, past a small frozen pond and several fallen trees, until you reach a silver ore vein. Just beyond is the Wayshrine, shrouded amidst a dense layer of fog.

The third shrine, the Wayshrine of Learning, is tended to by Prelate Celegriath. To reach it, head back to the stone arches and instead press on west, negotiating a narrow pass inhabited by frostbite spiders. Make your way down to the narrow river valley to a skeleton and the Unknown Book, Vol. I; reading it will start the Forgotten Vale Books Quest. Head downstream for a little while to reach the wayshrine.

To reach the fourth shrine, the Wayshrine of Resolution, cross the river and make your way up the turnpike path until you reach a large, frozen lake. Beware of the two dragons, Naaslaarum and Voslaarum, who will attack you while you cross the lake (provided you have completed Dragon Rising). The wayshrine, tended to by Prelate Nirilor, is above the northwest bank of the lake. Don't forget to pick up the Drain Vitality dragon shout from the large rock jutting out from the middle of the frozen lake south of this wayshrine.

walkthrough.heading: The Long Walk to Radiance
paragraphs: The fifth and final wayshrine, the Wayshrine of Radiance, is north of the Wayshrine of Resolution and is reached after a long, arduous trek through the Forgotten Vale and Glacial Crevice. To reach the latter, you can press on north and negotiate a long series of Falmer encampments and bridges suspended across the cliff-faces, or alternatively head southwest from the wayshrine across the mountainside and overlooking the lake. After a short while you arrive in a hanging valley with some moonstone ore veins; from here you can head down to the entrance of the Crevice. If you're looking for Unknown Book, Vol. III for the Forgotten Vale Books Quest, you can find it in a Falmer hut a couple of bridges before reaching the Crevice entrance.

The Crevice itself consists of a series of glacial chambers with icy ledges and rope bridges that ascend among a scattering of Falmer tents. Dispose of the many leveled Falmer and the odd frost troll that occupy this zone until you once again emerge out into the Forgotten Vale. This final part of the Vale consists of a confusing maze of Falmer tents and platforms crowded within a series of narrow, twisting canyons. Pick up Unknown Book, Vol. IV from a hut in the second village just before the entrance to the tunnel which takes you to the Wayshrine of Radiance, tended to by Prelate Edhelbor.

walkthrough.heading: Breaching the Sanctum
paragraphs: Down the path from the Wayshrine of Radiance and across a stone bridge lies the Inner Sanctum. Pour water from your Ewer into the stone basin, and the door in front of you will be bathed in green light before opening. Inside you will find a number of chambers with frozen Falmer and chaurus. Many of the Falmer hold items that can be looted, which may cause one or more of them to break out of their icy state and attack you. There is a chest tucked away in a partially hidden corner, some loose items lying about, and a number of lootable skeletons that Serana will raise during combat. Head north through the chambers, placing the Ewer on any pedestals to open the gates nearby, until you reach an icy tunnel leading to Auriel's Chapel. This tunnel branches to the left and doubles back leading to another chest and some more loose items.

Once you enter Auriel's Chapel, jump down from the stone ledge where you emerge and you will arrive in a stone chamber full of frozen Falmer and chaurus. From this point, you will not be able to retreat but can only continue forward. Vyrthur sits on a throne at the far end of the room, behind an impenetrable claw-like barrier. Once you come near, he will come to life and commence a fierce battle: the frozen Falmer and chaurus will start unfreezing in groups, while Vyrthur periodically summons a Frost Atronach, collapses parts of the ceiling and then hurls the broken boulders at you.

Once all enemies are defeated, in a mixture of rage and panic, Vyrthur will collapse the rest of the roof on you through a huge magical explosion, commencing a cutscene during which the only action you can undertake is walking or running. You awake to Serana telling you to get up and get on the balcony. Follow her until you reach Vyrthur, who will explain that after having been forsaken to vampirism by Auri-El, he created the prophecy that Lord Harkon is chasing. By dousing Auriel's Bow with the blood of a Daughter of Coldharbour—Serana— Vyrthur would exact his revenge by corrupting Auri-El's influence on Nirn.

Understandably displeased, Serana will lift him by the throat but will be thrown back as Vyrthur uses magic to free himself from her grip and attacks you. Once he has been defeated, a wayshrine will appear and Gelebor will walk through it. He will be surprised that the real reason for Vyrthur's actions was vampirism rather than corruption by the Falmer and thank you by proclaiming you worthy to carry Auriel's Bow. He will also bless some Sunhallowed arrows for you if you ask, and remain there if you wish to come back for more at any time. Retrieve Auriel's Bow from the newly-appeared wayshrine to complete the quest.

stages.text: The vision provided by the Elder Scrolls seems to indicate that Auriel's Bow may be located in a place known as Darkfall Cave. I should proceed there as soon as I'm prepared if I wish to recover the bow and stop Harkon from completing the Tyranny of the Sun. Objective 20: Locate Auriel's Bow

The vision provided by the Elder Scrolls seems to indicate that Auriel's Bow may be located in a place known as Darkfall Cave. I should proceed there as soon as I'm prepared if I wish to recover the bow and stop Harkon from completing the Tyranny of the Sun. Objective 20: Locate Auriel's Bow
Objective 30: Speak to Gelebor

I've encountered Gelebor, a snow elf Knight-Paladin of the Chantry of Auri-El. He's requesting I kill his brother, Arch-Curate Vyrthur, who's been corrupted by the Falmer. I've been given an Initiate's Ewer which will ultimately provide me access to the Chantry's Inner Sanctum where both Arch-Curate Vyrthur and Auriel's Bow are located. Objective 50: Survive Darkfall Passage
Objective 70: Fill the Initiate's Ewer (<Global=DLC1VQ07EwerFills>/5)

I've completely filled the Initiate's Ewer given to me by Knight-Paladin Gelebor. All that remains is gaining access to the Chantry's Inner Sanctum where both Arch-Curate Vyrthur and Auriel's Bow are located. Objective 80: Gain entry to the Inner Sanctum
I've gained access to the Chantry's Inner Sanctum. I should find and confront Arch-Curate Vyrthur in order to secure Auriel's Bow. Objective 90: Locate Arch-Curate Vyrthur
Objective 100: Confront Arch-Curate Vyrthur
Objective 110: Slay Arch-Curate Vyrthur
Objective 120: Speak to Gelebor
Objective 130: Retrieve Auriel's Bow

It's been revealed to me that the Tyranny of the Sun was created by Arch-Curate Vyrthur as his revenge upon Auriel for rebuking him when he was turned into a vampire. He possessed Auriel's Bow, but still needed the blood of a pure vampire to complete his ritual. This placed Serana in mortal danger, and I had no choice but to destroy him. I now possess the final piece of the Tyranny of the Sun, Auriel's Bow.

notes: You may use Auriel's Bow to blot out the sun. It is not permanent and will only last until 7pm (which is sunset; you can shoot out the sun again the next day, as the sun will rise at 5am).
After a wayshrine is opened, it will contain portals to three of the other four opened wayshrines, as well as to Darkfall Cave.

At the end of this quest there is an opportunity to gain a second permanent follower. Right after you kill the boss, Serana will stop following you around and you can fast travel away to grab a second follower. There isn't a direct return point, but you can fast travel back to Forgotten Vale and use the portals, then run quickly back through the castle and finish the quest by speaking with the NPC waiting for you and taking Auriel's Bow. This time, your second follower slot should be permanent - though you should make sure to have two followers for 'Kindred Judgement' and any plot quests that are instanced. You can swap your other follower, but never dismiss Serana or you will lose the second slot.
If you have not killed Naaslaarum and Voslaarum it is possible for one of them to fly to the balcony and interfere in the fight with Vyrthur. They can even kill him for you.

South of the Temple balcony is a hanging valley with a waterfall pouring from it down to the frozen lake. This valley is the location that the Emerald Paragon gives access to, and can be reached from the balcony by using the Become Ethereal shout and careful cliff walking. What's more, you can easily use Unrelenting Force to shout Vyrthur down the balcony, and give him a falling death.

Note: Nearly all of the bugs mentioned below occur because Gelebor, Serana, or Vyrthur have uncompleted scripts running. Be sure to allow any dialogue they are speaking to complete before taking further action. Also, make sure that the scripted actions with the Initiate's Ewer and the Wayshrines have completed before going on to the next wayshrine. Furthermore, when attempting the aforementioned by loading a saved game, some variables might not reset, thus rendering the attempt unaffected - shutting down Skyrim and launching it again will wipe out any residue from the memory.
You may be able to ask Serana to wait somewhere even though this is clearly not intended in the scripting. She is supposed to refuse when you ask her to wait for the duration of this quest.

The Unofficial Dawnguard Patch, version 2.0.2, addresses this issue. This was likely due to the previous quest's script not properly delaying things before this one starts. Serana's follower settings were ending up in an unreliable state as a result.
Serana may attack Gelebor immediately after you finish the first dialogue with him, ceasing quest progression.

Using the console command killall will fix this. You will have to wait a bit, until dialogue starts between Serana and Gelebor. They will both remain in the crouched, dying position, but they will go back to normal once a new area is entered.
Knight-Paladin Gelebor may not activate the first wayshrine.
Open the console and select Gelebor, enter the code disable, then enable.
Sometimes Serana can get stuck in combat mode, preventing her dialogue with Gelebor. Open the console and select Serana, enter the code disable, then enable.

You can fix this problem by using the console command setstage DLC1VQ07 50. This fix will not work unless Serana is next to you when you first speak with Gelebor. Serana has extensive dialogue exchange with Gelebor which leads to him giving you the Initiate's Ewer. Without the Ewer in your inventory, advancing the quest stage to open the Wayshrine will not help you.
When you activate the first wayshrine, the portal may not appear.
The portal may be invisible. Pressing the 'activate' button while standing in the back of the wayshrine may activate the invisible portal.
When given the objective to fill the Initiates Ewer, one of the wayshrines may not give you any water making the quest impossible to complete.
Reloading and visiting the wayshrines in a different order may fix this.
If you can't get water because Skyrim thinks you are in combat, exit the cell then re-enter it.
When you have finished collecting the ewer, and are about to pour it in the basin, it won't react and you will be stuck.

If you have this problem, open the console and enter GetStage DLC1VQ07 . If it returns 132.00, that means that somehow the quest progressed past the next stage of the quest. Since you cannot go back stages, the only way to solve this problem would be to use SetStage for every stage past "Gain Entry to the Inner Sanctum" until the current stage number is above 132 (meaning SetStage DLC1VQ07 200 , completing the quest, giving you the bow, and starting the next quest). This will mean skipping quite a lot of stages, but there's no way to fix this bug at the moment without skipping.
Alternatively you can use console command coc DLC1FalmerTemple01 and SetStage 110 (assuming you are just stuck at the basin).

If coc is useless, and your queststage is 110, use the sapphire paragon. You must use console command tcl, and then you can gain entry to the Inner Sanctum (remember to use tcl again after gaining entry). Then, leave from the Inner Sanctum via the door, and Serana will be with you again.
After confronting Arch-Curate Vyrthur and defeating the first wave of unfrozen enemies, he may not react and spawn a second wave, ceasing quest progress.

Each subsequent wave will only occur after all mobilized enemies have been killed. These enemies are not the frozen ones standing about but are spawned as the waves progress, sometimes replacing the frozen variety. Sometimes they spawn inside the architecture or get stuck in odd places. If area effect spells cannot kill them, reloading a save is your only recourse. After each wave there is a pause before Vyrthur gives another rant and unleashes the next wave. Sending an arrow or two, or an area damage spell in his direction may speed things along a little.

This can also be fixed by using the command killall in the boss arena (note that both Vyrthur and Serana will be put in the bleed out state as both of them are set to essential at the moment and can't die) but this updates Vyrthur's scripts and can hopefully allow you to progress. If that's the case and Vyrthur summons the Ancient Frost Atronach, immediately hit the console, click on Serana and use the command resurrect. Once you kill the Atronach, Vyrthur will do a shockwave and run to the balcony. As he reaches the balcony he will die (because he is not set to essential anymore), so just click on his corpse and resurrect him too, and that may trigger the following scene and boss fight to progress normally.
You may be unable to kill Arch-Curate Vyrthur.
If that happens use the console command killall. You might have to give Serana the resurrect command in the console afterward.

The final objective to 'Retrieve Auriel's Bow' may not properly register as completed as it should, even after picking it up. A message signifying the quest's completion will still turn up, though the game ceases to progress after that. Neither Serana nor Gelebor will have proper dialogue options, and the following quest, 'Kindred Judgement', does not begin.
The Unofficial Dawnguard Patch, version 2.0.0, fixes this bug.
Use the console command setstage DLC1VQ07 200 to properly complete the final 'Retrieve Auriel's Bow' objective.
After finishing the quest, Serana might not have the dialogue to start Kindred Judgment but will allow you to use her blood to make Bloodcursed arrows.
The Unofficial Dawnguard Patch, version 2.0.0, fixes this bug.
Completing a minor side quest before fighting Vyrthur may fix this.
The tier 5 Ancient Frost Atronach that is generated during this quest was incorrectly set to the same record as the tier 4 alias directly before it.
The Unofficial Skyrim Legendary Edition Patch, version 3.0.3, fixes this bug.

You can talk to Serana about helping the snow-elf priests while playing the vampire and Dawnguard sides of the quest. This is an error as the Editor ID indicates it was supposed to be exclusive to the vampire side.
The Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 4.1.3, addresses this issue. This was due to a missing variable check to be sure you are in fact playing for Harkon's side.

quick: Travel to Yngvild.
Collect the four journals.
Return to Vekel.

walkthrough.heading: The Proposition
paragraphs: If you approach Vekel in The Ragged Flagon and ask him for work, he will tell you about some journals that he's been after: "I have a buyer with a very odd taste in literature, looking for some particular books. I'm told they're the ravings of a madman, a wizard named Arondil and his peculiar cravings. It's said to be in four volumes and very hard to come by. My client is offering quite a reward for them, which I'd split with you." If you ask for him to elaborate further on the journals, he will go on to say, "Recently, a woman was found... naked and shivering along the road to Dawnstar. The only information the guard could get from her were tales of strange experiments and Arondil scribbling in his journals."

Asking about Arondil won't get you much, as Vekel says, "Only rumors. He used to have a home in Dawnstar until they burned it down. The people say he was doing unspeakable experiments on reanimation... rituals only a necromancer would perform. After he made for Yngvild, he was never heard from again."

Once you agree to retrieve the journals, he will conclude the conversation with: "Then we have a deal. In his later years, Andoril [sic] moved into some ice caves known as Yngvild. He prefered [sic] the solitude in which to perform his, um... experiments."

walkthrough.heading: Yngvild
paragraphs: Yngvild is an ice cave located on an island northeast of Dawnstar. To access it, find the entrance on the north side by following the pathway up the island. Once inside, you are able to find the first three journals. The first journal is located on a table near two Yngvild ghosts and a leveled draugr. The second journal can be found on a table alongside a woodcutter's axe and a scroll. The third journal can be found on a table just before the door leading to Yngvild Throne Room.

walkthrough.heading: Yngvild Throne Room
paragraphs: Once you enter the main chamber in the throne room, you will see Arondil sitting on his throne with an Yngvild ghost alongside him. The fourth and final part of the journal lies through the door behind him, on a table along with an unusual gem for the quest No Stone Unturned. Once you have retrieved the journals, you can exit the cave and head back to The Ragged Flagon to receive your reward.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: Return all four journals to Vekel and he will remark, "Good. I was hoping you hadn't forgotten about it. As promised, here's your payment for bringing them to me. Got it as part of a fair trade from my client." Your reward for returning the journals is a leveled and enchanted one-handed weapon.

stages.text: Objective 10: Enter Yngvild Barrow
Objective 20: Retrieve Arondil's Journals (<Global=FFRiften21JFound>/4)
Objective 30: Return to Vekel

notes: You don't have to kill Arondil to complete the quest, merely get his journals.
This quest can be started even if you're not a member of the Thieves Guild at all.
Sneaking into the final chamber unnoticed and removing the Soul Gem from the pedestal next to Arondil causes the ghosts near him to attack and kill him.
Objectives for this quest will add themselves to the quest log even if you'd never been to see Vekel about finding the books.
This is no longer the case with version 4.2.4 of the Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch.
Vekel will neither reward you on completion of the quest, nor take the journals.

The Official Skyrim Patch, version 1.9.26.0.8, addresses this issue. He will now reward you properly, and the journals will no longer be marked as quest items once the quest is complete, and can be dropped or sold.
As stated above, Vekel does not actually remove the journals from your inventory upon quest completion, even with the Official Patch.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.0, fixes this bug.

This quest can be started without talking to Vekel; if you go to Yngvild and pick up all four journals, you will receive a quest update telling you to return them to Vekel, even if you never spoke to him before.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 1.0, addresses this issue. He has been given appropriate dialogue to acknowledge the fact that he had never given you the task to find the journals prior.

quick: Speak with Brynjolf and Karliah at the Thieves Guild.
Meet Karliah at The Shadow Stone just outside Riften.
Enter Nightingale Hall and follow Karliah's instructions.
Equip the Nightingale Armor.
Proceed further into the cave and follow Karliah's instructions.
Speak to Brynjolf about the leadership of the Guild.

walkthrough.heading: Plans Revealed
paragraphs: Return to the Thieves Guild after your search at Riftweald Manor to show Brynjolf Mercer's plans for stealing the Eyes of the Falmer. Brynjolf will explain the significance of your findings; Mercer plans one more heist before disappearing for good. The only hope of catching him is to intercept him at the location. Brynjolf informs you that Karliah has requested to speak with both of you.

walkthrough.heading: A Secret Order
paragraphs: When you speak to Karliah, she reveals to you and Brynjolf that Mercer Frey was a Nightingale, an agent of Nocturnal. Because of this, Karliah is concerned about being at full strength and on equal footing before pursuing Mercer. She asks you and Brynjolf to meet her at The Shadow Stone outside of Riften.

walkthrough.heading: The Nightingale Edge
paragraphs: Here you will find yourself at the entrance to Nightingale Hall wherein is the edge over Mercer that Karliah was alluding to. Proceed inside, but don't get too far ahead as Karliah begins telling you more about the Nightingales and their role. She will later remark that this was the Nightingales' base, and that she will return here once done with Mercer. After crossing a bridge, you can find a copy of the Pickpocket skill book Purloined Shadows to the right.

Your first stop is the armor chamber. Activate the stone Karliah indicates and the Nightingale Armor is placed in your inventory. You must equip it in order to continue. Once you have donned the armor, Karliah will discuss the next step: your sworn oath to Nocturnal. Follow Karliah further into the cave past side passages leading to sleeping quarters where you can find a copy of the Sneak skill book The Red Kitchen Reader and living spaces.

walkthrough.heading: Trinity Restored
paragraphs: Once you have agreed to Nocturnal's conditions on becoming a Nightingale, Karliah will operate the pull chain for the gate leading into the Hall's "Welkinsight Chamber" where you will take your oath to become a Nightingale. You will be directed to stand on a specific platform. If you have a follower with you, their presence does not affect the outcome in any way. Karliah summons Nocturnal and asks to resume her role as a Nightingale as well as induct you and Brynjolf into their ranks. Nocturnal agrees.

Now that you are officially inducted into the Nightingales, Karliah will explain that Mercer got into the vault by using the Skeleton Key which he stole from the Twilight Sepulcher; a grievous insult to Nocturnal which threatens the very foundations of the Nightingales. The key needs to be returned to the Sepulcher to set things right and return the uncanny luck of the Thieves Guild.

This is a big day for you as now Brynjolf has something to add. With Mercer disgraced, the issue of the leadership of the Thieves Guild is at hand. Brynjolf states that he and Karliah think you would be the right person for the job, once you've proven yourself by dealing with Mercer and completing all of the Thieves Guild additional jobs. From here, leave for Irkngthand to begin Blindsighted.

stages.text: Before intercepting Mercer Frey, Karliah wishes to speak to both Brynjolf and myself. Objective 10: Listen to Karliah
(Karliah initiates dialogue)

Karliah has indicated Brynjolf and I are to meet her at an old standing stone just outside the Southwest Gate of Riften. Her motivations for doing so are mysterious, but I suspect it has something to do with the Nightingales. Objective 20: Meet Karliah at the standing stone
Objective 30: Follow Karliah

Karliah has informed Brynjolf and I that we're to join the elite ranks of the Nightingales and assist in reforming the trinity that was disrupted over twenty-five years ago when Mercer Frey murdered Gallus. Objective 40: Activate the Armor Stone Objective 42: Equip the Nightingale Armor (once Brynjolf and Karliah have donned their armor)
Objective 45: Follow Karliah
Objective 50: Stand on vacant floor glyph
I've undertaken the Oath and I'm now a Nightingale, guardian of the Twilight Sepulcher and a dedicated sentinel of the goddess Nocturnal.
Objective 60: Speak to Karliah
Objective 70: Speak to Brynjolf

Karliah has finally revealed the fundamental mission of the Nightingales... the guardianship of the Skeleton Key of Nocturnal. This powerful artifact, normally kept safely within the Twilight Sepulcher, has been stolen by Mercer Frey. As a Nightingale, the duty to recover the Skeleton Key falls squarely upon my shoulders.

notes: Although Karliah insists that you equip the Nightingale armor, you can then immediately unequip it again if you prefer your existing armor. It is not necessary to wear the Nightingale armor during the oath-taking ceremony.
There is no way to proceed with the questline without swearing service to Nocturnal intermittently during your lifetime and permanently after your death.
Brynjolf may not begin walking towards Karliah in the Ragged Flagon and the dialogue will not initiate to begin the quest.
Reloading from an earlier save may fix this.
Use the console command setstage TG08A 15 to have her start speaking, regardless.
If Karliah or Brynjolf are stuck (won't move, don't complete actions), the console command resurrect will sometimes force them to resume their usual scripted behavior.
It's possible that Brynjolf will walk away when you've arrived in the hall and are asked to get your armor.
Push him through the cave.

You can use the console by clicking on him (or typing prid 20545), and then typing moveto player to teleport him to you. Make sure he's near you when you don the armor when Karliah is about to ask you to take the oath, which should fix his AI (confirmed by his comment on his new outfit).

If only you and Karliah make it to the stones before taking the oath and Brynjolf is still walking away, use console command setstage TG08A 55. This starts the cinematic sequence without Brynjolf, who will join the show slightly later.
Karliah sometimes may not meet you at Nightingale Hall, making the quest impossible to finish.

Karliah will sometimes go back to the Frozen Hearth where you have met to decrypt Gallus' journal. It is related to the bug in the quest Hard Answers where the stages will not update. Redo Hard Answers step by step, and the quest Trinity Restored will reactivate.

You can use the console and type setstage TG06 60 and go to the cellar in the Frozen Hearth to talk again to Enthir and Karliah. After this Karliah and Brynjolf will be at the entrance of the Nightingale Hall. (You can further check if this is the problem by typing getstage TG06 in the console. If the Stage is smaller than 200 then this is the cause of Karliah's disappearance). If setting the stage to 60 doesn't work, enter setstage TG06 200 to complete the quest Hard Answers. Karliah will then begin her long trek to Nightingale Hall. Fast travel to the hall, wait for 24 hours and she will show up.

Alternatively, type in the console prid 00020545 (for Brynjolf) or prid 00058F1A (for Karliah), followed by the command moveto player. Use the latter command as many times as necessary to lead the selected NPC to the stones; you may need to activate the stone multiple times to get Brynjolf and/or Karliah to equip their Nightingale armors. You may still be required to use the command as you continue further down the halls. Do not use the placeatme commands on unique NPCs, as you will create a clone of the NPC which will cause undesirable results in-game - only use moveto player.
Sometimes, Karliah will simply turn around and walk out of the cave instead of opening the gate. As she is the only one able to open it, this will render the quest impossible to complete.

Actual bug caused by the TG08aKarliahOpenGate AI package, the "Once Per Day" flag is set on that package and that flag somehow prevents the package from running. Turning off that flag in a patch MOD like "Trinity Restored Karliah Gate Fix" on Nexus mods will fix the problem unless some other mod also updates that AI package (and at least ONE does exist) and restores that bug.
After Karliah asks you to take the oath and is done talking, immediately wait 1 hour, this will allow her to warp to the chain and open the gate. Worked on my first try.

After Brynjolf accepts the terms of becoming a Nightingale, Karliah will ask you if you accept. Accept the terms, Karliah will then turn and head to the gate. Immediately interrupt her and ask her any question. This lets Brynjolf move ahead of her and fixes this bug. In some cases you might need to interrupt Brynjolf rather than Karliah and let her get to the gate first. This can be achieved by standing in his way.
Attacking Karliah may cause her to turn around and open the gate.
Exiting the conversation with her will allow the stage to reset itself, and may fix this.
Since the bug seems to involve the conversation with Brynjolf, you can sometimes circumvent the bug by talking to Brynjolf continually until Karliah opens the gate.
Allow the cell to completely reset and quickly run to the gate.

You can also fix Karliah from walking away if you tell her that you don't understand the full meaning of being a Nightingale. She will ask you again and then if you say you are ready, you can enter the room to finish the ritual.

Before accepting Nocturnal's conditions from Karliah, force her to and keep her directly at the gate using Unrelenting Force and Paralyze. Accept the conditions and keep her at the gate until Brynjolf joins you both. She may then pull the chain and progress the quest.
Open the console, click on the gate and use the command disable, then setstage tg08a 52. You can now see the cinematic involving Nocturnal. As with all console commands, exercise extreme caution.

Karliah may be going to the exit instead of opening the door to the Nightingale contract. To repair this, use disable on the door, and use disable on Karliah and enable to fix her before using moveto player to teleport her to you. After that, use setstage tg08a 52 and they may walk to their own spots.

The same can be done as above only instead of disabling the door, it is possible to run activate 58f1a on the door (which simulates Karliah pulling the chain instead of removing the door from the game).

Also, you can attack Karliah while she is talking to Brynjolf and use relenting force to move her to where the chain is. After, use Emperor's Voice to calm her down and then talk to her. She will then pull the chain and you can proceed. If you are not an imperial and do not have this power, you can use the command /showracemenu to change it to imperial and then change it back to your original race.

If none of the above works, run to the gate while Karliah talks to Brynjolf. After they are done talking, open the console and execute the following commands: prid 58f1a and moveto player. This should teleport Karliah to you. If she doesn't start a conversation with you just talk to her. After you accept the oath she should now open the gate and proceed inside the chamber

The following solution worked on multiple tries. After accepting the oath, run up to the chain by the bars and open up the console and execute the following commands prid c6996. Then execute activate 58f1a. That should simulate Karliah pulling the chain to bring the bars down. Run inside and then bring up the console again and execute prid 58f1a and then moveto player to teleport Karliah to you. Once you and Karliah are both inside execute setstage tg08a 52 to progress the quest.
Just go ahead to the gate and ignore them. After they have talked before the stairs, Use console move karliah near the gate opener and talk to her to progress the quest.

When presented with the choice to take the oath hit your Escape key to end the conversation. Use the command console, select Brynjolf, run to the previous room or the room before that and moveto player Brynjolf. Then run back to Karliah and accept the oath. She will open the gate, allowing the quest to continue. Brynjolf will join shortly.
When you stand on the marker to summon Nocturnal, nothing may happen.
Move around a little until the cinematic begins.
If the above fails, make sure you have exhausted all dialogue with Karliah and try again.

After entering Nightingale Hall and donning the Nightingale armor, Karliah may pull the chain for the gate twice, when it should only be once. Because only Karliah can activate the chain, this can be problematic, trapping Karliah, Brynjolf, and possibly you inside or outside the cave.
Quickly talk to Karliah before she can pull the chain a second time.
If you enter the cave with your followers, Karliah may stop before the bridge and not go any farther.
Have your followers wait outside.

quick: Talk to Ondolemar.
Steal Ogmund's Amulet of Talos from his house.
Return to Ondolemar.

walkthrough.heading: A Thalmor's Task
paragraphs: Ondolemar is a Thalmor Justiciar living in Markarth. You can find him pacing in front of the jarl's throne room in Understone Keep, accompanied by two Thalmor Soldiers. Talk to him and he will tell you his duty in Markarth. "I was sent here to lead the Thalmor's interests in this corner of Skyrim. It's my mission to root out all Talos worship in this city." As a member of the Thalmor, he doesn't recognize Talos as a god and thinks Talos does not deserve to have a place in their pantheon. In his opinion, citizens of the Empire have a responsibility to cease their heretical worship. Then he will pay some attention to you. "You're awfully inquisitive, aren't you? I like that. Perhaps you'd care to solve a little problem I'm having?" He knows that Ogmund the skald, an old and respected man, worships Talos in his home, but the jarl has been reluctant to have him arrested. Ondolemar wants you to break in to Ogmund's home and find evidence for him.

walkthrough.heading: To Catch a Bard
paragraphs: Ogmund's house is just above the market stalls. You may need to pick a novice-level lock and get into his house. There is a chest in the north part of the house holding Ogmund's Amulet of Talos. This is the evidence Ondolemar requires. Steal the amulet and leave the house quietly. If you run into the authorities, do not resist arrest and make the guards turn hostile to you, as Ondolemar will attack you as well, and it will be impossible for you to talk to him during the fight. Pay your fine and the amulet won't be removed from your inventory.

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: Bring the amulet to Ondolemar. He believes it will be all he needs to have Ogmund taken care of. He graciously thanks you for your assistance and rewards you with leveled gold.

stages.text: Objective 10: Find evidence of Ogmund's Talos worship
Objective 15: Bring Ogmund's Amulet of Talos to Ondolemar

notes: If the Reach is given to the Stormcloaks in Season Unending or conquered for them after The Battle for Fort Sungard, this quest becomes unavailable, as Ondolemar will no longer be present. Likewise, killing Ogmund before the quest will also render it permanently unavailable.
If the Stormcloaks capture Markarth while this quest is in progress or if you kill Ogmund, you will fail it immediately.
Completing this quest will also grant you access to the Thalmor Headquarters without it being considered as trespassing if you enter, and taking anything from there will no longer count as theft.
Completion of this quest and a Speech skill of 50 or better are required to convince Ondolemar to provide a distraction for you in Diplomatic Immunity.

After this quest, using Ondolemar as a distraction during Diplomatic Immunity will cause his disposition toward you to fall to -2. Doing Diplomatic Immunity first and then finishing this quest will cause his disposition toward you rise to +1.

Although Ondolemar is a member of the Thalmor, and technically not a citizen of the Reach as he's only posted in Understone Keep, helping him via this quest still counts towards helping people of the Reach if you're working on becoming Thane of the Reach.

An option to bring the amulet to Ogmund was apparently planned, and is available in the code, but there is no dialogue that allows for it. Quest stage 25 appears to be related to this, as setting it with console commands will mark the quest completed and sets Ogmund and Ondolemar's relationship to you to 1 and -1, respectively.
Ogmund is supposed to go to the stocks in Understone Keep once you bring the amulet to Ondolemar, but due to a scripting bug, fails to do so.
The Unofficial Skyrim Patch, version 2.0.1, fixes this bug. (details)

quick: Kill the leader of the assigned location.
Return to Farkas.

paragraphs: This is a radiant quest given by Farkas when asked for work. Farkas has received a contract to clear out a troublesome area. The enemies you encounter depend on the location of the quest. In order to complete the contract, you need to travel to the location and kill the leader. The quest is randomized and repeatable.

walkthrough.heading: Radiant Options
paragraphs: The target location is randomly chosen from 118 possible locations, amounting to a majority of the dungeons that contain boss-type enemies. The location will be limited to holds that you have previously visited, so early in the game you may only receive destinations within Whiterun Hold, but later in the game there are many more possible destinations. Possible types of locations are:
A Bandit Camp or Bandit-Occupied Fort: (28 possible locations) — "Nothing but a bunch of lowly bandits. Cowards, who will take little effort."
A Draugr Crypt: (17 possible locations) — "The restless dead. Not pretty, but if you don't stop them, they'll move on to the locals."
A Falmer Hive: (12 possible locations) — "The Falmer. There have been reports that they've been attacking people at night."
A Forsworn Camp: (8 possible locations) — "It's a problem with the Forsworn. Unpredictable, unknowable, and dangerous. Be careful."
A Giant Camp: (12 possible locations) — "It's a clan of giants. The war is driving them out of their lands, and they've started attacking settlements."
A Hagraven Nest: (11 possible locations) — "You'll be clearing a nest of those Hagraven things. I've never faced one myself, but I hear... disturbing things about them."
A Spriggan Grove: (8 possible locations) — "Oddly enough, Spriggans. Usually they let alone, but for some reason, this particular grove isn't."
A Vampire Lair: (6 possible locations) — "Bloodsuckers. Vampires. Take every precaution. One bite, and you could end up as one of them."
A Warlock Lair: (17 possible locations) — "Rogue wizards. I've never trusted magic types. The College is bad enough. Destroy them."

(Note that the provided categories list all locations with the given type of occupant, including locations that do not have a boss-type enemy and therefore cannot be possible destinations for this quest).

walkthrough.heading: Reward
paragraphs: The Unofficial Skyrim Legendary Edition Patch, version 3.0.3, fixes this bug. (details)

notes: If Dragonborn is installed, some radiant locations may be on Solstheim. If you are in Skyrim, you will not receive a quest marker pointing you to the quest location, but must travel to Solstheim first (at which point any quest markers you have to quests in Skyrim will disappear).
Despite having dialogue and quest stages to send you to a Giant Camp, the quest does not have the correct conditions to select a Giant Camp as a destination.

If you clear Driftshade Sanctuary (or any of radiant locations this quest can get) prior to starting this quest, it may become uncompleteable. This bug can occur even if you haven't discovered the location to which the quest directs you.

You may use the console to manually enable the next stage in the main companions quest line. First enter the command setstage C01 0 then setstage CR05 0 and then setstage CR05 20 ; then speak to whoever who gave you this quest so you can finish this quest without doing it again. This seems to work, though other issues may or may not arise later (has not been thoroughly tested).
You can also use the console command setstage cr05 20 to manually progress the quest to the next stage.
If you are using console commands, you should deselect the quest beforehand; if you do not, the quest may remain highlighted, leaving a permanent quest marker on your map.
You may resurrect the bandits and kill them again.
The quest is greyed out in the journal (completed) when you've returned to Farkas.

The quest is switched to "completed" at a point outside of Whiterun as you return. (This bug is from multiple radiant locations.) Whether you fast travel or not back to Whiterun, the quest is "completed" but you cannot accept further work as you are stuck on this particular quest.
Use the console command setstage cr05 100. You will receive a reward and be able to ask for more work.
Another solution is to load a save prior to taking the quest, decline it when offered, then take a quest from another Companion leader.

On PC, you can also reload a previous save, then use the console command prid 1A693 followed by moveto player in order to select Farkas and teleport him to your location. There you will be able to talk to him and turn in the quest as normal. He will then slowly walk back home but if you don't want to wait, you can travel back to the hall and use the exact same commands to teleport him back there.
If the location of the quest is Dimhollow Crypt and you haven't started Awakening yet, some of the dungeon is inaccessible, preventing you from killing the dungeon boss.
Start Awakening to gain access to the area and proceed completing both quests.

quick: (Optional) Enter Fahlbtharz Forge.
Locate all four Fahlbtharz Forge Gems.
Take the Unenchanted Weapon from Hand Kenro Hlan at Fahlbtharz Forge.
Place the weapon and the four gems into the forge to obtain Trueflame.

walkthrough.heading: An Unenchanted Weapon
paragraphs: Finding any of the four Dwarven Forge Gems hidden throughout Solstheim or entering the Temple in Raven Rock and stumbling upon the Ghosts of the Tribunal quest will begin this quest.

Trueflame is located in the Dwarven Forge in Fahlbtharz where Hand Kenro Hlan will attack you. He is in possession of Trueflame, although it appears as an Unenchanted Weapon without the enchanted flames it traditionally bears. He also has a note giving direction, and a sample of Pyroil Tar which will be needed once you have all four Gems.

walkthrough.heading: Fahlbtharz Forge Gem Locations
paragraphs: The gems are found:
On the body of Hand Kenro Hlan.
On the body of the buyer after following the Redoran guard during Buyer Beware.
In the armory in Ashfall's Tear.
On the body of Erden Relvel at the end of the quest Ashen Heart.

walkthrough.heading: Reforging the Blade of Nerevar
paragraphs: With the Unenchanted Blade and all four gems in hand, you must return to Fahlbtharz Forge and place the four gems within the forge's receptacles. You will then need to apply the pyroil tar to the blade and place it in the sword slot; doing so will complete this quest and reignite the weapon with a visually impressive fire damage enchantment. Congratulations, you now possess Trueflame, the legendary Blade of Nerevar.

stages.text: I've picked up a Dwarven gem that looks like it's tied to the Dwarven Forge in Fahlbtharz. I placed the gem into the forge's main panel, which has four slots in total.

I've picked up four Dwarven gems that appear to be tied to the Dwarven Forge in Fahlbtharz. I should place them in the main panel to restore power to the forge. Objective 20: Place the gems in the forge (0/4)
I've picked up an Unenchanted Weapon that looks like it's tied to the Dwarven Forge in Fahlbtharz.

I found a journal on the body of a heretic that implies he was attempting to make use of a Dwarven forge. I should investigate the area and see what else I can find. Objective 3: Retrieve the Unenchanted Weapon

I've picked up a Dwarven gem that looks like it's tied to the Dwarven Forge in Fahlbtharz. With enough gems, I may be able to restore power to the forge. Objective 10: Collect the Dwarven Forge Gems throughout Solstheim (0/4)

I've picked up a Dwarven gem that looks like it's tied to the Dwarven Forge in Fahlbtharz. I placed the gem and three others into the forge's main panel and restored power to the machine. Objective 70: Apply the Pyroil Tar to the Unenchanted Weapon

In order to help restore Trueflame's enchantment, I covered the Unenchanted Weapon in Pyroil Tar, a special ingredient used in Dwarven smithing. Objective 80: Place the Unenchanted Weapon in the forge

I found an Unenchanted Weapon and placed it into a special slot in the Dwarven Forge. Once the forge has its power restored, it should enchant the weapon. Objective 1: Use the forge to enchant and restore Trueflame
I found an unenchanted weapon and placed it into a special slot in the Dwarven Forge. Once the forge has its power restored, it should enchant the weapon. Objective 90: Activate the forge

I found an unenchanted weapon and placed it into a special slot in the Dwarven Forge. With the forge fully operational, the weapon's enchantment has been restored and I can now remove it. Objective 100: Pick up Trueflame
I found an unenchanted weapon and placed it into a special slot in the Dwarven Forge. With the forge fully operational, the weapon's enchantment has been restored and I can now remove it.

notes: You must also complete all the other related quests in order to obtain the 4 Fahlbtharz Forge Gems.
These quests are:
Ghosts of the Tribunal
Her Word Against Theirs
Buyer Beware
Careless Curation
Ashen Heart (All previous quests must be completed to unlock the armory and the Ashen Heart quest)
The animations for creating Trueflame will cause the screen to freeze on the Nintendo Switch. You need to close and restart the game to continue.
The easiest way to bypass this bug is by pressing A to insert the blade, followed immediately by waiting for an hour, skipping the animation that freezes the game.

This bug can be solved by going into sneak mode, then placing the Unenchanted Weapon and opening the character menu simultaneously. Without exiting the menu, press start and manually save the game. After that, exit both menus. If the screen is still frozen, close and restart the game, loading up the mid-animation save. After that, you should be able to take the Trueflame without issue.
Sometimes the pyroil tar does not apply to the unenchanted weapon.
To fix this bug, try unequipping all apparel items then continue with the quest normally.

If you add the gems to the forge and ignite the forge before inserting the unenchanted weapon, you may not be able to finish the quest normally. You can use the console to advance the quest, as discussed below, but you will still have the unenchanted weapon in your inventory, unless you also remove it with console commands.
The game may freeze if you perform the Trueflame ritual too quickly.
The Official Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 1.6.1130, fixes this bug.

quick: Speak with Hafjorg.
Obtain an unusual quicksilver ore sample from Filnjar.
Return the ore sample to Hafjorg.

walkthrough.heading: Helping out
paragraphs: Should you find yourself in Elgrim's Elixirs, commiserate with Hafjorg about how much she has to do at the shop. She will tell you that caring for her husband, Elgrim, is holding her back from getting things done; specifically running an errand to Shor's Stone to retrieve an unusual ore sample. Offer to fetch it for her:

walkthrough.heading: Shor's Stone
paragraphs: In Shor's Stone, seek out Filnjar at his home and smithy. Let him know you are there for the ore, and after some derisive comments about Elgrim, he hands over a sample of quicksilver. He explains that he needs Elgrim to examine this particular piece as its discovery coincided with a strange invasion of frostbite spiders in Redbelly mine:

walkthrough.heading: Four Potions
paragraphs: Bring the sample to Hafjorg. She makes a sarcastic comment about her husband's busy schedule, but had him make you four leveled skill potions to compensate you for your travel:

stages.text: Objective 10: Obtain Ore Sample from Filnjar
Objective 20: Return Ore Sample to Hafjorg

notes: The ore sample is a special variety of quicksilver ore; it cannot be used for smelting.
Although Filnjar has apparently been waiting for a courier for some time, the quest can only be started through Hafjorg.
While it is implied that the special ore is in some way related to the appearance of the spiders at the mine, this is never addressed or brought up again in any other quests.
The quest incorrectly sets disposition for Filnjar instead of Hafjorg upon completion. Although Filnjar is also involved, these quests normally only raise the disposition with the quest giver.
The Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 4.1.4, fixes this bug. (details)

quick: Read Bounty: Fangtusk.
Obtain an Arctic Grayling.
Travel northeast of Yngol Barrow.
Place the grayling on the rock.
Kill Fangtusk.
Search Fangtusk for the Vampiric Ring.
Speak to the steward of Windhelm.

paragraphs: This quest can be started after Crustacean Extermination has been completed by talking to Viriya:
She will hand you the bounty, read it and you will learn of a monsterous horker known as Fangtusk, which has been terrorizing fishermen north of Hollyfrost Farm.

You need to obtain an arctic grayling and then head northeast of Yngol Barrow to a rock by water that has two skeletons lying next to it, place the arctic grayling on the rock and Fangtusk will emerge from the icy water.
Once you have killed Fangtusk, inspect his body and you will find vampire dust, vampire gloves, and a Vampiric Ring, suggesting Fangtusk ate a vampire.
Take this ring to the steward of Windhelm and speak to them:
You will then be rewarded 200 gold.

stages.text: The Jarl of Windhelm has put out a bounty on a monsterous horker known as Fangtusk, which has been terrorizing fishermen north of Hollyfrost Farm. Fishermen have learned that it seems to enjoy arctic grayling above all other fish. I should obtain an arctic grayling and leave it near its feeding grounds in order to lure it out. Objective 0: Obtain an arctic grayling Objective 10: Place an arctic grayling at Fangtusk's feeding grounds
I've placed an arctic grayling at Fangtusk's feeding grounds, which seems to have lured it out. I can now slay it in order to rid the area of its hostility. Objective 40: Kill Fangtusk

I have slain Fangtusk. During the battle, I discovered that the rumors about its ability to drain the life of those around it are true. I should inspect it to learn what, if anything, has granted it this unnatural ability. Objective 50: Inspect Fangtusk

After slaying Fangtusk, I discovered the remains of a vampire inside its gut, along with an enchanted vampiric ring. I should show the Jarl's steward the ring as proof that the deed is done. Objective 80: Speak to <Alias=Steward> in Windhelm
I showed the vampiric ring taken from Fangtusk to Jarl of Windhelm's steward, who rewarded me for fulfilling the bounty.

notes: The bounty on Fangtusk may not be marked as a quest item, even though you need to read it to advance the quest.
The Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch, version 4.3.4, fixes this bug.

quick: Ask for permission to use the alchemy lab.
Combine the ingredients at an alchemy lab to create a potion.

walkthrough.heading: The Recipe
paragraphs: Ask any of the quest givers if you can use the alchemy lab located in their shop or inn, as the case may be. They will all consent with the same reply, "Long as you clean up. You know how to use it right? Mix a couple of ingredients together, see what happens. A little Wheat and Blisterwort makes a healing potion, if you didn't know. We have plenty of ingredients for sale, too." This is just a suggestion, crafting any potion will complete the quest objective, you can buy ingredients directly from the quest giver.

walkthrough.heading: Crafting the Potion
paragraphs: Once your ingredients are collected, approach the alchemy lab and select at least two of them. Note that to succeed in crafting a potion, there must be at least one alchemical effect shared by at least two of the ingredients. Confirm the crafting and create a potion to complete the quest. After this, the effect will be added to the Alchemy menu if you don't have it already.

stages.text: Objective 10: Craft a potion

quick: Forge an iron dagger at the forge.
Temper the iron dagger at the grindstone.
Craft leather at the tanning rack.
Craft a hide helmet at the forge.
Temper the hide helmet at the workbench.

walkthrough.heading: Craft a Dagger
paragraphs: Take the iron ingot and the leather strips from the quest giver and then use the forge to create an iron dagger. As soon as the dagger is crafted, return it to the quest giver. Now they will ask you to sharpen the dagger with another iron ingot. Go to the grindstone and sharpen the iron dagger, and present it to the smith.

walkthrough.heading: Craft a Helmet
paragraphs: Secondly, they will ask you to craft some leather. Go to the tanning rack and craft leather, and again speak to the quest giver. Now you have to create a hide helmet at the forge. Take the supplies you are given and use the forge to create the helmet, and then return to the smith.
